papers.title: VisCurate: Evaluating Behavioral Equivalence of Visual Skills
papers.summary: Modern vision-based agents have shifted toward skill-based problem-solving, where a skill is an executable image-to-image operation, e.g., cropping, thresholding, or edge detection. As these skill libraries grow, they accumulate duplicated, mislabeled, and defective skills. The signals normally used to curate them (a skill's name, description, or source code) say little about how the skill visually changes the image. We present VisCurate, a framework and benchmark that curates visual skill libraries from observed execution rather than from text. VisCurate runs each candidate skill pair on a shared probe battery and assigns one of six behavioral relations, each tied to a library edit that is safe to make. The benchmark injects seven defect types into a clean library at controlled rates, producing 300 reproducible instances with ground-truth relations and repairs. While text baselines accept up to five of six false merges on hard negatives, our verifier accepts none and recovers 51.2% of the pairs that are truly mergeable. On two real, uncurated libraries, VisCurate finds that 92% of the skills a package shares with its downstream copy are redundant, while execution confirms only 10 of 17 published equivalence claims. The curation problem also remains open, as the strongest of the nine automated curators recovers only about half of the repairs. We emphasize that visual skill libraries should be curated by behavior, not by description.

papers.title: K-CLUE: A Segmentation-to-Clustering Framework for Ki67 Cell Typing
papers.summary: Ki67 is a key marker of tumor proliferation in breast cancer, but its quantification from immunohistochemistry images normally depends on supervised classifiers trained per dataset. We examine the role of frozen pretrained visual representations in annotation-free Ki67 cell typing. To this end, we use K-CLUE, a framework that segments individual nuclei, represents each nucleus with a pretrained encoder, reduces the resulting embeddings with principal component analysis, and separates Ki67-positive from Ki67-negative nuclei using k-means clustering, without task-specific training or manual annotations. Clustering the raw components is highly sensitive to the choice of encoder: across seven encoders, the Ki67-positive F1-score on matched MIST nuclei varies by 44 points, although Ki67 status remains linearly decodable from every representation, with supervised probe AUCs above 0.98. Analysis of the embedding spaces shows that clustering succeeds when DAB-related variation occupies the leading directions of variance. Whitening the retained principal components removes this dependence, reducing the spread across encoders to 1.00 F1-score point. Handcrafted color representations are also competitive, confirming that Ki67 status is strongly reflected in chromatic information, but they require an explicit choice of color space. In end-to-end evaluation, K-CLUE reaches F1-scores of 85.00% and 81.91% for Ki67-positive and Ki67-negative nuclei on MIST, and 79.59% and 81.16% on BCData, outperforming DeepLIIF and IHCScoreGAN on both datasets. These results show that pretrained representations can support annotation-free Ki67 typing when their variance structure is accounted for.

papers.title: Semantic-First: Temporal Scheduling in Flow Matching for Reliable Emotional Image Generation
papers.summary: Affect-controlled image generation should change how a scene feels while preserving what the prompt specifies. We study the temporal allocation of stochastic exploration and policy optimization in flow-matching models as a means of controlling this balance. During RL training, our semantic-first schedule uses deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE) sampling during the high-noise phase and confines stochastic differential equation (SDE) exploration and group relative policy optimization (GRPO) to a late window. Controlled experiments separate exploration location, optimization location, and terminal-step sampling, showing distinct semantic benefits from late exploration and late updates. On FLUX.1-dev, semantic-first improves prompt faithfulness, independently evaluated affect accuracy, and human-rated semantic preservation and overall preference. The expanded semantic audit records 2.7% subject drift, while GRPO training time decreases by 41.1% relative to original full-path Flow-GRPO. Window-width experiments characterize the affect-semantic and computational trade-offs, and replication on SD3.5-Medium reproduces the scheduling advantage. These results establish denoising time as a practical control dimension for reliable emotional image generation.

papers.title: Can One Hear Geometry? Gauge-Invariant Spectral Descriptors for Text-to-B-rep Retrieval
papers.summary: Text-to-3D solid retrieval faces a fundamental representation gap: while natural language describes intrinsic shapes, Boundary Representation (B-rep) entangles precise geometry with arbitrary variations in pose, scale, and boundary encoding conventions. Existing methods either discretize B-reps at the cost of analytic precision, or learn features from topological graphs without explicit invariance guarantees. We propose a text-to-B-rep retrieval framework based on geometric equivalence classes and spectral invariants, mathematically eliminating representation ambiguities prior to cross-modal alignment. Formalizing translation, rotation, reflection, uniform scaling, and contour re-indexing via group actions, we exploit the planar-profile-and-extrusion structure of engineering solids to construct a unified spectral descriptor across cross-sectional regions, contour boundaries, and extrusion depths. On public benchmarks, our method achieves state-of-the-art recall performance across all evaluation metrics.

papers.title: UltraFlash: Accelerating Megapixel Visual Synthesis
papers.summary: Megapixel visual synthesis with latent diffusion models requires operating far beyond the resolutions at which these models are typically trained. Cascade refinement is a leading strategy for this setting: it starts from a base image at a native resolution and progressively upsamples it to the target resolution through multiple refinement stages. Each stage typically performs a pixel-space resolution transition followed by latent-space denoising. While prior acceleration efforts mainly focus on reducing denoising cost, we identify a complementary and underexplored bottleneck: the repeated movement of representations through the VAE. We call these operations pixel-space transitions. In cascade pipelines, intermediate latents are often decoded to RGB, resized, and re-encoded before refinement, while final latents are decoded patch by patch with dense overlap to suppress boundary artifacts. We propose UltraFlash, a transition-efficient approach that accelerates these VAE-heavy operations. UltraFlash has two components. Latent Hyperloop replaces intermediate RGB round trips with a learned latent-space shortcut that approximates the decode-resize-encode transformation without repeated VAE decoding and encoding. Sparse Patch-based Decoding accelerates final reconstruction by addressing patch seams caused by inconsistent GroupNorm statistics and reusing cached statistics across patches, enabling sparse VAE decoding with much smaller overlap. Integrated into a state-of-the-art cascade baseline, UltraFlash reduces 4K generation latency by approximately 2x while improving image quality. These results show that optimizing pixel-space transitions can improve both efficiency and fidelity, offering an effective route toward fast, high-quality megapixel visual synthesis.

papers.title: WMEval: Evaluating Interactive World Models Grounded on Physical Simulations
papers.summary: Interactive world models hold immense potential for high-stakes applications in robotics, game engines, and immersive digital twins, yet existing benchmarks primarily focus on perceptual similarity rather than the physical-causal coherence essential for real-world utility. We introduce WMEval, a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates interactive world models against Unity-based physical simulations. By leveraging Unity as a high-fidelity ground-truth oracle, we shift evaluation beyond perceptual visual assessment toward the objective state-based verification required for downstream applications. Spanning 9 diverse scenes, WMEval assesses action controllability, scene and character consistency, prompt adherence, kinematics, fluid mechanics, physical causality, and lighting. By executing matched action sequences in both the simulator and the world model, WMEval enables evaluation at both the perceptual level and the physical-causal level, using simulator-derived states as reference. Experiments on state-of-the-art models reveal significant room for improvement in dimensions that remain hidden by standard perceptual metrics but are vital for real-world deployments. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/WMEval.

papers.title: CropReward: A Human-Preference Benchmark and Reward Model for Aesthetic Image Cropping
papers.summary: Aesthetic image cropping (AIC) aims to improve image composition and aesthetic quality by removing extraneous or distracting content. Over the past decade, AIC methods have evolved from specialized vision models to multimodal large language models(MLLMs). Reliable evaluation that reflects human preferences is essential for benchmarking AIC methods and guiding model optimization. However, the current AIC evaluation relies largely on geometry-based metrics such as intersection over union (IoU), as well as image aesthetic assessment(IAA) models. Although inconsistencies with human preferences have long been observed, the robustness and reliability of these evaluation criteria remain underexplored. To bridge this gap, we first construct CropBench, a large-scale benchmark comprising 106,995 human preference pairs for 1,019 images, with each candidate set containing the original image and candidate crops produced by 14 AIC methods. A systematic study on CropBench reveals that the existing criteria, ranging from IoU to off-the-shelf IAA assessment models, only exhibit limited alignment with human preferences. Building upon CropBench, we further propose CropReward, an MLLM-based reward model that evaluates a candidate crop by comparing with the original uncropped image and outputs a score indicating explicit aesthetic improvement or degradation relative to the original. In addition, we employ CropReward to construct CropReward-300k, the largest AIC dataset to date, and further develop CropAlign, a preference-aligned AIC model trained solely with CropReward supervision, without human-annotated crop boxes. Experimental results demonstrate that CropReward aligns with human preferences significantly better than AIC existing criteria. CropAlign also surpasses the state-of-the-art AIC methods, demonstrating the advantage of CropReward in guiding AIC model optimization.

papers.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.summary: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking
papers.summary: Existing multi-agent collaboration (MAC) methods have primarily explored a group thinking collaboration topology, where agents independently generate solutions and aggregate their outputs. In this work, we investigate an alternative relay thinking topology, where reasoning ownership is dynamically transferred across agents, allowing subsequent agents to inherit and refine an evolving reasoning trajectory. We introduce Multi-Agent Confidence-guided Relay (MACR), a framework that enables dynamical relay collaboration among agents. The key challenge is determining when reasoning should be relayed and which agent should continue the process. method addresses this challenge through confidence-guided relay triggering and a bidding mechanism that selects the next agent based on its confidence. Experiments on four benchmarks show that method outperforms the strongest single-model strategies in accuracy, e.g., +3.3% on MathVista and +3.9% on MMStar, and remains on par with multi-agent strategies while consuming 6.0x less token overhead on HallusionBench and MMStar. Further analysis demonstrates that relay collaboration enables heterogeneous agents to progressively integrate complementary insights, combining heterogeneous capabilities across reasoning stages. Our source code is available at https://github.com/67L1/MACR.

papers.title: Metric Scale for Insta360 Structure-from-Motion from the Camera's Embedded IMU
papers.summary: Structure-from-motion (SfM) from the dual-fisheye video of a consumer 360-degree camera recovers geometry only up to a similarity transform; in the pipeline considered here, metric scale is obtained from smartphone ARKit or ARCore poses captured alongside the camera. This paper evaluates a self-contained alternative: the IMU embedded in the Insta360 X5 and X6, recorded at 1 kHz. The sensor is characterised (noise density, camera-IMU synchronisation, accelerometer scale factor, bias stability), the camera-IMU rotation and frame timing are estimated from the data, and the scale is recovered by a linear visual-inertial alignment over the SfM poses of a whole survey. The standard formulation, with gravity and accelerometer bias shared across the survey, overestimates the scale by 3.4% on average; estimating each contiguous segment independently and averaging removes the bias. On nine surveys with a co-mounted LiDAR scanner the inertial scale deviates from the LiDAR by 0.81% in mean absolute error, against 1.94% for the smartphone scale; on printed fiducial markers both agree within the 1% uncertainty of the target. On the reference trajectories of thirty sequences of a public benchmark, brought to scales of 1/40, 1 and 40, the estimator recovers the metric scale with a mean error of -0.07% and a standard deviation of 1.28%. On fifty production surveys where the smartphone is the only reference, the two scales agree to a standard deviation of 2.3%, the inertial scale being 0.3% lower on average; the difference is uncorrelated with run length, grows with the extent of the smartphone anchor, and cannot be attributed to either reference. An ablation over window construction and a comparison with monocular metric-depth networks complete the study.

papers.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
papers.summary: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. We introduce VibeVideoBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on code-driven video generation. Its 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese span 12 categories, from data stories and music-driven pieces to classroom lessons and paper explainers; each asks an agent, running in its native harness inside a sandbox with no image or video generation model, to deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour. Evaluation is hierarchical and evidence-based: program checks of the delivery spec, about 13k task-specific rubric checks traced to the requirements they enforce, and five quality dimensions anchored per task, scored by three VLM judge panels. Across nine frontier agent systems and 2,151 scored rollouts, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 rank first and second with both the judges and human annotators, and the strongest system satisfies every core requirement on 76.3% of tasks. Delivery is a second axis: counting missing videos as zero changes the ranking, and three quarters of the lost videos are final renders that started too late, ran too slowly or never started, a failure of how agents plan their hour. Agents build their own rendering pipelines and inspect their own frames, yet how much they look does not predict quality. The judges' ranking of the systems closely matches blind human preferences.

papers.title: Latent Representation Learning from 3D Brain MRI for Latent Analysis and Prediction in Multiple Sclerosis
papers.summary: Neurological diseases can cause significant cognitive impairment, yet linking brain structure to cognitive function remains challenging due to the limitations of conventional methods and the black-box nature of deep learning. We propose InfoVAE-Med3D, an adaptation of InfoVAE for three-dimensional brain MRI that learns informative latent representations by relaxing the mutual information regularization penalty between inputs and latent representations. We evaluated the method on a healthy control (HC) dataset (\(n=6{,}503\)) with age and sex information and a multiple sclerosis (MS) dataset (\(n=916\)) with age, sex, and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) scores. Two-dimensional visualizations revealed sex-related clustering and smooth transitions in grey and white matter volumes. Removing the mutual information regularization penalty generally improved MRI reconstruction and brain age and SDMT prediction using support vector regression, outperforming other variational autoencoder variants and achieving competitive performance with deep learning predictors, particularly on the MS dataset. InfoVAE-Med3D provides informative latent representations for investigating brain-related characteristics and supports latent-space analysis and imaging biomarker discovery for cognitive impairment, particularly in MS.

papers.title: Learning to Feel the Future: DreamTacVLA for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown remarkable generalization by mapping web-scale knowledge to robotic control, yet they remain blind to physical contact. Consequently, they struggle with contact-rich manipulation tasks that require reasoning about force, texture, and slip. While some approaches incorporate low-dimensional tactile signals, they fail to capture the high-resolution dynamics essential for such interactions. To address this limitation, we introduce DreamTacVLA, a framework that grounds VLA models in contact physics by learning to feel the future. Our model adopts a hierarchical perception scheme in which high-resolution tactile images serve as micro-vision inputs coupled with wrist-camera local vision and third-person macro vision. To reconcile these multi-scale sensory streams, we first train a unified policy with a Hierarchical Spatial Alignment (HSA) loss that aligns tactile tokens with their spatial counterparts in the wrist and third-person views. To further deepen the model's understanding of fine-grained contact dynamics, we finetune the system with a tactile world model that predicts future tactile signals. To mitigate tactile data scarcity and the wear-prone nature of tactile sensors, we construct a hybrid large-scale dataset sourced from both high-fidelity digital twin and real-world experiments. By anticipating upcoming tactile states, DreamTacVLA acquires a rich model of contact physics and conditions its actions on both real observations and imagined consequences. Across contact-rich manipulation tasks, it outperforms state-of-the-art VLA baselines, achieving up to 95% success, highlighting the importance of understanding physical contact for robust, touch-aware robotic agents.

papers.title: DeFM: Learning Foundation Representations from Depth for Robotics
papers.summary: Depth sensors are widely deployed across robotic platforms, and advances in fast, high-fidelity depth simulation have enabled robotic policies trained on depth observations to achieve robust sim-to-real transfer for a wide range of tasks. Despite this, representation learning for depth modality remains underexplored compared to RGB, where large-scale foundation models now define the state of the art. To address this gap, we present DeFM, a self-supervised foundation model trained entirely on depth images for robotic applications. Using a DINO-style self-distillation objective on a curated dataset of 60M depth images, DeFM learns geometric and semantic representations that generalize to diverse environments, tasks, and sensors. To retain metric awareness across multiple scales, we introduce a novel input normalization strategy. We further distill DeFM into compact models suitable for resource-constrained robotic systems. When evaluated on depth-based classification, segmentation, navigation, locomotion, and manipulation benchmarks, DeFM achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates strong generalization from simulation to real-world environments. We release all our pretrained models, which can be adopted off-the-shelf for depth-based robotic learning without task-specific fine-tuning. Webpage: https://de-fm.github.io/

papers.title: Multimodal Knowledge Aggregation for Microbial Keratitis: Geographic Confounding and Shortcut Risk in Pooled Multicountry Data
papers.summary: To develop an open-source multimodal model for bacterial-versus-fungal microbial keratitis classification and assess shortcuts from geographic pooling. Participants: 1,645 US and Indian patients contributed 17,158 slit-lamp images under blue-light, sclerotic-scatter, and white-light illumination. Methods: The model combined cross-modality contrastive learning, modality-specific fine-tuning, and fusion with 7 clinical variables. Diagnoses used smear, culture, and polymerase chain reaction results, with expert review of culture-negative cases. The model and 5 comparators used 5 patient-disjoint outer folds stratified by country and organism, with inner validation. Secondary analyses examined within-country performance, a country-only reference, ablations, and imbalance mitigation. Code: https://github.com/yqwang01/TPMKA. Main Outcome Measures: Patient-level macro-F1, class-specific F1, accuracy, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), overall and by country. Results: The model had the highest overall macro-F1 (83.06%; 95% CI, 81.58-84.56) and accuracy (84.50%; 95% CI, 83.16-85.84) among matched comparators, with 89.9% AUROC (95% CI, 88.7-91.1). Paired differences were not consistently significant. AUROC was 83.9% in India and 67.0% in the US; bacterial F1 in India was 47.78%, and fungal F1 in the US was 40.97%. A country-only reference achieved 81.88% accuracy and 78.2% AUROC overall despite 50.0% AUROC within each country. Resampling and group distributionally robust optimization improved some underrepresented groups without removing the geographic pattern. Conclusions: The model compared favorably with matched methods, but geographic prevalence differences made pooled performance more reassuring than within-country discrimination. Independent geographic validation is needed.

papers.title: Spacetime Sentinels: a Qiskit game that exposes the competition between spacetime checks and magic in low-overhead quantum error detection
papers.summary: We present Spacetime Sentinels, a game in which the player protects a noisy circuit with spacetime Pauli checks and is scored on the post-selected fidelity and the fraction of shots that survive, with every number computed in Qiskit. The player spends a budget of ancilla qubits on checks found by the qiskit-paulice add-on, must inject a quota of $T$ gates into the protected circuit, and chooses whether to place them where they commute with every check or to ignore the checks. Each move is evaluated exactly with Qiskit Aer density-matrix simulation against a stabilizer or statevector reference, and the evaluation agrees with 50,000-shot runs of the SamplerV2 primitive. We score moves with a fidelity rate $R=F_{\mathrm{ps}}\kappa^{1/2}$, whose inverse square is the sampling overhead of detection followed by rescaling. Exhaustive evaluation of all 5,412 legal moves under two noise models, together with sweeps over five random payloads, reveals three trade-offs that are not obvious before playing. Checks pay for themselves only above a break-even depth: at depth 6 adding checks lowers $R$, while at depth 18 the best number of checks raises it by a factor of 1.103 and lifts the fidelity from 0.629 to 0.886. $T$ gates add no noise on hardware, yet each check removes spacetime locations where a $T$ gate can be placed safely, from all 90 at depth 18 with no checks to about 14 with four, so the optimal number of checks falls as the magic quota grows. Finally, a check broken by a $T$ gate is worse than no check: with sixteen $T$ gates at depth 18, blind placement lowers the post-selected fidelity to 0.158, and retiring the broken checks lowers it further to 0.102, below the 0.628 of the unprotected circuit. The game runs in the browser and in the terminal, and all code and data are open source.

papers.title: Accelerating fits in high-energy physics and beyond
papers.summary: Data analysis in particle physics often involves optimizing a loss function that quantifies how well a theoretical model describes the observed data, in order to estimate the parameters of the model. This is referred to as fitting. As datasets grow larger and more expensive analysis methods are used, the time required to perform this parameter estimation can be a limiting factor. This work explores techniques that can significantly accelerate the fitting process, and measures their performance on a set of example models chosen to be representative of a variety of physics fits. We compare the speed and precision of variants of several well-known optimization algorithms, namely Newton's method, BFGS, and the Migrad algorithm (commonly used in physics fits). We observe significant speedups when using some algorithms: most notably, some variants of BFGS are consistently about $10\times$ faster than Migrad across our benchmarks, while achieving the same precision. For quasi-Newtonian algorithms like BFGS and Migrad, we find that the initial value of the Hessian matrix has a large impact on the runtime. We additionally discuss methods for accelerating the evaluation of the loss function and its derivatives, using algebraic simplifications, automatic differentiation, and modern hardware features on the CPU and GPU. We find that basic algebraic simplifications of the loss function can significantly improve speed and precision. On the GPU we explore using mixed precision computation, and show that this achieves much higher throughput on most accelerators without significant precision loss. Lastly we discuss efficient parallelization strategies for both the CPU and the GPU. All of the techniques and algorithms in this paper are implemented in our new FastFit library, which was used for all of our benchmarks.

papers.title: What We Could Lose by Trying to Make Mars Habitable
papers.summary: The recent push to develop Mars terraforming technologies, increasingly driven by unaccountable private wealth, risks the irreversible destruction of planetary records we have barely begun to read. In this sense, terraforming Mars would be akin to the destruction of the Library of Alexandria. Echoing Carl Sagan's words about the library, in this piece we argue that we should not let such an extensive loss of information happen again. As terraforming Mars would melt and destroy the icy record on Mars, we suggest closing an important gap in the COSPAR planetary protection framework, by expanding regulations on preventing biological contamination to preventing large-scale atmospheric modification and destruction of cryospheric and geologic records.

papers.title: New constraints on holographic dark energy with high-redshift galaxy observations from JWST
papers.summary: Observations of high-redshift galaxies from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide a complementary probe of early structure formation. Meanwhile, DESI results have provided further indications of possible dynamical dark energy, prompting investigations of theoretically motivated dark energy models. In this work, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) and interacting holographic dark energy (IHDE) using JWST ultraviolet luminosity function measurements, cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations from Planck and ACT, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, and DES-Dovekie type~Ia supernova data. We find that JWST has little impact on the parameter constraints of $\Lambda$CDM and HDE but produces more pronounced changes in those of IHDE. For CMB+DESI+DES-Dovekie, adding JWST shifts the holographic parameter $c$ from $1.270^{+0.146}_{-0.096}$ to $1.091\pm0.095$ and the interaction parameter $\beta$ from $0.650^{+0.104}_{-0.034}$ to $0.498^{+0.090}_{-0.061}$, accompanied by an increase in $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and a decrease in $S_8$. For the full data combination, $\chi^2_{\rm JWST}$ decreases by approximately $7$ for both HDE and IHDE compared with $\Lambda$CDM, indicating improved fits to the high-redshift galaxy abundances. Our results highlight the complementary role of high-redshift galaxy observations in probing the HDE and IHDE models.

papers.title: Walk on Multiscale Media: Compiling Editable and Composable Transport Medium Prefabs for Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
papers.summary: Monte Carlo PDE solvers enable mesh-free pointwise queries, but repeatedly traversing heterogeneous media is costly, particularly in scenes with reusable or dynamically changing materials. We introduce Walk on Multiscale Media (WoMM), which compiles fine-scale transport into reusable, editable and composable transport prefabs. A probabilistic interpretation of multiscale finite-element bases and condensed operators yields coarse transitions retaining fine-scale material effects. Each prefab combines port-level operators, entrance-dependent exit distributions, and Poisson-marked trajectory records, enabling incremental updates for overlapping absorption fields, gradient-field steering through path reweighting and transient diffusion. Integrated with conventional Walk-on-Spheres in a hybrid continuous--discrete solver, these prefabs accelerate repeated pointwise PDE queries and support interactive material edits without repeatedly solving the fine-scale problem.

papers.title: Dynamical systems analysis of Bianchi type-IX cosmology with a scalar field mediated dark sector interaction
papers.summary: The recent DESI DR2 results preference for a time-varying dark-energy equation of state, together with the long-standing difficulty of explaining why an initially anisotropic universe should evolve toward isotropy, motivates the study of interacting dark-sector models in anisotropic backgrounds. We investigate the dynamics of Bianchi type-IX cosmologies containing pressureless dark matter coupled to dark energy in the form of a quintessence scalar field $\phi$ with exponential potential $V(\phi)=V_0\,e^{-\lambda\phi}$. Energy exchange between the two dark components is mediated by the scalar field through the interaction term $Q=\kappa\beta\dot\phi\,\rho_{\rm DM}$, where $\kappa^2=8\pi G$ and $\beta$ is a dimensionless coupling. Because Bianchi~IX models generically recollapse, the Hubble scalar $H$ vanishes at the moment of maximum expansion, where the expansion-normalized variables of the standard Wainwright--Ellis formalism diverge. We therefore adopt the $D$-normalized phase-space formalism of Hewitt, Uggla, and Wainwright, which compactifies the state space and remains regular through the recollapse, including the moment of maximum expansion at which $H = 0$. Together with the modified conservation equations for the two dark components, the Einstein equation reduces to a closed autonomous polynomial dynamical system, whose fixed points we classify by linear stability analysis, supplemented by center-manifold theory for the non-hyperbolic points. The fixed points shows the kinetic-dominated, coupling modified matter dominated, curvature scalar, scalar field dominated and coupled scaling families; the last is the anisotropic analogue of the Amendola scaling attractor. Restricting to the initially expanding, isotropizing trajectories, we map the region of the $(\lambda,\beta)$ plane in which anisotropic Bianchi~IX models approach an accelerating Friedmann--Robertson--Walker state.

papers.title: Structure of Logarithmically-Corrected Starobinsky Fuzzy Dark Matter Black Holes
papers.summary: This work constructs an anisotropic, Einasto-profile fuzzy dark matter (DM) black hole (BH) using a logarithmically-corrected Starobinsky gravity, $f(R)=R+\beta R^2+\gamma R^2\ln(R/\mu^2)$, a form motivated by one-loop quantum corrections to the gravitational action rather than by the pure quadratic term alone. We derive the generalized trace equation for this action, show that its $\beta$- and $\gamma$-dependence collapses to a single compact source term, and solve the resulting field equations perturbatively about an exact general-relativistic (GR) background for two distinct anisotropic equations of state: a de~Sitter-type branch and a non-local branch, the latter worked through to a closed tangential-pressure profile rather than left incomplete. The logarithmic correction is found to raise the extremal (zero-temperature) threshold relative to pure quadratic gravity and to increase the core tangential pressure noticeably in the non-local branch.

papers.title: Theoretical study of high-order harmonic generation in solids based on deep-learning methods
papers.summary: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. The former is caused by the modification of the inter-site hopping in the system, while the latter is mainly influenced by the structural disorder induced by the thermal effects, in agreement with experimental observations. This work establishes a scalable computational strategy for investigating HHG in solids and provides new insights into the interplay between lattice fluctuations and ultrafast electron dynamics.

papers.title: Testing Schouten--Codazzi Gravity: Cosmological Constraints and Deviations from $\Lambda$CDM
papers.summary: Schouten--Codazzi gravity (SCG) admits a cosmological background that extends flat $\Lambda$CDM by one integration constant, $\gamma_0$. Its contribution to the Friedmann equation scales as $(1+z)$ and corresponds to an effective component with equation of state $w_{\gamma_0}=-2/3$. We constrain this extension using 15 combinations of Type~Ia supernovae, DESI~DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and compressed cosmic microwave background information, supplemented by a big-bang nucleosynthesis prior as specified in the analysis. Supernovae paired with either BAO or CMB favor positive $\Omega_{\gamma_0}\equiv\gamma_0/H_0^2$, with approximate marginal departures from zero of $1.7$--$3.2\sigma$. In contrast, all three supernovae$+$BAO$+$CMB combinations are consistent with $\Omega_{\gamma_0}=0$ within their 68\% credible intervals. Their central log Bayes factors favor $\Lambda$CDM, with $\Delta\ln\mathcal{Z}$ between $-2.54$ and $-1.13$, and the inferred Hubble constants remain close to those of the corresponding $\Lambda$CDM fits. These results provide a background-level test of SCG conditional on the adopted priors and likelihood approximations, particularly the model assumptions entering the CMB compression.

papers.title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
papers.summary: This paper focuses on the numerical and analytical determination of the mechanical parameters of aluminum-matrix nanocomposites using atomistic-scale simulations within a multiscale modeling framework. Molecular statics simulations were employed to evaluate the tensile and compressive behavior of Al based composites reinforced with nanosized alumina particles. Two classes of atomistic models were investigated. First, a unit-cell model containing a single Al2O3 monocrystal embedded in an aluminum matrix was used to examine the influence of the volume fraction of the ceramic inclusion on the effective mechanical properties. Second, a polycrystalline RVE model comprising an alumina particle was analyzed to assess the effect of the number of Al grains on effective properties. For each case, the mechanical response was characterized by stress-strain curves, enabling the identification of upper-scale material parameters associated with the elastic regime (bulk, shear and Young's modulus) and the damage stage (ultimate strength, ultimate strain, and failure strain). The isotropized elastic constants evaluated from molecular simulations were compared with classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill bounds to assess their applicability in the elastic regime. Finally, atomistic-scale simulation outputs provided insight into the dominant deformation/damage mechanisms (brittle versus ductile) and fracture modes (transgranular versus intergranular).

papers.title: Derivation of OH sum rules without Rayleigh--Jeans approximation: a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants
papers.summary: In this paper, we show that the optical depths of any OH $\Lambda$-doublet quartet obey one exact linear relation in every velocity channel. No approximation is needed. The only exception is the $^{2}\Pi_{1/2}$ $J{=}1/2$ level, which has three transitions only, because its $F{=}0{\leftrightarrow}0$ line is strictly forbidden. The relation is $\tau_{S_1}(v)/\mu_{S_1}^{2}+\tau_{S_2}(v)/\mu_{S_2}^{2}=\tau_{M_1}(v)/(a\mu_{M_1}^{2})+\tau_{M_2}(v)/(b\mu_{M_2}^{2})$, where $a=2J^{2}+J-1$, $b=2J^{2}+3J$, and the $\mu_i^{2}$ are reduced transition dipole moments derived from the catalogued Einstein $A$ coefficients. It holds equally for gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), for non-LTE gas, for masers and for conjugate gas. We suggest that it is a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants.

papers.title: Parameter-Decoupled Superresolution with Airy-Disk-Informed Learning: Application to NGC 4486B
papers.summary: Estimating the separation of two unresolved or nearly unresolved sources from recorded intensity images is difficult when source brightness, mutual coherence, and phase are unknown and the point-spread function (PSF) departs from a Gaussian. We formulate Hermite--Gaussian (HG) projections of one- and two-dimensional Airy amplitudes and prove that ratios of mode probabilities with equal longitudinal parity exactly cancel the brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters under a symmetric two-source model. For a one-dimensional Airy slice we achieve an explicit multi-ratio separation inversion. For the physical two-dimensional circular-pupil PSF we obtain exact finite-pupil overlap integrals and locally invertible separation responses. Motivated by these analytical invariants, we examine Airy-informed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on synthetic Airy images with known separations. At 150,000 training images, the approximate mean absolute errors are 0.018 in plotted separation units, 10 times better comparing to 0.18 for non-Airy Gaussian PSF approximation. Applied to an archival Hubble Space Telescope image of the double nucleus of NGC 4486B, the Airy-informed CNN gives estimates of approximately 9.6--12.0 pc for training sets of 100,000--150,000 images, broadly consistent with the historical approximately 12 pc value. We distinguish exact optical-mode nuisance cancellation from empirical robustness of an image-only learned estimator and identify the limits imposed by PSF mismatch and extended galaxy structure.

papers.title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
papers.summary: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the $\ell$-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.

papers.title: Efficient regime boundary detection in discontinuous simulation models
papers.summary: Many computational models exhibit multiple operating regimes separated by abrupt or non-smooth transitions as the input parameters vary. Such regime transitions complicate the construction of global parametric reduced-order models, often necessitating large training datasets to capture the distinct system behaviors. Accurate regime boundary detection instead enables localized modeling strategies by partitioning the parameter space into regions of qualitatively distinct behavior. In many cases, regime switching corresponds to the excursion set of a simulator output. When such a quantity is discontinuous or non-smooth, regression-based algorithms for level set estimation can struggle to correctly approximate the boundary. In this work, we show that solving a resulting binary classification problem can improve sample efficiency and we further propose a novel adaptive sampling strategy for support vector machines. Unlike uncertainty-based sampling schemes, the proposed approach uses a continuous search space and efficiently explores the currently estimated boundary in its tangential directions by gradient-based dynamic sampling. Because the decision function admits analytical gradients, this exploration incurs negligible computational overhead relative to the underlying model evaluations. Then, a space-filling subset of the generated samples is selected as the next batch to be queried. We demonstrate improved sample efficiency compared to existing active learning algorithms on analytical and numerical examples. The proposed method provides a sample-efficient framework for regime boundary detection in a broad class of discontinuous simulation-driven problems.

papers.title: Attenuation of shoaling extreme wave crests by artificial salt marshes
papers.summary: Laboratory experiments in a wave flume investigated the attenuation of shoaling extreme waves by artificial salt marshes placed immediately before an abrupt depth transition. Increasing vegetation density systematically reduced the excess kurtosis of the surface elevation distribution in the intermediate water depth regime. Nonetheless, attenuation exhibits a short saturation regime at low vegetation densities, whereas at very high densities, excess kurtosis decreases significantly across the gauges. However, kurtosis attenuation becomes ineffective as waves approach shallow-water conditions or as second-order nonlinear effects become significant. Furthermore, the highest experimental densities where the kurtosis is tamed exceed typical natural salt marsh stem densities. Thus, in natural settings, salt marshes are likely to provide only partial mitigation of extreme wave statistics in intermediate and shallow water depths, as the wave field retains some hazardous nonlinearity.

papers.title: RPAx Instabilities from Ground- and Excited-State References
papers.summary: Random-phase approximation with exchange (RPAx) calculations based on ground- or excited-state references can yield complex excitation energies, causing the corresponding RPAx correlation energy to become complex as well. In this work, we investigate the origin of these complex energies using \ce{H2} in the 6-31G basis set as a minimal model. For the ground-state restricted Hartree-Fock reference, complex roots emerge at the well-known triplet instability associated with the appearance of a lower-lying unrestricted, symmetry-broken solution. For excited-state references, we identify two distinct mechanisms leading to complex excitation energies. The first is similarly associated with symmetry breaking. The second arises when a positive-energy excitation becomes degenerate with the positive-energy de-excitation associated with a negative-energy transition. Finally, we demonstrate the practical implications of these findings for spin-flip Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations of cyclobutadiene and state-specific core-ionization calculations for selected systems. These examples show that, in the absence of the relevant instabilities, methods sharing the generalized eigenvalue structure of RPAx can be applied to excited-state references without resorting to the Tamm-Dancoff or core-valence separation approximations, while retaining real excitation energies.

papers.title: A generative foundation model for 2D magnetized plasma turbulence
papers.summary: We present a proof-of-principle study demonstrating a conditional generative foundation model for self-organizing magnetized plasma turbulence. Built on a multichannel flow-matching framework with a spectral decomposition strategy, the model is trained on direct numerical simulations of 2D modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (MHW) turbulence across the hydrodynamic to adiabatic parameter range. Without retraining, this \textit{single} model successfully performs three distinct downstream tasks: (i) unconditional generation of statistically faithful quasi-steady-state snapshots that recover the directional energy spectra and amplitude statistics, from which statistical transport quantities, including turbulent flux and effective diffusivity, alongside their uncertainties, are inferred directly; (ii) super-resolution from $4\times$ and $8\times$ downsampled observations to reconstruct fine-scale turbulence and large-scale zonal structures; and (iii) full-field inpainting from sparse spatial observations covering as little as $\sim 10\%$ of the domain. The generated fields faithfully reproduce regime-dependent turbulence vs. zonal-flow states and energy partitioning. Under extreme sparsity the long-correlation zonal flows are pinned by only a handful of observations, while the residual uncertainty concentrates in the small-scale turbulent fluctuations. These results establish flow-matching generative models as powerful, unified surrogates for state generation, statistical inference, and sparse-data reconstruction, providing a scalable baseline for 3D plasma turbulence and experimental applications.

papers.title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications
papers.summary: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. Within this framework, we identify longitudinal and transverse modulation channels, analogous to electro-optic phase modulation and acousto-optic diffraction of light, respectively, and show how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and optical-field geometry. This formulation organizes PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM as limiting regimes of a common modulation picture. The resulting framework provides design principles for free-electron modulators that can control energy spectra, temporal density, transverse wavefronts, and electron-photon quantum interfaces, establishing LEM as a device-level platform for programmable femtosecond-to-attosecond matter-wave control.

papers.title: Towards operational data-driven regional weather forecasting: extreme-event skill and near-real-time verification with HRRRCast
papers.summary: Improving convective-scale skill in data-driven regional weather models requires better representing rare high-impact events, training at native resolution, broadening variable output, and demonstrating performance in real-time settings. Here, we evaluate these challenges using HRRRCast, a data-driven convection-allowing emulator trained on the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) analysis data. HRRRCast combines native 3-km training, moderate sigmoid-weighted loss reweighting for reflectivity and precipitation, and broader system improvements including expansion of the training archive from 3 to 9 years (2016--2025), increased vertical resolution, expanded outputs, and architectural upgrades. The weighted loss improves high-threshold skill while preserving common-event behavior. Native-resolution training avoids aliasing from 6-km subsampling and substantially improves fractions skill score at convective scales, with gains that persist across pooling windows. HRRRCast has also been running in near-real-time mode for the past year. In seven months of independent observation-based verification, HRRRCast ensemble means improve several near-surface metrics relative to operational HRRR and maintain strong precipitation and reflectivity performance. Single-member reflectivity skill is strongest at 20--30 dBZ; at 40 dBZ, skill is near parity at 6-km pooling and better at pooling radii $\geq$30 km. Precipitation skill remains competitive through 1 in/h and extends to about 3 in/h in the best recent configuration. A focused comparison with HREF further shows useful low-cost probabilistic guidance for 3-h precipitation. At storm scale, HRRRCast exhibits a displacement--structure trade-off, with generally better storm placement than storm morphology.

papers.title: QMOMKit: A C++ library for quadrature-based moment methods
papers.summary: QMOMKit is an open-source C++ library for the phase-space evolution of population balance equations with quadrature-based moment methods. The present version implements the quadrature method of moments (QMOM) and the conditional quadrature method of moments (CQMOM). QMOMKit is designed to be independent of any particular application and can be used either as a standalone solver for spatially homogeneous population models or as a local phase-space solver coupled to a host application. It handles the numerical aspects of the evolution of a population in phase space, including quadrature reconstruction, advection of the quadrature abscissas, and changes to the population through moment sources and phase-space boundary contributions. The number of quadrature nodes is adapted to what the supplied moments support, subject to prescribed bounds of the phase-space coordinates, and the CQMOM implementation supports an arbitrary number of phase-space dimensions as well as any conditioning order. The principal numerical algorithms of QMOMKit are verified against analytical and manufactured solutions. Standalone spatially homogeneous applications, ranging from aerosol evaporation to particle dynamics and fragmentation, are compared with Monte Carlo solutions of the same population models, while coupling examples with OpenFOAM and deal.II demonstrate how QMOMKit can be embedded in finite-volume and discontinuous-Galerkin simulation frameworks. Together, these capabilities provide a tested and reusable foundation for a wide range of population-balance problems, and a basis for extending QMOMKit to other quadrature-based moment methods.

papers.title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
papers.summary: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$\beta$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

papers.title: Two-layer conjugate flows in an open channel
papers.summary: We investigate conjugate flows in a two-layer fluid system with a flat bottom and a free surface. These are up- and downstream states consistent with simultaneous conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; and therefore candidate end-states of one-dimensional dissipationless bores. By choosing variables in a specific way, we are able to explicitly parameterize all physical non-trivial conjugate flows in the system, using only rational functions. This two-parameter family can be categorized according to whether the states are compatible with (1) a rising surface, and falling internal interface; or (2) vice versa. In particular, we rule out the existence of monotone bore solutions, consistent with an earlier result due to Chen, Walsh, and Wheeler. However, here we do so already at the level of conjugate flows. Separating these two distinct categories is a one-parameter family of critical trivial conjugate flows. The complete description obtained in the present paper serves as an important stepping stone towards finding actual realizing heteroclinic orbits connecting such conjugate states.

papers.title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
papers.summary: The prediction of transition remains challenging because the receptivity amplitude is usually prescribed rather than measured. This work uses Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) to study an unforced Mach 6 nitrogen boundary layer over a 120 mm flat plate, with no imposed inlet wave, wall signal, modal shape, or disturbance spectrum. The retained unsteady field is the intrinsic finite-particle stochastic fluctuation field carried by the DSMC representation. Changing the DSMC particle count provides an independent numerical control parameter that sets a predictable finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged boundary-layer flow. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) is then applied to unforced DSMC snapshots. The DMD eigenvalues and spatial modes estimate the quantities that appear in the LST normal-mode description, including frequency, temporal growth or decay, wavenumber, wavelength, phase speed, mode location, and amplification envelope. LST is used after extraction to test whether the data-derived structures occupy the expected second-mode band. The results show that DSMC data can connect a measured finite-particle stochastic disturbance level to second-mode instability dynamics without imposed disturbance spectra.

papers.title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
papers.summary: We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfv\'en waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.

papers.title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
papers.summary: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}\Sigma_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.

papers.title: Spatially-Adaptive Neural-Network Based Extraction of Significant Wave Heights from HF Radar Data
papers.summary: Significant wave height (SWH) retrieval from high-frequency (HF) radar data conventionally relies on Doppler-spectrum processing and interpretation of the weak second-order scattering continuum. This article investigates adaptive spatial processing for time-domain SWH estimation using ordered envelope statistics. In our previous study, a physics-guided linear ordered-statistics estimator (LOSE), motivated by first-order rough-surface scattering assumptions and radar-envelope statistics, mapped the largest rank-ordered magnitudes of Bartlett-beamformed voltages to buoy-observed SWH through least-squares regression. The LOSE framework is extended using three trainable complex spatial filters initialized around the buoy look direction. Ordered magnitudes are extracted independently from each spatial output, concatenated, and mapped to SWH through least-squares regression, while the spatial weights are optimized using gradient-based updates. Both estimators use causal sliding-window averaging. Evaluation used measurements from a 13.385-MHz, 12-receiver element WERA radar at Argentia, Canada, paired with directional-wave buoy observations. Under a common chronological training-evaluation partition, the selected adaptive configuration reduced root-mean-square error by approximately $14.3\%$, while maintaining the Pearson correlation coefficient at $0.949$. These results support the potential of adaptive multi-beam processing to improve time-domain SWH estimation relative to fixed Bartlett-based LOSE. Feature counts and smoothing windows were selected using the evaluation interval; independent testing is therefore needed to establish the generality of the improvement.

papers.title: Neutron-Lean D-3He Fusion by Asymmetric Enhancement of the Primary Reaction: A Spin-Polarized Non-Thermal Hot Tail
papers.summary: This paper focuses on a modified fuel that combines the theory of spin-polarized fuel with non-thermal "hot-tail" reactions for D-T, D-3He, and D-D reactions. We find that this combination is particularly advantageous for the D-3He fuel in several respects. First, a large reactivity enhancement: one order of magnitude at 10 keV for a small hot tail (F = 0.1), rising to two orders of magnitude for a larger one (F = 0.6), with polarization adding a further factor of 1.5. Second, an ideal ignition energy far below the thermal value: 9.5 keV at F = 0.3 down to 3.2 keV at F = 0.5, which polarization reduces further to 3.8 keV and 1.3 keV, respectively. Third, the asymmetric enhancement between the primary reaction and the secondary reactions in the fuel opens the possibility of a neutron-lean reaction. Quantifying this with a neutrons-per-watt metric, we find that a thermal D-3He plasma at 10 keV is barely neutron-lean at all (90-95% of the D-T neutron rate per watt), whereas a hot tail of F = 0.1 reduces it by 4.7-7.7x and the polarized non-thermal fuel at its ignition point reaches 3.0-5.4% of the D-T value, with only 0.4-2.4% of the fusion power carried by neutrons. The range spans prompt removal versus complete in-situ burnup of the bred tritium. Applied to a 200 MW worked example anchored on the ARTEMIS D-3He reactor design, this is a first-wall neutron loading of 0.008-0.043 MW/m^2 against 1.45 MW/m^2 for D-T in the same chamber, extending the time to reach 20 dpa from about 1.5 full-power years to 27.

papers.title: Image-Domain CT Metal Artifact Reduction Using an Endpoint-Conditioned Diffusion Bridge
papers.summary: Background: Metal implants cause streaking and shading artifacts in computed tomography (CT), obscuring anatomy and distorting Hounsfield-unit (HU) values. Conventional diffusion models reconstruct images from Gaussian noise rather than directly exploiting anatomical information retained in artifact-corrupted CT. Purpose: To develop an image-domain metal artifact reduction (MAR) method connecting artifact-corrupted and metal-free CT images through an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge. Methods: The proposed RDBM-MAR method uses an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge and initializes reconstruction from the artifact CT image. A conditional U-Net predicts an image-domain correction from intermediate bridge states. Inference uses 10 deterministic reverse steps. We used 14,000 paired CT slices from the AAPM CT-MAR Grand Challenge, including 12,045 training, 633 validation, and 1,322 held-out test slices. One clinical benchmark case was assessed qualitatively. We compared RDBM-MAR with CycleGAN, Pix2Pix, Res-SRDiff, I2I-Mamba, and I2SB using PSNR, SSIM, MAE, and LPIPS. Statistical analysis used Friedman and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction. Results: RDBM-MAR achieved the highest PSNR (43.67 +/- 4.56 dB) and SSIM (0.9856 +/- 0.0138) and the lowest MAE (14.74 +/- 8.68 HU). All four metrics differed significantly among methods (p < 0.001). RDBM-MAR outperformed all five comparators in PSNR, SSIM, and MAE (adjusted p < 0.001); Res-SRDiff achieved the lowest LPIPS. Difference maps, HU profiles, and the clinical case showed reduced artifacts with preservation of surrounding anatomy. Conclusions: RDBM-MAR provides a direct restoration trajectory from artifact CT toward metal-free CT, achieving strong structural fidelity and HU accuracy using 10 reverse steps.

papers.title: Activity-based temporal hypergraphs: from individual activity to collective social dynamics
papers.summary: Temporal hypergraphs provide an interesting representation for many social systems, as they integrate both the temporal and group nature of social interactions. Designing models of time-varying hyper-networks yields thus a convenient way to generate surrogates of empirical social systems, to understand the mechanisms underlying their emergent properties, and to investigate the evolution of dynamical processes taking place on such structures. Here, we focus on a specific and powerful class of these models, the activity-based temporal hypergraphs. We show how activity mechanisms provide control over the time scale of the dynamics, allow high modelling flexibility, and capture heterogeneity in agents' behavior. We also highlight how the activity can straightforwardly be extracted from empirical data to create surrogate datasets. We present paradigmatic examples of such models: the higher-order activity-driven models (HADx), which show that different underlying rules for the selection of active interactions produce different higher-order dynamics; the Emerging Activity Temporal Hypergraph model (EATH), able to generate surrogates of empirical systems by using higher-order mechanisms driven by both activity and group memory. We conclude discussing future perspectives for activity-based temporal hypergraphs, highlighting the potential of this framework to bridge realistic modelling of social dynamics with the study of the complex dynamical process they can support, from social contagion to opinion dynamics.

papers.title: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring
papers.summary: Live-cell imaging of cellular and tissue samples relies predominantly on optical modalities, such as fluorescence, confocal, and multiphoton microscopy, in which cellular information is encoded in emitted photons. Photons scatter and attenuate in biological samples, restricting depth resolution, while the excitation light required to produce them induces photodamage that perturbs the very biology under observation. Magnetic fields, by contrast, traverse biological samples without attenuation at cellular length scales, but the imaging modality that extracts the encoded information, magnetic resonance imaging, cannot resolve individual cells. Here we present Quantum Cell Monitoring (QCM), a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that encodes single-cell information in stray magnetic fields rather than emitted photons and reads it out at subcellular resolution. Integrated with a specialized live-cell incubator, QCM tracks magnetically labeled living cancer for up to 72 h through their individual magnetic field signatures. It captures single-cell mitosis and morphological remodeling, as well as cell cluster formation, splitting, and migration even within dense regions where brightfield contrast collapses. By shifting the carrier of single-cell information from propagating optical photons to static magnetic stray fields, QCM decouples cell from cellular optical accessibility and auto-fluorescence, enabling sustained live-cell observation in regimes inaccessible to optical microscopy.

papers.title: A flexible regularization for magnetic vector inversion with petrophysical, structural, and sparsity constraints
papers.summary: Magnetic vector inversion (MVI) is widely used because it can account for both induced and remanent magnetization by inverting for a magnetization vector model. This flexibility comes at the cost of nonuniqueness, since the number of unknowns is three times that of scalar inversion, and prior information can be required to make the result geologically useful. Recent work has applied sparse norms to the vector model, but many of the other tools for incorporating prior information within scalar inversions remain either unavailable for a vector model or unavailable without introducing artifacts or significant nonlinearity. We introduce a vector regularization, formulated in Cartesian coordinates, that generalizes existing sparse Cartesian formulations. We formulate the smallness term to admit a Cartesian reference model, from susceptibility and oriented remanence, and a magnitude reference model, from unoriented remanence or total magnetization. Because a nonzero magnitude reference model makes the Hessian of the smallness term indefinite, we derive its eigendecomposition analytically and modify the eigenvalues so that standard conjugate-gradient solvers can be applied. We formulate the smoothness term to penalize changes in both the direction and magnitude of magnetization. It is independent of the choice of Cartesian basis, so sparse norms can be applied without coordinate-aligned artifacts, and it admits arbitrary preferred smoothing directions through a rotated gradient operator. We demonstrate the method on synthetic data from a folded body with spatially variable magnetization direction, where each form of prior information improves the recovered model. We then apply it to airborne magnetic data over the DO-27 kimberlite, where incorporating petrophysical measurements yields a model more consistent with the measured properties and the geologic model inferred from drilling.

papers.title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moir\'e Lenses Enabled by Cyclic Self-Assembly and Laser Nanoprinting
papers.summary: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moir\'e lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase levels to 54.8% for six levels. Using this six-level modulation strategy, the fabricated GO Moir\'e lens achieves continuous focal-length tuning from approximately 10 to 90 mm. Full-colour imaging with magnifications ranging from 1X to 9X is experimentally demonstrated. These results establish a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy for efficient multilevel GO flat optics and demonstrate its potential for compact, reconfigurable imaging.

papers.title: Submerged Immiscible Oil Jet: Breakup Dynamics and Droplet Size Modelling
papers.summary: Immiscible liquid-liquid jets occur in numerous industrial and environmental settings, including oil spill response and liquid-liquid extraction, yet the coupled evolution of turbulence, interfacial instability, and droplet size distribution across transitional to turbulent regimes remains poorly understood. We present a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a silicone oil jet injected into refractive-index-matched sugar water, employing simultaneous Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and Planar Laser-Induced Fluorescence (PLIF). Beyond the breakup region, mean velocity and Reynolds stress profiles exhibit self-similarity. Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) of the volume fraction reveals a systematic shift in the dominant instability mechanism with increasing Reynolds number: axisymmetric Rayleigh-Plateau modes govern breakup at low Reynolds numbers, sinuous and varicose modes coexist in the transitional regime, and Kelvin-Helmholtz-driven shear-layer breakup dominates at higher Reynolds numbers. Droplet sizes are extracted from PLIF images using a convolutional neural network-based segmentation approach. In the transitional regime, a bimodal droplet size distribution is observed, reflecting the coexistence of shear-induced breakup and Rayleigh-Plateau instability. As the Reynolds number increases and turbulent dissipation intensifies, the distribution evolves toward a single mode with smaller characteristic droplet sizes. To predict the droplet size distribution, existing population balance models are extended to include droplet coalescence. Incorporating coalescence substantially improves agreement with experimental measurements, particularly for larger droplets. These findings demonstrate that turbulent dissipation, interfacial instabilities, and droplet coalescence collectively govern the evolution of droplet size distribution in immiscible liquid-liquid jets.

papers.title: Optically gated transduction enables silicon electrical readout of mid-infrared light
papers.summary: Silicon is the dominant platform for integrated photonics, yet its wide electronic bandgap of 1.1 eV fundamentally prevents efficient detection of mid-infrared (MIR) photons through direct valence band to conduction band excitation. Existing approaches therefore seek to enhance sub-bandgap absorption or introduce external infrared absorbers. Here we demonstrate a profoundly different detection strategy based on optically gated transduction, in which MIR photons modulate a pre-established excitation state rather than directly generating photocarriers. Our device integrates Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface supporting dual resonances that simultaneously enhances optical gating in the near infrared and resonantly couples incident MIR radiation. The MIR illumination redistributes the Nd3+ emission pathways, producing an optical-state change that is converted into an electrical signal through a silicon Schottky junction. The device achieves room-temperature zero-bias detection at 6.8 um with a modulation responsivity of 103 uA/W and resolves combined gate and MIR inputs into three electrically distinguishable current states. Rather than extending silicon absorption into the infrared, this work establishes gated optical transduction as a route for reading MIR optical information on a silicon platform, opening opportunities for integrated infrared sensing, signal processing and programmable photonic systems.

papers.title: A pathway to improve Nb$_3$Sn for SRF accelerator cavities via Zr inclusion
papers.summary: Nb$_3$Sn has the potential to exceed the performance of niobium-based superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) cavities, both in particle accelerators and in high-$Q_0$ cavities operating in multi-tesla magnetic fields for axion dark matter searches. We studied how the incorporation of Zr into the Nb$_3$Sn matrix by co-sputtering affects the microstructure and superconducting properties of Nb$_3$Sn films. As the atomic fraction of Zr increased, the surface morphology improved and the bulk and surface void densities decreased. At the optimal Zr content, the superconducting properties improved and a thinner surface niobium oxide formed. These results identify co-sputtered Nb$_3$Sn:Zr as a promising material to advance the performance limits of SRF cavities.

papers.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. I. Molecular dissociation with fixed real-space and orbital partitions
papers.summary: Van Aggelen et al. [Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 11, 5558 (2009)] showed that variational second-order reduced-density-matrix (2-RDM) calculations with the standard two-index conditions dissociate diatomic molecules into fractionally charged atoms with energies far below the exact limit, a drastic violation of size consistency; the proposed subsystem constraints require auxiliary calculations with the physical fragment Hamiltonians. We show that two long-known ingredients, combined, remove most of this failure without such calculations: the requirement that the number of electrons in a part of the molecule be an integer, imposed as linear conditions on the 2-RDM, and a chemically motivated partition of the molecule into atomic regions bounded at the bond critical point of the Hartree-Fock density. In a minimal basis, compared with full configuration interaction, a single such condition reduces the energy errors of NO$^+$ and CN$^-$ at 6 {\AA} from 108.9 and 80.7 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ to less than 0.02 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. In N$_2^+$, whose fragments have the correct mean population but too small a fluctuation, the region and three-index conditions act complementarily, reducing the error at 4 {\AA} from 138.0 to 1.6 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. At the separated-atom limit, the region cuts make the $P$, $Q$, $G$ energy additive over the fragments to within 0.2 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ in 7 of 10 systems, 3 already nearly additive without cuts; adding the $T_1$ and $T_2$ conditions also makes CO nearly additive, while a nonadditive error remains for N$_2^+$ and CO$^+$. Effective partitions are those whose condition is nearly saturated by the exact state.
