papers.title: Neutrino-induced hyperon final-state interactions as a probe of the in-medium hyperon potential
papers.summary: Hyperon single-particle potentials U_Y(rho) govern hyperon propagation in nuclei and the appearance of hyperons in dense matter, where they soften the neutron-star equation of state (EOS) and lower the maximum mass M_max, the hyperon puzzle. Charged-current (anti)neutrino interactions on argon-40 create Lambda and Sigma hyperons inside the nucleus. The reconstructed Lambda yield and momentum and a kaon-vetoed final-state-interaction (FSI) Sigma+ tag respond to U_Lambda and U_Sigma at SBND and DUNE energies. We write the potential at low density as U_Y = U_Y(rho_0) (rho/rho_0)^gamma, plus a correction that vanishes at saturation. A detector-level Fisher forecast, with production cross sections, fluxes and efficiencies as nuisance parameters and the muon kinematics calibrating the production model, determines U_Lambda best at rho* = 0.82 rho_0, independently of gamma. The statistical precision is 1.5 MeV; with the production model profiled and the remaining systematic uncertainties added in quadrature, the total is +-31 MeV, of which the largest item, 18 MeV, is the convention by which the cascade applies the potential. The measurement is a check, with different systematics, of the hypernuclear constraint, +-3.3 MeV at rho*. U_Sigma is not constrained. In relativistic mean-field EOSs anchored to hypernuclear and Sigma-atom depths, M_max for n p Lambda Sigma- matter is 1.94 M_sun for GM1 and 2.03 M_sun for FSU2H with the phi meson; it depends on a high-density Lambda NN term c_Lambda that the neutrino data do not constrain. The calculations use the StrangeMC Monte Carlo generator.

papers.title: PBR sensitivity to boosted dark matter explanation for the KM3-230213A event
papers.summary: POEMMA-Balloon with Radio (PBR) is a hybrid fluorescence and optical Cherenkov telescope that is a pathfinder instrument for a future Probe Of Extreme Multi-Messenger Astrophysics (POEMMA), together with a radio instrument, to be flown on a super pressure balloon in Spring 2028. One of its science objectives is follow up of astrophysical event alerts via signals of tau decays in the atmosphere, sourced by Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. The recent report of the KM3NeT Collaboration's muon event with $ E_{\mu}=120^{+110}_{-60}$ PeV sparked searches for beyond the standard model (BSM) physics explanations. Using a specific, boosted dark matter scenario which together with the KM3NeT observation, sets a scale for the fluence of boosted dark matter in this energy range, we assess the capabilities of PBR to constrain or discover such a source for a boosted dark matter energy spectrum above $\sim 10^8$ GeV. PBR has discovery potential for dark matter energies above $10^9$ GeV, and depending on BSM input parameters, to dark matter energies as low as $1.5\times 10^8$ GeV. While the analysis is focused on one BSM example, the methodology is applicable to any BSM physics that affects tau production in the Earth.

papers.title: Update on transverse-spin azimuthal asymmetries in single-hadron SIDIS on transversely polarised deuterons at COMPASS
papers.summary: Over the years, the COMPASS experiment at CERN has pursued an extensive SIDIS programme aimed at a comprehensive understanding of the structure of the nucleon, using a high-energy muon beam and polarised targets. Within this programme, measurements with a transversely polarised deuteron target were performed in 2022 using the 160 GeV/c muon beam. In single-hadron SIDIS on such a target, eight transverse-spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetries arise, providing sensitivity to several transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions and to subleading-twist partonic correlations. We report the simultaneous extraction of all eight asymmetries from the complete 2022 deuteron sample. The Collins and Sivers asymmetries, previously presented using about 70% of the 2022 statistics, are updated with the full sample and found consistent with the earlier result, while the six remaining asymmetries are presented for the first time with the full 2022 statistics. Combined with the existing proton results, these measurements complete a comprehensive COMPASS programme on transverse-spin effects in SIDIS, providing essential input for global analyses.

papers.title: Prospects for exploring quantum-correlated neutral $D\overline{D}$ decays at STCF
papers.summary: We investigate the prospects for determining charm mixing, indirect $C\!P$ violation and hadronic parameters in charm decays with quantum-correlated neutral charm mesons at the proposed Super Tau-Charm Facility. The study is based on time-integrated double tag rates of coherent $D\overline{D}$ pairs produced at $\sqrt{s}=3.773$ and $4.030$ GeV, from $e^{+}e^{-}\to D^{(*)}\overline{D}^{(*)}$ processes. Here, one $D$ is tagged with the quasi flavour-specific decays $D\to K^-\pi^+\pi^+\pi^-$, $K^-\pi^+\pi^0$, and $K^-\pi^+$, while the other $\overline{D}$ is detected with the final states in flavour-specific mode, $C\!P$ eigenstate mode, or self-conjugate mode. The expected sensitivities are evaluated assuming an integrated luminosity of $1~{\rm ab}^{-1}$ at each energy point, demonstrating the capability on precise determination of the charm mixing parameters, the indirect $C\!P$ violation parameters, the strong-phase differences, and the coherence factors. The constraints of the hadronic-parameters provide unique inputs to the CKM angle $\gamma$ fit, while the measurements of charm mixing and indirect $C\!P$ violation parameters are complementary to the time-dependent measurements in the Belle II and LHCb experiments.

papers.title: Antenna-coupled microstrip summing network for wave-like dark matter searches
papers.summary: A commonly used technology for axion and other wave-like dark matter searches is a microwave resonator. In such experiments, the detected signal strength depends on the coupling between the resonator and the microwave transmission line that delivers power to the amplifier. In Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) and other cavity searches, this coupling is typically achieved using a compact wire antenna inserted into the cavity. While this approach is adequate for right-cylindrical cavities, it can become difficult to efficiently extract power from large-volume, multi-wavelength ($V \gg \lambda^3$) resonators targeted for higher frequencies, such as those designed by ADMX-VERA (Volume Enhanced Resonant Axion). Here, we present a solution based on a microwave slot-antenna array capacitively coupled to a microstrip "summing network," which coherently combines signals from multiple transmission lines into a single output. This summing architecture is adapted from designs originally developed for cosmic microwave background (CMB) detectors. We demonstrate the design and characterization of a new high-frequency resonator that employs this readout scheme in the $19-21$ GHz range. Finally we discuss the potential to reach Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky (DFSZ) sensitivity using multiple summing network cavities fitted into a large volume.

papers.title: Search for $e^{+}e^{-} \to \pi^0 K^+K^-J/\psi$ at $\sqrt{s}= 4.26 \sim$ 4.95 GeV
papers.summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at 27 center-of-mass energies between 4.26 and 4.95 GeV corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of $13.0~\text{fb}^{-1}$, we report the first search for the process $e^{+}e^{-} \to \pi^0 K^+K^-J/\psi$. We additionally probe the cross section spectra for potential charmonium-like vector states and invariant mass distributions for intermediate $Z_c/Z_{cs}$ state signals, and find no resonant structures consistent with these exotic candidates. Given the absence of observed resonant signals, upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are determined for the Born cross sections, along with their best-fit values, as well as for the production of the intermediate states.

papers.title: Improved measurement of $\psi(3686)\to \pi^+\pi^- \eta$
papers.summary: Using a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3) \times 10^6$ $\psi(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector, we perform a partial wave analysis of the decay $\psi(3686)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\eta$ with the $\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ invariant mass in the $\rho(770)^0$ mass region, [0.3, 2.2] $\mathrm{GeV}/c^2$. The cross section line-shape around the $\psi(3686)$ resonance is measured using energy-scan data sets, enabling the estimation of continuum contribution and its interference with the $\psi(3686)$ resonance. The branching fraction of $\psi(3686)\to\rho(770)^0\eta$ is determined to be $(1.34 \pm 0.03\pm0.13) \times 10^{-5}$. The $\psi(3686)\to a_{2}(1320)^{\pm}\pi^{\mp}$ decay is observed for the first time with a significance of $35.7\sigma$, and its partial branching fraction is measured to be $(2.13 \pm 0.05\pm0.32) \times 10^{-5}$. The $\eta$-$\eta^{\prime}$ pseudoscalar mixing angle $\theta_P$ is then found to be $(-11.2 \pm 1.6\pm3.6)^\circ$ or $(-19.4\pm 3.1\pm5.7)^\circ$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic.

papers.title: Precision measurement of the $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ branching fraction and search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ at BESIII
papers.summary: We present a precision measurement of the branching fraction of the rare decay $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$, and a search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ that couples only to the second and third lepton generations, using a data sample of $(8998 \pm 39) \times 10^6$ $J/\psi$ events collected by the BESIII detector. The branching fraction of the $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ decay is measured to be $B(J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-)=[0.91\pm0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.07~{\rm (syst.)}]\times 10^{-6}$, representing the most precise measurement to date and consistent with the theoretical prediction within one standard deviation. Additionally, we search for $CP$ asymmetry in the $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ decay and determine the T-odd observable to be $A_T = [0.05\pm 0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.01~{\rm (syst.)}]$, which is consistent with $CP$ conservation. In the search for $J/\psi\to Z^{\prime}\mu^+\mu^-$ via $Z^{\prime}\to\mu^+\mu^-$, no significant $Z^{\prime}$ signal is observed in the $\mu^+\mu^-$ invariant mass region of $(0.212,~2.6)$~GeV$/c^2$, and we set upper limits on the ${\rm U}(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}}$ model coupling constant $g^{\prime}$ ranging from 0.001 to 0.294 at the 90\% confidence level, which is comparable to the upper limits set by Belle II for $Z^{\prime}$ masses below $0.7$~GeV$/c^2$.

papers.title: Observation of $\chi_{c1,2}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+} +c.c.$ and search for $\chi_{c0}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+} +c.c.$
papers.summary: By analyzing $(2.712\pm0.014)\times10^9$ $\psi(3686)$ events collected by the BESIII detector, we report the first experimental study of the decays $\chi_{cJ}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+}+c.c.~(J=0,1,2)$. The decays $\chi_{c1}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+}+c.c.$ and $\chi_{c2}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+}+c.c.$ are observed for the first time with significances of $9.0\sigma$ each, and their branching fractions are determined to be $\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{c1}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+}+c.c.} =(9.6^{+2.2}_{-2.0}\pm0.8)\times10^{-6}$, and $\mathcal{B}_{\chi_{c2}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+}+c.c.} =(7.5^{+1.8}_{-1.5}\pm0.5)\times10^{-6}$, where the first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. No significant signal is observed for $\chi_{c0}\to p K^- K^- \bar \Xi^{+}+c.c.$, and an upper limit on its branching fraction of $12.7\times10^{-6}$ is established at the 90\% confidence level.

papers.title: Search for Neutrino-Produced Long-Lived Particles Using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope
papers.summary: The Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) is a liquid argon time projection chamber in Fermilab's Short-Baseline Neutrino Program, positioned 110 meters from the neutrino target along the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB). In addition to its neutrino physics goals, SBND enables searches for new physics, including long-lived particles (LLPs) produced via neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay into visible final states. Although neutrino data taking with the full SBND experiment began in December 2024, a subset of the Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) system operated from 2017--2018 as a standalone detector, referred to as the CRT Beam Telescope, collecting data corresponding to $2.95\times 10^{20}$ protons on target from the BNB. Originally intended for commissioning and performance studies, the substantial dataset collected also enables searches for displaced LLP decays. This paper presents the first search for physics beyond the Standard Model using data from the SBND CRT Beam Telescope, targeting LLP decays into electron-positron pairs. We observe no significant excess above the expected background and set 90% confidence-level upper limits on an effective production cross section at the level of $10^{-38}$ cm$^2$ for laboratory decay lengths of 0.3-100 m. These results complement existing searches by probing displaced decay signatures at meter-scale decay lengths.

papers.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda$ elliptic flow
papers.summary: The first measurement of the elliptic-flow coefficient ($v_{2}$) of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ hadrons performed in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV with the ALICE detector is presented as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) in central and semi-central collisions. For the $\phi$ meson, in particular, this is the first measurement of the elliptic flow in a small collision system. At low $p_{\rm T}$, a characteristic mass ordering of $v_{2}$ is observed, consistent with collective expansion of the system, in which heavier hadrons are shifted to higher $p_{\rm T}$ by a common velocity field. At intermediate $p_{\rm T}$, above 3 GeV/$c$, a baryon$-$meson splitting with a $10\sigma$ significance emerges, with the $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ baryon exhibiting larger $v_{2}$ values than mesons, while, despite its mass being close to the mass of the $\Lambda$, the $\phi$ follows the K$^{0}_{\rm S}$. The $\phi$ meson behavior disfavors a purely mass-driven interpretation of the observed patterns and supports the role of hadronization via quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium. These results provide complementary evidence that key signatures of partonic collectivity observed in Pb$-$Pb collisions persist in light nucleus$-$nucleus systems.

papers.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-$\Lambda$ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.summary: The recent measurements of event-by-event correlations between the antideuteron and antiproton numbers in Pb$-$Pb collisions at the LHC deviate from the statistical hadronization model parameterizations that describe the yields and fluctuations of light-flavored hadrons. This discrepancy may stem from nucleosynthesis processes involved in the formation of composite states like antideuterons. In this letter, we present the first measurement of the antideuteron$-$net-$\Lambda$ number correlation obtained in Pb$-$Pb collisions with the ALICE detector. This quantity is mostly sensitive to the quantum-number correlations induced by the hadronization process, as $\Lambda$ hyperons are not constituents of antideuterons. Both the antideuteron$-$net-$\Lambda$ number correlation and the normalized second-order cumulant of the net-$\Lambda$ number are well described by the statistical hadronization model implemented in Thermal-FIST. This establishes strong evidence that the antideuteron$-$antiproton correlation is driven by the nucleosynthesis processes, while the correlation between antideuterons and non-nucleonic hadrons is primarily sensitive to the hadronization mechanism.

papers.title: Search for resonant production of pairs of dijet resonances through broad mediators in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A reinterpretation of a prior narrow-resonance search is performed to investigate the resonant production of pairs of dijet resonances via broad mediators. This analysis targets events with four resolved jets, requiring dijet invariant masses greater than 0.2 TeV and four-jet invariant masses greater than 1.6 TeV. The search uses a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the CMS experiment in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV. The reinterpretation considers the production of new heavy four-jet resonances, with widths ranging from 1.5 to 10% of their mass, which decay to a pair of dijet resonances. This analysis probes resonant production in the four-jet and dijet mass distributions. Upper limits at 95% confidence level and significances are reported on the production cross section of new resonances as functions of their widths and masses, between 2 and 10 TeV. In particular, at a four-jet resonance mass of 8.6 TeV, the local (global) significance ranges from 3.9 (1.6) to 3.6 (1.4) standard deviations (s.d.) as the resonance width is increased from 1.5 to 10%. This relative insensitivity to the choice of width indicates that a broad resonance is an equally valid interpretation of this excess. The broad resonance hypothesis at a resonance mass of 8.6 TeV is supported by the presence of an event with a four-jet mass of 5.8 TeV and an average dijet mass of 2.0 TeV. Also, we report the reinterpretation of a second effect, at a four-jet resonance mass of 3.6 TeV, which has a local (global) significance of up to 3.9 (2.2) s.d.

papers.title: Inclusive jet cross section in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 200$ and $510$ GeV
papers.summary: Jets are collimated clusters of particles formed by the hadronization of partons following a hard interaction. In proton-proton ($pp$) collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC), jet production is dominated by $gg$ and $qg$ partonic processes, allowing us to directly probe the gluon parton distribution function (PDF) in the proton in a way complementary to deep inelastic scattering. In this paper, we report the double-differential inclusive-jet cross sections as a function of jet transverse momentum, $p_{\rm T}$, and pseudorapidity, $\eta$, at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s} = 200$ and $510$~GeV, from $pp$ collisions studied with the STAR detector. The jet $p_{\rm T}$ is corrected for underlying event contributions by applying an off-axis cone method. At mid-pseudorapidity, $|\eta| < 0.9$, the kinematic coverage of our data extends to $0.07 < x_{\rm T} \text{ (}= 2p_{\rm T}{} / \sqrt{s} \text{)} < 0.5$ and $0.03 < x_{\rm T} < 0.31$ at $\sqrt{s} = 200$~and 510 GeV, respectively, where the gluon PDF is poorly constrained by the TeV-scale $pp$~($p\bar{p}$) colliders. The inclusive jet cross sections are compared to the next-to-next-to-leading order perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations using several recent PDF sets as inputs. These results will further constrain the gluon PDF, help tune Monte Carlo generators, and provide critical reference data needed to study the quark-gluon plasma.

papers.title: Study of $\phi\to K\bar{K}$ in the amplitude analysis of $D^{+}\to K_{S}^{0}K_{L}^{0}\pi^{+}$
papers.summary: We present the first amplitude analysis and branching fraction measurement of $D^{+} \rightarrow K_{S}^{0}K_{L}^{0}\pi^{+}$ decay. The analysis uses a dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 20.3~$\rm fb^{-1}$, which was recorded at a center-of-mass energy 3.773~GeV by the BESIII detector. The measured branching fraction is $\mathcal{B}(D^{+} \rightarrow K_{S}^{0}K_{L}^{0}\pi^{+})=(5.780\pm0.085\pm 0.052)\times10^{-3}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic. Using the known value of ${\cal B}(D^+ \to \phi \pi^+,\,\phi \to K^+K^-)$, we determine the relative branching fraction between $\phi \to K_{S}^0K_{L}^0$ and $\phi \to K^+K^-$ to be $\mathcal{B}(D^{+} \to \phi \pi^{+}, \phi \to K_{S}^0K_{L}^0)/\mathcal{B}(D^{+} \to \phi \pi^{+}, \phi \to K^+K^-)= 0.628\pm0.022\pm 0.015\pm0.017$, where the third uncertainty is related to $\mathcal{B}(D^{+} \to \phi \pi^{+}, \phi \to K^+K^-)$. This result is significantly lower than the previous world average and is consistent with the isospin expectation for the $\phi$ meson's coupling to charged and neutral kaon pairs.

papers.title: Precise Measurement of the Inclusive Cross Sections of Open-Charm Mesons at Energies from 3.80 to 4.95 GeV
papers.summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from $3.80$ to $4.95~\text{GeV}$, the inclusive production cross sections of open-charm mesons, $\sigma(e^{+}e^{-}\to D^{0}/D^{+}/D_{s}^{+}+X)$, are measured by tagging a $D^0$, $D^+$, or $D_s^+$ meson, where $X$ denotes any accompanying particles. Open-charm production dominates the total hadronic yield above threshold. Therefore these measurements provide a vital reference for understanding hadron production and for validating global $R$ value results. The results offer crucial inputs for investigating heavier charmonia and exotic states coupled to open-charm final states, while serving as a benchmark for comparison with the sum of measured exclusive channels. This comparison directly evaluates the completeness of current exclusive datasets and clarifies the underlying hadronization mechanisms in the open-charm region.

papers.title: Easier parameter scans with hmcdj
papers.summary: We present hmcdj, a new tool developed to ease the process of generating large numbers of gauge ensembles for a given theory. Building on top of the Grid library, hmcdj allows quick specification of lattice gauge theories in C++ with minimal boilerplate, and precise specification of per-ensemble parameters to be controlled at run time from a YAML input file. Additionally, it supports many quality-of-life features for managing large numbers of running jobs, including automatic tuning of the molecular dynamics step size to control the Metropolis acceptance rate; output of ILDG-compliant data; and integration with HPC schedulers to dynamically adapt the target trajectory count of a job to match its time limits. hmcdj is openly available under the GPLv2 license, and welcomes new contributions.

papers.title: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models
papers.summary: Gauge-Higgs theory in flat spacetime provides a prime theoretical model of multiple phases of matter with distinct entanglement structures. More recently, there has been interest in hyperbolic space and the influence its extensive boundaries have on these structures. Entanglement transitions between non-equilibrium phases, such as topological phases, can be realized by the competition of non-commutating measurements. Here we study the entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices described by measurement-only dynamics. We chart 2D phase diagrams by employing topological entanglement entropy and introducing a generalized measurement-induced entanglement tailored for hyperbolic Higgs phases. Utilizing duality, we find a phase absent in Euclidean space, wherein the bulk lattice hosts separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order. Transitions between this "archipelago" phase and neighboring topological and trivial phases feature a critical exponent $\delta$ belonging to a mean-field universality class. Our essential tool is a 3D resource state inspired by measurement-based quantum computation that simulates the spacetime evolution of the 2D quantum state with a third direction of entanglement. This allows us to analyze spacetime "sponges" of entanglement, which map to classical percolation theory and allow us to infer values of critical points on our phase diagrams' boundaries.

papers.title: The [Y/Mg] chemical clock and the stellar ages of solar-type stars in the solar neighbourhood
papers.summary: Stellar ages are an important parameter for studying the chemical evolution of the Galaxy. To improve age estimates, various complementary methods to the conventional isochrone-fitting method have been implemented in the last decade. The [Y/Mg] ratio has been proposed as a chemical clock for solar-metallicity stars, due to its strong dependence on stellar age. In this work, we study the behaviour of the abundance ratio [Y/Mg] in metal-poor stars, along with other solar-type disk stars, as a function of stellar age determined through isochrones. The analysis is based on the line-by-line differential technique, applied to a sample covering a wide metallicity range ($-$0.70 $\leq$ [Fe/H] $<$ +0.34), using high-resolution (R = 115,000) and high S/N spectra (= 270 - 1000) taken with the HARPS spectrograph at the ESO La Silla Observatory. We find that the stellar sample follows a metallicity-dependent [Y/Mg]-Age relation.

papers.title: The SIRMOS mission concept: a space-based near-IR spectroscopic survey of 100 million galaxies in the Euclid Wide Survey footprint
papers.summary: SIRMOS is a mission concept for a future NASA Astrophysics Explorer opportunity that aims to revolutionize our understanding of the universe by mapping the large-scale structure of galaxies in unprecedented breadth and detail to explore cosmic origins and evolution. Specifically, the primary science goals of SIRMOS are to discover how cosmic inflation seeded large-scale structure, reveal the nature of the accelerating expansion of the universe, and measure the sum of neutrino masses to exceptionally high precision. Its secondary science goals include determining how environment shapes galaxy evolution at cosmic noon and beyond, and probing the Milky Way's dust-enshrouded regions, reaching the far side of our Galaxy. To accomplish its transformative science goals, SIRMOS executes a 3-year cosmology survey over the Euclid footprint of ~14,000 deg$^2$, obtaining slit spectra for ~100 million galaxies at 1<z<4. SIRMOS is the first space mission designed specifically to leverage Euclid's wide near-infrared (IR) imaging survey for target selection and employs a digital micro-mirror device (DMD) to acquire up to 4,000 simultaneous spectra over a wide 0.9 deg$^2$ field of view. The instrument's excellent spectral resolution of $R=1300$ and continuous wavelength coverage from 1.25--2.5 $\mu$m capture the redshifts of distant galaxies with no gaps, reducing systematic biases to achieve ground-breaking science.

papers.title: A High Precision Metacalibration Response Correction
papers.summary: In Metacalibration the shear response of a weak lensing measurement is estimated by applying an artificial shear to the image, but the shear operation imprints a spin-2 modulation on the image noise power, which biases the measured response. The standard fix adds a sheared noise field that symmetrizes the anisotropy, at the cost of doubling the noise variance ($\sqrt2$ in the noise). The fusion correction presented in this note reaches the same unbiased response while adding only the minimum power needed. It measures the noise power transfer by passing an impulse through the Metacal process, forms the common-level azimuthal deficit that equalizes the spin-2 ($m{=}2$) and spin-6 ($m{=}6$) modulations across the metacal types, and adds just that deficit by filtering the rotated noise field. The fusion correction raises the per-pixel noise by only $\sim2\%$ for a round PSF (versus $\sqrt2$ for the standard correction), rising toward the $\sqrt2$ level only for highly elliptical PSFs.

papers.title: Field-level modeling of halo and galaxy alignments
papers.summary: We develop an effective field theory (EFT) of intrinsic alignments at the level of spin-2 field fluctuations of large-scale structure tracers, such as the shapes of galaxies and dark matter halos. Our perturbative model includes the non-linear treatment of the Zel'dovich displacement, and contains all necessary shape operators through the third order. We apply our field-level model to the full 3D distribution of galaxy shapes, whose sky projections are a known contaminant of cosmic shear measurements. Our field-level EFT model achieves a better description of the helicity fields of dark matter halo shapes than the standard non-linear alignment (NLA) and tidal torquing + tidal alignment (TATT) models in the literature, as evidenced by improved correlations with the simulations' initial conditions. We perform precision measurements of field-level bias parameters by means of a generalized least-squares problem, for which we derive an optimal estimator and analytic covariance matrices. We measure the full set of linear, quadratic, and cubic shape bias coefficients as a function of halo mass in the $\texttt{Quijote}$ N-body simulations. We then study the intrinsic alignments of galaxies in the $\texttt{FLAMINGO}$ hydrodynamical simulation, focusing on observationally relevant samples: spirals, ellipticals, luminous red galaxies (LRG) and emission-line galaxies (ELG). We detect linear and nonlinear alignment coefficients at high significance for LRG, spiral and elliptical galaxies. We also find evidence for non-zero density-weighted tidal bias coefficient of the simulated ELG. This work supports the notion that EFT-based models of alignments will be paramount in optimally extracting constraints from future shape correlations, and lays the foundation for the development of simulation-based priors for future galaxy shape samples.

papers.title: Two-dimensional galaxy cluster shapes using lensing data: a simulated analysis
papers.summary: Context. Cluster morphology reflects assembly history and dynamical state. High-resolution weak lensing can reveal departures from spherical symmetry, but its ability to recover two-dimensional shapes remains less explored. Aims. We assess how reliably weak lensing recovers projected cluster morphology and its dependence on orientation and dynamical state. We also compare large-scale weak-lensing morphology with that traced by strong lensing near the cluster centre. Methods. We study three clusters at $z=0.22$ from The Three Hundred Project, representing relaxed, mildly disturbed and unrelaxed systems. For each, we consider three random projections and three along the principal axes of the mass tensor. For each projection, we generate 128 weak-lensing catalogues with a source density of 30 arcmin$^{-2}$ and intrinsic ellipticity dispersion $\sigma_{\epsilon}=0.3$. We constrain mass and concentration from one-dimensional NFW and BMO fits, then recover ellipticity, position angle and centre using a two-dimensional elliptical NFW model. We also measure morphology from true convergence maps, Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions and strong-lensing tangential critical lines. Results. Recovered parameters depend on orientation and dynamical state. The relaxed cluster has similar inner and large-scale shapes, whereas disturbed systems appear more elliptical centrally. Two-dimensional weak-lensing modelling recovers the projected mass orientation despite source sampling and shape noise. Kaiser \& Squires reconstructions recover the position angle well but favour rounder mass distributions. Centroid offsets are larger in unrelaxed systems. Conclusions. Combining weak- and strong-lensing morphology probes cluster structure across physical scales and offers a promising way to investigate morphology and dynamical state.

papers.title: The Stellar Populations of Resolved Galaxies
papers.summary: The study of galaxies outside the Milky Way using observations of resolved stellar populations has experienced extraordinary growth over the past two decades. There now exist panchromatic photometry and precise astrometry for hundreds of millions of individually resolved stars in hundreds of galaxies that span $\sim10^9$ in luminosity, $\sim10^3$ in metallicity, and sample a wide range of environments. Here, we review advances in extragalactic astronomy enabled by resolved stellar population imaging. We summarize major observational programs and focus on four interconnected science areas: the star formation histories of galaxies, 'bursty' star formation, the stellar initial mass function, and the orbital histories of Local Group galaxies. We review the literature in each area, synthesize key findings, identify emerging trends, and discuss how new and future facilities (e.g., JWST, LSST, Euclid, Roman, CSST, ELTs, HWO) will enable further progress. Finally, we highlight shortcomings in current datasets and discuss promising directions for new areas of investigation.

papers.title: Detection of star formation in a near-pristine pocket of the Universe
papers.summary: We detect two high-confidence star-forming sources in the environment of a chemically near-pristine ([Fe/H] $<-3.66~;2\sigma)$ Damped Ly$\alpha$ system (DLA) using Keck/KCWI. These are found via the hydrogen Ly$\alpha$ emission line at $\Delta v=-1200$ kms$^{-1}$ (LAE1) and $\Delta v = -200$ kms$^{-1}$ (LAE2) relative to the DLA redshift ($z_{\rm abs} = 3.078$) at an impact parameter of $b=66$ physical kpc and $b=137$ physical kpc. We measure Ly$\alpha$ fluxes of $F(\rm Ly\alpha)_{\rm LAE1} =4.4\pm 0.7\times10^{-18}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}$ and $F(\rm Ly\alpha)_{\rm LAE2} =3.8\pm 0.9\times10^{-18}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}$. This marks the first detection of star formation in the environment of a chemically near-pristine DLA. We use red channel Keck/KCRM data to place limits on the associated He II 1640 A emission flux of these sources, $F(\rm He\,II)<3.8\times10^{-19}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}~(3\sigma)$ and $F(\rm He\,II) <3.7\times10^{-19}~\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}~(3\sigma)$. The weak and narrow properties of the Ly$\alpha$ emission, combined with the inferred position on the mass-metallicity relation, suggest a metal-paucity of these galaxies. Future rest-frame optical observations are required to pin down the metallicity of LAE1 and LAE2 and test if chemically near-pristine DLAs can be used as a signpost to search for primitive, metal-poor galaxies 2 Gyrs after the Big Bang.

papers.title: What sets the star-formation rate in the Milky Way? I. A multi-scale view of the star-formation rate
papers.summary: Context. The star-formation rate (SFR) is one of the key quantities that characterizes the star formation process and has been extensively investigated both observationally and theoretically. Aims. We aim to provide a coherent multi-scale view of star formation by connecting Galactic-scale conditions (kpc) to the properties of individual star-forming clumps at sub-parsec scales. Methods. We perform a set of numerical simulations with large-scale turbulent forcing designed to reproduce physical conditions typical of the solar neighbourhood. Using adaptive zooming down to 0.03 pc, we obtain a population of star-forming clumps that is analyzed and compared with observational catalogues in a companion paper. Results. For column densities and velocity dispersions consistent with Galactic values, the resulting SFR is close to the rate inferred for the Milky Way. Comparing this value with the SFR expected from pure free-fall collapse shows that turbulence provides multiscale support that lowers the SFR by more than an order of magnitude. Additional regulation by stellar feedback, including ionizing radiation and protostellar outflows, likely reduces the SFR by an additional factor of 3-10. Comparisons with observations across multiple spatial scales show good overall agreement with this model. Conclusions. These results support a picture in which turbulence plays a central role in regulating star formation in the Milky Way. In combination with stellar feedback, it limits the star formation efficiency to only a few percent. Key words. stars: formation -- ISM: clouds -- physical processes: turbulence

papers.title: Does the Escape Fraction Prescription Shape Reionization History and Morphology?
papers.summary: The escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, is one of the least constrained quantities of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), and the opacity of the intergalactic medium prevents its direct measurement at high redshifts. We constrain three power-law parameterizations, $f_{\rm esc}(z)$, $f_{\rm esc}(M_{\rm h})$, and $f_{\rm esc}(z, M_{\rm h})$, against JWST UV luminosity functions and EoR observables (the ionizing emissivity, the neutral hydrogen fraction, and the Thomson optical depth) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo, with priors that allow $f_{\rm esc}$ to either increase or decrease with redshift and halo mass. We then propagate the best-fit models into the semi-numerical simulation SimFast21 and compare their ionization morphology and 21 cm power spectra with those of a constant-$f_{\rm esc}$ model. All models reproduce the observations with nearly identical global reionization histories. The data favor an escape fraction that decreases with increasing redshift, from $\approx 0.8$ at $z = 5$ to $\approx 0.35$ at $z = 15$. The halo-mass-only model prefers $f_{\rm esc}$ increasing with halo mass, but this trend acts as a proxy for redshift evolution. When we vary both dependencies jointly, the data prefer a mass-independent $f_{\rm esc}$. At matched global neutral fraction, the ionization morphology is closely similar for all four prescriptions, and the 21 cm power spectra agree to within $\approx 10\%$. These results suggest that, once calibrated against the same observations, the details of the $f_{\rm esc}$ prescription, which are set by the physics of the interstellar medium, largely average out in both the global observables and the 21 cm power spectrum. Distinguishing them may require statistics beyond the power spectrum, such as sightline statistics of the Ly$\alpha$ and 21 cm forests, or forecasts that exploit their small differences in reionization timing.

papers.title: An intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion in the Small Magellanic Cloud
papers.summary: We present discovery of SMASH J004005$-$733351, an intermediate-mass stripped helium star in the Small Magellanic Cloud with a dark companion. The system was identified in a new optical color-selected survey for stripped stars and confirmed through spectroscopic follow-up. We measure an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb}=19.95\pm 0.002$ hours and a radial-velocity semi-amplitude of $K=91.7 ^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. Simultaneous modeling of the optical spectrum and ultraviolet-to-optical spectral energy distribution yields a stripped star evolutionary mass $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$, temperature $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4$ kK, surface gravity $\log g= 4.76 \pm 0.12$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot)= 4.28 \pm 0.13$, radius $R= 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, and an unusually high surface hydrogen abundance of $X_{\rm H, s}=0.63 \pm 0.04$. The companion is undetected spectroscopically, and the orbital solution and stripped-star evolutionary mass imply a minimum companion mass of $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$. The absence of photometric variability from irradiation rules out a main-sequence companion. The companion is most likely a neutron star (NS), although a massive white dwarf or low-mass stripped star cannot be fully excluded. Binary evolution models predict that the stripped star will refill its Roche lobe after core helium exhaustion, likely producing a stripped or ultra-stripped supernova and ultimately a double NS binary if the system survives. SMASH J004005$-$733351 is among the first known stripped stars with a compact object companion. The system provides a new empirical benchmark for the late stages of binary interaction that lead to (ultra-)stripped supernovae and double NS binaries.

papers.title: ECH0EZ: Estimating the Hubble constant with ZTF SN Ia DR2
papers.summary: Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are instrumental for a precise measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) from the local distance ladder, yet the data used hitherto for this purpose are inhomogeneous and subject to severe selection effects. We present the first, preliminary, cosmological analysis of 772 SNe Ia from the Zwicky Transient Facility's second data release: an untargeted single-telescope sample whose volume-limited subset (z<0.06) is largely free of Malmquist bias. We correct the public data for known instrumental and calibration biases and the redshifts for peculiar motions. Using the 42 SH0ES calibrators (their host distances computed from Cepheids and geometric anchors) and a Bayesian hierarchical model of SN Ia standardisation, dust extinction, redshift and calibration uncertainties, we infer $H_0 = (71.6 \pm 1.5)$ km/s/Mpc after marginalising over deceleration with a flat prior (or $(72.3 \pm 1.1)$ km/s/Mpc if a prior on matter density from Pantheon+ is imposed), with the uncertainty dominated by the number of calibrators. We demonstrate robustness to the choice of light-curve and Milky Way dust models and to extensions of the model to include peculiar-velocity correlations, a host-mass step, and two stretch populations. These results are in agreement with previous distance-ladder measurements and $2.7\sigma$ ($4.1\sigma$) away from the value obtained from Planck data, suggesting that the resolution of the Hubble tension lies outside of SNe Ia---or the distance ladder entirely.

papers.title: Dependence of Merger-driven Star Formation and Gas-phase Metallicity Evolution on Merger Type and Stellar Mass
papers.summary: Galaxy mergers play a fundamental role in driving gas inflows, altering star formation, and redistributing metals, yet how these processes depend on merger type, merger stage, and progenitor galaxy properties remains incompletely understood. In this work, we investigate the resolved impact of mergers on star formation rate (SFR) and gas-phase metallicity using MaNGA integral-field spectroscopy and the MaNGA Galaxy Merger Catalog of Comerford et al. (2024). By comparing merger galaxies to matched controls, we quantify local offsets in SFR and metallicity as functions of merger type, merger stage, stellar mass, and galactocentric radius. We find that major mergers generally exhibit stronger SFR enhancement and greater metallicity dilution than minor mergers. In major mergers, SFR enhancement is often spatially extended, whereas in minor mergers it is weaker and more centrally concentrated. The SFR response in major mergers varies non-monotonically with merger stage, with stronger enhancement in the early (first-passage) and post-coalescence stages and weaker enhancement in the late (between-passage) stage. Metallicity dilution is generally strongest in early-stage major mergers and weaker at later stages, although this stage dependence is not monotonic across all stellar-mass bins. We also find stellar-mass dependence that lower-mass systems show stronger metallicity dilution in both major and minor mergers, while the strongest SFR enhancement occurs in intermediate- and high-mass major mergers. These results show that the resolved star formation and metallicity responses depend jointly on merger type, merger stage, and stellar mass and exhibit different behaviors across the merger sequence.

papers.title: Prospects for Near-Far Constraints on Reionization from Simulated LSST Observations of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies and Stellar Streams
papers.summary: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will detect resolved stellar populations of intact dwarf galaxies and disrupted stellar streams in the Milky Way (MW) halo and beyond, opening a new avenue for near-field cosmology, particularly for constraining the faint galaxies during reionization. To interpret these data, we present and publicly release mock LSST catalogs of satellites, stellar streams, phase-mixed galaxies, and field galaxies around 13 MW-mass hosts in the FIRE-2 zoom-in simulations, generated with \textsf{py-ananke}. Using a surface brightness limit of $\mu_{g} \leq 34$ $\rm{mag}$ $\rm{arcsec^{-2}}$, we find that $\approx29\%$ of streams with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 5 \times 10^5$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable with tidal tails, while another $\approx38\%$ are detectable only through their bound progenitors and would appear as satellites. We estimate that $\approx96\%$ of satellites and $\approx64\%$ of field galaxies (out to $\sim$3.5 Mpc) with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{5}$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable, decreasing to $\approx$59\% and $\approx$42\% for $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{4.5}$ $M_{\odot}$ owing to resolution limits. Including streams detectable as satellites reproduces the radial distribution of observed MW satellites, suggesting that some observed satellites may be bound remnants of disrupted systems. Our mock galaxies match the sizes of observed satellites with $M_{\rm{V}} \lesssim -6$. Star-formation histories computed from only the detectable stars broadly recover the simulated star-formation histories. As an application, we test the near-far technique for reconstructing the proto-MW ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) during reionization ($z \gtrsim 6$). Adding the detectable streams improves the recovered faint-end slope at $z = 7$ and reduces the halo-to-halo scatter by $\approx33\%$.

papers.title: What sets the star-formation rate in the Milky Way?. II. Comparing the star-forming clumps from simulations and observations
papers.summary: Context. Linking the star formation (SF) properties of dense clumps to their parent large-scale environment is a key step to interpret Galactic surveys. Achieving a consistent, multi-scale picture of SF requires a comparative analysis of observations and simulations. Aims. We exploit kiloparsec-scale magneto-hydrodynamic simulations designed to reproduce local Milky Way conditions. Leveraging the wide range of scales covered by the simulations (reaching a resolution of 0.03 pc), we aim to compare the properties of the simulated population of star-forming clumps with observational catalogues. Methods. After extracting the star-forming structures with the HOP clump-finding algorithm, we compare their physical (mass and size) and SF properties (SF rate and efficiency) with those of the Hi-GAL compact source catalogue. Results. Despite the different methodologies and the three-dimensional nature of our clump extraction, the simulated clumps show good agreement with the observed sample in their mass and size distributions. We discover a consistently linear relation between mass and SF rate (SFR) for the simulated clumps, which is remarkably independent of the initial conditions of the boxes. Using scaling relations to distinguish between turbulence- and gravity-regulated gas inflow onto the clump scales, we find tentative evidence in favour of a gravity-regulated regime of SF at the probed sub-parsec scales. Key words. methods: numerical - stars: formation - ISM: clouds

papers.title: The evolutionary history of ultra-compact accreting binaries. II. HST spectroscopy of two eclipsing AM CVn stars
papers.summary: AM CVn stars are ultra-compact binaries in which a white dwarf (WD) accretes helium-rich material from a hydrogen-deficient donor. They are promising mHz gravitational-wave sources and potential progenitors of Type Ia supernovae. However, their evolutionary pathways remain uncertain. Three formation channels have been proposed: the WD, helium star, and cataclysmic variable channels. We aim to determine the atmospheric chemical composition of the underlying accreting WDs in two eclipsing AM CVn systems, YZ LMi and ZTF J0407-00, in order to constrain their formation channels. Using ultraviolet spectra obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope, we modelled the atmospheres of the accreting WDs, whose surface compositions are enriched by material transferred from the donor and therefore trace the donor's composition. In particular, the nitrogen-to-carbon abundance ratio provides a diagnostic of the donor's nuclear burning history and hence of the system's formation channel. We measure effective temperatures Teff = 24400 $\pm$ 1500 K and surface gravities logg = 8.36 $\pm$ 0.05 for YZ LMi, and Teff = 29900 $\pm$ 2200 K and logg = 8.37 $\pm$ 0.05 for ZTF J0407-00. The inferred masses of the two WDs are 0.84 $\pm$ 0.10 and 0.86 $\pm$ 0.12 solar masses, respectively. Carbon is not detected in either system, yielding lower limits on the nitrogen-to-carbon mass ratio of N/C > 117 and N/C > 185. We increase from one to three the number of AM CVn systems whose accreting WDs and chemical abundances have been analysed using detailed UV atmosphere models. The high N/C ratios rule out the helium star formation channel for both systems. The WD channel is favoured by the absence of detectable hydrogen at all observed wavelengths, although the evolved cataclysmic variable channel cannot be conclusively excluded.

papers.title: CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker--Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations
papers.summary: Numerical modeling of cosmic-ray (CR) spectra and the resulting non-thermal emission is important for understanding the physical mechanisms of CR acceleration and transport in astrophysical environments. Galaxy clusters and cosmic filaments provide particularly important environments for studying these processes, where shocks, turbulence, magnetic fields, and CRs jointly shape diffuse synchrotron emission. Spectrally resolved modeling of CRs, including cooling, re-acceleration, and hadronic interactions, requires solving time-dependent Fokker--Planck (FP) equations. An increasing number of studies employ FP solvers coupled with magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) simulations to follow the evolution of CRs in dynamically evolving environments. We present a new C/C++-based FP solver with GPU acceleration for post-processing outputs from cosmological MHD simulations. The code evolves CR proton and electron spectra along Lagrangian tracer trajectories and consistently includes re-acceleration and secondary-particle production processes. With the Chang--Cooper finite-difference scheme, the FP equation for each tracer is reduced to an independent tridiagonal system, which is solved on NVIDIA GPUs using a CUDA implementation of the parallel cyclic reduction (PCR) algorithm. The code uses sub-stepping between tracer snapshots, with the timestep constrained by the relevant CR cooling or re-acceleration timescale, and a batching algorithm that groups tracers with similar sub-stepping patterns for efficient execution. We find that the GPU acceleration increases the per-node throughput by a factor of $\approx$10 on the Leonardo Booster system operated by CINECA. The fast FP solver is useful for high-resolution simulations dedicated to comparison with next-generation radio observations and future multi-messenger applications combining radio, gamma-ray, and high-energy neutrino observations.

papers.title: The Cosmic Ultraviolet Baryon Survey X: Density and Pressure Profiles of Clumpy Circumgalactic Gas at $z=0.4-0.7$
papers.summary: The thermodynamic state and turbulent properties of the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) are investigated for 23 galaxies and galaxy groups at intermediate redshift ($z=0.4$--0.7) in the Cosmic Ultraviolet Baryon Survey (CUBS) midz sample using background QSOs within the virial radius. Kinematically resolved absorption-line measurements from Hubble Space Telescope/COS and STIS spectra, combined with photoionization modeling, yield gas densities of $n_\mathrm{H}\approx10^{-4}$--$10^{-2} \ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, temperatures of $T\approx(1$--$5) \times 10^4\,\mathrm{K}$, and non-thermal line broadening of $b_\mathrm{NT}\approx2$--$30 \ \mathrm{km \ s^{-1}}$ for individual cool clumps. Combined with published samples at similar redshifts, the results indicate that photoionization equilibrium accurately describes the cool CGM and that turbulent motions are predominantly subsonic. At fixed projected distance, cool-gas density decreases systematically with halo mass, while inferred cool-gas pressures in $M_h\approx10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ halos are consistent with hot-gas pressures inferred from stacked X-ray observations. The analysis uncovers a near constant total cool gas mass across a broad halo mass range, which directly translates to a declining baryon mass fraction in the cool phase from $\approx 6$--$19\%$ in halos of $M_h \approx 10^{12}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ to $\approx 0.6$--$1.5\%$ in halos of $M_h \approx 10^{13}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$. Finally, several CUBS galaxies exhibit kinematically aligned low- and high-ionization species spanning up to two orders of magnitude in density, reflecting local fluctuations in the halo gas pressure.

papers.title: Heavy Seeds and the Multi-scale Fueling of Early Supermassive Black Holes and Little Red Dots
papers.summary: The formation of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in the early Universe has been a longstanding mystery due to the brief period available to assemble them. More recently, the unexpected discovery with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) of Little Red Dots (LRDs), compact sources exhibiting signatures of active galactic nuclei (AGN), has accentuated this challenge. Cosmological simulations investigating their formation and evolution confront the limitation that the compact scale of SMBH/LRD physics cannot be simultaneously resolved with the larger-scale cosmological environment. We address this limitation by utilizing a cutout technique, selecting a targeted region around an SMBH seed from a cosmological parent simulation and re-running the cutout at higher (sub-pc) resolution for shorter periods. We explore two SMBH formation scenarios: the standard, light seed stellar-remnant case, and the heavy-seed, direct collapse black hole (DCBH) channel. Within the high-resolution achieved by the cutouts, the DCBH, due to its larger mass, is able to induce a buildup of high density gas nearby and accrete gas in bursts of super-Eddington phases, growing in mass and producing an LRD-like spectrum. In contrast, the stellar remnant cannot do so and remains dormant, unable to affect the nearby gas or significantly evolve by gas accretion alone. Therefore, we find that observed high-redshift SMBHs and LRDs require the existence of heavy seeds to assemble dense gas around themselves, enabling efficient growth and producing red optical spectra with strong Balmer breaks resembling LRDs.

papers.title: Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS) X. Preliminary statistics of 6.7 GHz masers near POETS sources
papers.summary: So far, the POETS survey has focused on studying at high angular resolution the properties of both 22.2 GHz H2O masers and the radio continuum emission near young stellar objects (YSOs). Now, we want to add the information coming from another star formation tracer, the Class II 6.7 GHz CH3OH (methanol) maser, towards the same POETS targets. We seek to probe the existence of 6.7 GHz maser emission near POETS sources with high sensitivity observations and study their kinematic properties with respect to local radio continuum and 22.2 GHz maser emission at high angular and spectral resolutions. Within the POETS survey, we used the Very Large Array (VLA) in the A configuration, operating at high spectral resolution (0.1 km/s) and achieving a sensitivity of a few mJy/beam per channel map, in order to (i) probe the emission from methanol gas in the 6.7 GHz maser transition and (ii) trace its absolute spatial distribution and local standard of rest velocity. We present a preliminary analysis of 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser emission toward a subsample of the POETS survey (22 fields observed so far), 60 % of which show detection above a brightness temperature threshold of 10^7 K. Five sources among this subsample are new detections. We draw a 6.7 GHz maser brightness function by studying the distribution of the intrinsic luminosity of the maser population and predict that more than 30 % of the whole population is undetected at typical interferometric sensitivities of a few 10 mJy/beam. We confirm that 6.7 GHz masers arise close to the young star they are associated with and quantify that, on average, 90 % of them are distributed within radii of 3000 au only. Furthermore, we find a tight correlation between the 6.7 GHz maser luminosity coming from a given source and the local free-free emission, suggesting that the radio continuum provides the dominant source of seed photons amplified by the methanol gas.

papers.title: Dynamical constraints on the companion mass from pulsar timing and cyclotron line confirmation in the SFXT IGR J16418-4532
papers.summary: Supergiant Fast X-ray Transients (SFXTs) show extreme X-ray variability on timescales of minutes to hours, driven by accretion processes that remain poorly understood. IGR J16418-4532 is an intermediate SFXT with detected X-ray pulsations and a candidate cyclotron line, making it a key system for probing neutron-star accretion and magnetic fields in this class. We analysed a 148 ks NuSTAR observation and archival RXTE observations, using epoch folding to search for pulsations while correcting photon arrival times for a range of trial $a_x \sin i$ values, and performed phase-averaged spectroscopy with several continuum models. We detect coherent pulsations at $P_{\rm spin} = 1208.67 \pm 0.04$ s (NuSTAR) and $1209.4178 \pm 0.0084$ s (RXTE/PCA). The pulse detection depends clearly on the assumed projected semi-major axis and is most significant for $a_x \sin i = 55.1 \pm 3.5$ lt-s (NuSTAR) and $51.3 \pm 2.6$ lt-s (RXTE/PCA). Sliding-window pulse profiles show the orbital delay in the uncorrected data, which is fully removed after orbital correction. The inferred orbital parameters constrain the companion mass and radius to $\sim$12-18 $M_\odot$ and $\sim$13-16 $R_\odot$. This is the first constraint on the binary mass function of an SFXT obtained from the orbital motion of the neutron star. The spectrum shows a robust cyclotron absorption line at $\sim$50 keV, independent of the continuum model, implying $B \approx 5 \times 10^{12}$ G. Optimising pulse detection with trial $a_x \sin i$ corrections, rather than modelling pulse arrival-time delays, offers a route to dynamical mass measurements in other SFXTs whose variable pulse profiles limit conventional timing techniques.

papers.title: A Model to Map Brown Dwarf Companions to White Dwarfs in Partial Secondary Eclipse
papers.summary: Eclipse mapping is a well-established technique for constraining the spatial emission of hot Jupiter exoplanets. Brown dwarfs in ultra-short orbits around white dwarfs are an analog to hot Jupiters that can only ever be eclipsed within a limited range of latitudes. We adapt the eigenmapping method to disentangle the signals from the ever- and never-occulted regions. The result of this signal separation is a super-position of map structures, yielding sharp boundaries at the occultation region. We introduce a model that penalizes the harmonic complexity of the model map with Tikhonov regularization, whose parameters are tuned to reproduce the fit quality of the eigenmapping model. We use JWST NIRSpec/PRISM full-orbit observations of the eclipsing WD 1202-024 system as a template to construct and run injection-recovery tests on simulated light curves, isolating both latitudinal structures as well as emission from a physically-realistic general circulation model (GCM). In the latter, the narrow equatorial jet driven by the BD's rapid rotation manifests as an eclipse depth asymmetry, which our model reproduces as a latitude-dependent phase offset. Such a model, however, is only statistically preferred at approximately $3 \times$ the signal-to-noise ratio of the JWST data. When fitting to the actual JWST data of WD 1202, the full-phase eigenbasis model is statistically preferred. However, the resulting model map of WD 1202 B does not resemble the GCM predictions, with a concentrated day-side hotspot at the sub-stellar point with an angular size $\approx 15^\circ$. Interpreting this result more carefully requires follow-up work to disentangle systematics from true emission signals. This model framework provides a means to detect emission features from these rare types of eclipses, and ultimately to test predictions of models of atmospheric circulation across hot Jupiters and their BD analogs.

papers.title: ASTRA: An Autonomous Framework for Physics-Validated Analysis and Hypothesis Generation in Astrophysics
papers.summary: We present ASTRA, an autonomous framework for physics-validated analysis and hypothesis generation in astrophysics without per-step human intervention. It integrates dimensional analysis, structural causal models, Bayesian evidence computation, and multi-wavelength data fusion in a single automated workflow. Five test cases on real observational data recover known results: Herschel filament scaling, Chandra Deep Field South cross-matching, SDSS galaxy correlations, Gaia causal inference, and Bayesian virial model selection. A sixth case runs unsupervised on synthetic galaxy data. The main sequence and mass-metallicity relation are recovered, and the outlier detector, with a false-discovery-rate threshold and no contamination parameter, recovers the blind injected fraction on ten sealed datasets (purity > 0.99) and flags nothing on the 3,000-galaxy sample. A knowledge-isolation ablation shows pattern detection and physical validation are invariant to removal of domain knowledge, which affects only interpretation. In a direct comparison, agentic-LLM and pure-ML baselines match the statistical fitting but not the physics-validation stage. They rarely derive the equilibrium benchmark, split evenly on the physical verdict, and adopt a supplied erroneous benchmark in all six trap runs, an astrophysics-specific fine-tuned model completes zero of six runs. On live SDSS DR16 data it flags 197 of 4,999 galaxies at a data-determined threshold, ranked extremes classifiable from withheld spectroscopy. These are recovery validations and capability demonstrations rather than discoveries, with hypothesis generation demonstrated qualitatively.

papers.title: The inner galaxy as a window on its early assembly: lessons from a cosmological Milky Way analogue
papers.summary: Characterising the assembly history of the inner Milky Way is a key goal of upcoming spectroscopic surveys, yet disentangling its overlapping stellar components remains challenging. We investigate the chemodynamics of the centre of a Milky Way analogue in the Auriga Superstars cosmological hydrodynamical simulation suite, focusing on a high-resolution halo (~ 800 M_sun star particles) with a realistic galactic bar and accretion history. We classify stars within the inner 4 kpc into proto-galaxy, subsequent in-situ, and accreted components to assess their distinguishability using kinematics, dynamics, ages, and metallicities. Stellar net rotation declines sharply between [Fe/H]=0 and [Fe/H]=-1, marking the transition from disc-like in-situ stars to the proto-galaxy. While significant chemical and dynamical overlaps complicate the search for structures in energy-angular momentum (E-Lz) space, metal-poor stars ([Fe/H]97%) sample of proto-galaxy stars. Conversely, the high-energy, metal-poor tail offers the best chance of detecting accreted debris. However, at high energies the inner accreted halo is dominated by low-mass systems (M_star ~ 10^7 - 10^9 M _sun), not the earliest massive mergers. Dynamically, few clues remain from early mergers, and early enrichment is rapid and similar across progenitors. In-situ contamination is an issue for [Fe/H]>-1 throughout E-Lz space. Overall, while accurate stellar ages and high-precision chemical abundances may help further constrain the Milky Way's history, we should be cautious when associating stars with individual merger events in the inner galaxy.

papers.title: Unveiling the nonthermal environments of NGC 3411 and NGC 5903 through new MeerKAT observations
papers.summary: Galaxy groups are key laboratories for investigating the interplay between active galactic nucleus (AGN) outbursts and the dynamical processes of the intra-group medium. We aim to characterize the morphology, spectral properties, and magnetic field structure of the diffuse nonthermal radio emission in two peculiar galaxy groups, NGC 3411 and NGC 5903, selected from an originally larger sample, in order to constrain its origin and its connection with the dynamics of the intra-group medium. We present new MeerKAT UHF- and L-band observations of the two groups, complemented by archival Chandra and XMM-Newton data already analyzed in previous works. In NGC 3411, we detect extended radio emission surrounding the central AGN over scales of ~70 kpc, and resolve previously undetected arc-shaped substructures on scales of ~20-30 kpc. This extended component exhibits a relatively uniform steep spectrum ($\alpha$ ~ -1.7). We discuss possible scenarios for its origin, including mini-halos, aged AGN plasma, weak shocks, and the possibility of a radio galaxy observed along the line of sight. In NGC 5903, MeerKAT reveals a complex filamentary morphology, including a previously unknown ring-like structure surrounding the central AGN. Spectral-index mapping shows localized flattening ($\alpha$ ~ -0.9) along the north arc, while polarization data reveal ordered magnetic fields and a patchy rotation measure distribution across the source. Together with the disturbed X-ray morphology, these results support a scenario in which fossil AGN plasma has been redistributed and locally reenergized by group-scale dynamical processes such as turbulence, shear, and weak compression. Our results demonstrate that galaxy groups can host a rich variety of nonthermal phenomena, whose properties can only be fully revealed through the combination of sensitive, high-resolution, and multifrequency radio observations.

papers.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
papers.summary: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

papers.title: Propulsion Systems for a Starshade Rendezvous Mission with the Habitable World Observatory
papers.summary: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints affect exo-Earth characterization with a starshade rendezvous mission for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)-like telescope at Sun-Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo simulations with EXOSIMS, we model a 60 m starshade for visible-band spectroscopy (500-1000 nm) and a 35 m starshade for near-ultraviolet characterization (250-550 nm). For the 60 m design, we compare AEPS Hall, NEXT ion, and Starlink-class Hall thrusters and examine sensitivity to propellant capacity, the fraction of each retargeting slew spent accelerating and decelerating, and on-orbit refueling. With 1000-3000 kg of initial propellant and no refueling, NEXT provides the highest characterization yield: 9-13% more characterizations than AEPS and 13-16% more than the Starlink-class option. Its higher specific impulse enables more retargeting slews per kilogram of propellant. With refueling, yields converge across thruster choices to about 120 cumulative characterizations over 10 years, while propulsion choice mainly affects the number of refueling events. For the 35 m starshade with AEPS, yields are less sensitive to fuel and are dominated by mission duration and geometric accessibility. Increasing the minimum solar keepout angle from 40 to 50 degrees has little effect on yield; increases from 50 to 65 degrees have a modest effect, while angles above 65 degrees rapidly reduce yield, with severe degradation near 80 degrees. These results distinguish fuel-limited and time- or keepout-limited regimes and guide propulsion selection, tank sizing, refueling policy, and keepout constraints for HWO starshade missions.

papers.title: Measuring masses of transiting Earth-like planets: first insights from the PLATO RV data challenge
papers.summary: The PLATO Stellar Variability Mitigation Working Group designed a radial-velocity (RV) data challenge to assess the precision and accuracy achievable on RV semi-amplitudes in the context of the future PLATO follow-up. Using Sun-as-a-star observations obtained with HARPS-N, we generated three multi-planet systems with realistic sampling, an effective signal-to-noise ratio of S/N ~ 450, an exposure time of 15 minutes, and a total of approximately 1000 observations. The resulting data set is publicly available and can serve as a benchmark for the community to test and compare RV analysis methods. Eight independent teams participated in the challenge, aiming to recover the semi-amplitudes of both transiting and non-transiting planets. A meta-analysis of the submitted results shows that, with current data analysis methods, HARPS-N-like stability and the observing strategy studied in this paper, achieving a precision on semi-amplitudes better than 10% for habitable-zone signals around a solar-type star is challenging, and is typically limited to planets with masses of approximately 8-10 Earth masses. This performance is expected to improve for K dwarfs, where planets down to approximately 2-5 Earth masses may be characterized at a similar level of precision. Finally, based on the results of this challenge and the occurrence of false positives, we derive an empirical detection threshold for RV surveys, which can be used to distinguish robust planetary detections from candidates.

papers.title: DUETS II - Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.summary: Red giants displaying solar-like oscillations allow precise stellar properties to be derived. Asteroseismic binaries (ABs), which are gravitationally bound systems where both stars show detectable oscillations, can provide constraints on the interior of two coeval stars, allowing us to model them jointly and potentially obtain constraints unavailable from either star individually. This makes ABs potential laboratories for calibrating stellar evolution theory. In this context, AB candidates (ABCs) are systems showing two oscillators, which are as of yet not confirmed as gravitationally bound. We aimed to confirm ABCs and other red giant binary candidates, as well as demonstrate the advantages of AB modeling inference. We obtained spectroscopic indicators of binarity for 60 oscillating red giants that have photometric (33 stars) and/or asteroseismic (38) indications of binarity. We confirm 12 of our 60 targets as spectroscopic binaries, 8 of which are ABs as well. Cross-matching with Gaia DR3 and APOGEE DR17, we identify a further 9 likely binaries, at least 6 of which are also ABCs. We then investigated the impact of simultaneously modeling the oscillation modes of both oscillators of an AB. We inferred stellar properties for; one binary of extra-Galactic origin containing one detectable red-giant-branch (RGB) oscillator; one AB with RGB oscillators; and two ABCs with RGB oscillators. We find that the mode frequencies of the two ABCs and the confirmed AB are well-described with a coeval modeling of the stellar components. We demonstrate that the simultaneous modeling of ABs with two RGB stars can be used to infer the stellar helium content down to $3\%$ precision, compared to $5\%$ when using only the brightest star. Finally, the metal-poor binary KIC2971380 hints for a need to correct the $\nu_{\rm max}$ scaling relation, supporting recent studies of extremely metal-poor oscillators.

papers.title: Testing Pre-main-sequence Evolutionary Models with Gaia and SPHEREx Observations of Canis Major North
papers.summary: Pre-main-sequence (PMS) evolutionary models can assign different ages across stellar mass within the same population. We use joint Gaia and SPHEREx spectral energy distributions to infer effective temperatures, radii, and luminosities for members of Canis Major North (CMaN), a nearby association with independent lithium and kinematic age constraints near 23 Myr. The SPHEREx fluxes agree with 2MASS and WISE photometry to 3--6\%, and we anchor the absolute flux scale to Gaia, 2MASS, and WISE. Using the revised temperatures, we obtain a lithium age of $22.4^{+2.8}_{-1.5}$ Myr. For a 29-star PMS sample, population-wide HR-diagram fits yield $20.5^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Myr for unspotted SPOTS models, consistent with the external constraints, $18.4^{+1.4}_{-1.3}$ and $18.7^{+1.3}_{-1.2}$ Myr for the Feiden nonmagnetic and BHAC15 models, and substantially older ages of $32.2^{+2.3}_{-2.1}$ and $55^{+5}_{-5}$ Myr for the Feiden magnetic and PARSEC models. No grid returns a temperature-independent age. The Feiden, SPOTS, and BHAC15 models assign older ages to stars above $4000$ K, whereas PARSEC assigns increasingly older ages toward lower temperatures. The intrinsic luminosity dispersion is also mass dependent, approximately $0.14$ dex below $3450$ K but $0.05$ dex at intermediate temperatures. At a fixed age of 23.0 Myr, a single SPOTS filling factor cannot reproduce the width of the low-temperature sequence, whereas the empirical filling-factor distribution of young stars overpredicts it. Spotted isochrones can enclose every cool member only at ages of 37--50 Myr, inconsistent with the lithium and kinematic ages.

papers.title: NOCTURNE. VI. Hour-timescale radio variability in early-stage active galactic nucleus SDSS J122844.81+501751.2
papers.summary: Recently, a sample of radio-weak active galactic nuclei (AGN) was discovered to exhibit extreme Jy-level radio flares at 37~GHz. The origin of these extraordinary flares remains unknown. All sources host low-mass supermassive black holes, and most of them can be classified as narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. We employed multiwavelength observations to investigate one of these sources, SDSS J122844.81+501751.2, during a period of high 37~GHz activity. Our data include radio observations from Mets\"ahovi Radio Observatory (MRO) at 37~GHz, OVRO at 15~GHz, and JVLA at 15, 22, and 33~GHz, as well as optical, UV, and X-ray observations from \textit{Swift}/XRT and UVOT. We studied the variability of the multiwavelength light curves (LC) using statistical tests, as well as derived the $e$-folding timescales of the flares. Utilising the timescales and the observed flare properties, we estimated the variability brightness temperatures and Doppler factors associated with the flares. Most individual LCs do not show statistically significant variability, which is likely due to the low number of measurements. The shortest timescale we estimated is only 1.1~hours, measured between MRO 37~GHz and JVLA 33~GHz detections. This is the fastest intrinsic radio variability reported in an AGN so far. This yielded an extreme variability brightness temperature of $T_\mathrm{B}$ = 4.20 $~\times$ 10$^{18}$~K and a variability Doppler factor of 438. We discuss magnetic eruptions near the black hole as a possible explanation for the extreme radio flares, and show that both incoherent and coherent processes can produce flares at these timescales. These flares challenge our current understanding of AGN radio variability. Whereas magnetic eruptions offer a viable explanation for the flares, more observations, preferably broadband and including polarisation, will be required to confirm their origin. (abridged)

papers.title: Impact of Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus Debris on Milky Way Escape-velocity Estimates in TNG50
papers.summary: The escape velocity is a key probe of the Milky Way (MW) potential, but standard estimates can be biased by unrelaxed substructures. Using MW analogs from the TNG50 cosmological simulation, we investigate the impact of the dominant, highly radial Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) debris on escape-velocity measurements. We introduce an adaptive selection strategy that balances statistical reliability with sample size to identify the power-law decline regime of the local halo velocity distribution. Applying this strategy to 16 MW analogs with prominent GSE-like structures and continuous high-velocity tails, we find that retaining GSE-like stars yields a systematic underestimate, with a recovery fraction of $97.5^{+2.1}_{-2.9}\%$, while removing GSE-like stars alone increases the recovery fraction to $99.4^{+2.1}_{-2.5}\%$. The $\sim 2\%$ underestimation of the escape velocity corresponds to an $\sim 6\%$ underestimation of the total mass. This improvement persists in LAMOST-like magnitude and footprint selection. GSE-like debris is therefore a key contributor to the systematic underestimation of escape-velocity measurements, with direct implications for the inferred MW mass.

papers.title: Reconstruction of very inclined air showers with radio data and application to the first GRANDProto300 cosmic-ray candidates
papers.summary: Radio detection of very inclined extensive air showers (EAS) offers a promising way to study ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and neutrinos above $10^{17}$ eV. We present a method to reconstruct the arrival direction and energy of EAS with zenith angles above $60^\circ$, applicable in principle to upward-going neutrino-induced showers. The approach combines a point-source-like description of the radio wavefront with the Angular Distribution Function (ADF), a phenomenological model describing the angular pattern of electric field amplitudes in the 50-200 MHz band. On realistic cosmic-ray simulations, we achieve better than $0.07^\circ$ resolution on arrival direction and ~15\% on primary energy. Applied directly to voltage traces, this method allows efficient cosmic-ray selection with accurate direction reconstruction and first-order energy estimation. We illustrate the method on the first cosmic-ray candidates detected by the GRANDProto300 prototype of GRAND, validating its detection principle and paving the way for high-precision neutrino searches.
