papers.title: JWST/MIRI Observations of Amorphous Silicates in Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
papers.summary: We present JWST/MIRI Low Resolution Spectroscopy (LRS) of 3I/ATLAS obtained post-perihelion at a heliocentric distance of 2.21 au. Our spectrum contains a prominent 10 micron silicate emission feature with a broad, smooth shape that is distinct from those commonly observed in Solar System comets. We model the spectrum using thermal emission from amorphous carbon, amorphous olivine, and amorphous pyroxene grains. Our models strongly favor a pyroxene-dominated, amorphous silicate composition and show a degeneracy between silicate grain size and the relative abundance of silicate and carbon dust. Across a set of representative models, the best-fitting crystalline abundance is zero, and we place an upper limit of 5.3% on the crystalline fraction of the silicates. We identify an emission feature near 6.83 microns that is consistent with aliphatic C-H-bearing material. The overwhelmingly amorphous silicate composition supports previous work that measured unusual volatile and isotopic composition in suggesting that the material incorporated into the object experienced little thermal processing and preserves information about the conditions in which this interstellar planetesimal formed.

papers.title: Little Red Dots with Broad H$\beta$ Lines Reveal the Black Hole Mass Function at 7<z<9.5
papers.summary: We present a systematic search for broad H$\beta$ emission at $7<z<9.5$ in 21,770 JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra drawn from four blank fields and six lensing clusters with photometry spanning 1942 arcmin$^2$. We find a sample of 20 sources with statistically significant broad-H$\beta$ emission, including 13 new sources. Our entire sample has colors and morphologies consistent with little red dots (LRDs), compared to only 37\% of broad-line emitters at $3.5<z<6$. Interpreting the broad-lines as indicators of Broad-line Active Galactic Nuclei (BLAGN), we infer black hole masses of $4.2\times10^{6}-2.1\times10^{8}$\,$M_{\odot}$. We calculate completeness corrections and construct the black hole mass function at $z\sim8$. The normalization of the black hole mass function rises by $\approx1.0$~dex from $z\sim8-5$, consistent with average black hole growth at $f_{\textrm{Edd}}\approx0.1$. Comparing with cosmological simulations, the $z\sim8$ black hole mass function requires heavy ($10^5$\,$M_{\odot}$) seeds or super-Eddington accretion onto light or intermediate mass seeds to match its normalization. Finally, we infer bolometric luminosities for the sample and construct a bolometric luminosity function. We integrate over this luminosity function to derive a black hole accretion density (BHAD) of $4.8^{+5.8}_{-2.6}\times10^{-7}~M_{\odot}~\textrm{yr}^{-1}~\textrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, showing broad agreement with previous photometric work, but disagreement with previous X-ray models, reinforcing the idea that BLAGN are more common in the early universe than previously expected.

papers.title: Effects of Dust in Electron-Capture Supernovae: Difficulty in Explaining Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients
papers.summary: The progenitors of intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs) spanning the luminosity gap between novae and supernovae are under debate, and electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) have been proposed as a strong candidate. ECSNe from super asymptotic giant branch (super-AGB) stars have been theoretically predicted to be much brighter than ILRTs, but attenuation by dusty winds of their super-AGB progenitors may ease this tension. Here we construct a semi-analytical framework for calculating the light curves of ECSNe with dust attenuation and re-emission, by combining recent ECSN light curve predictions with a model for dust physics. Even by varying both the wind mass-loss rate and the ECSN model parameters, we find it challenging to simultaneously fit the light curve and color evolution of ILRTs. This poses a potential challenge to the standard models of ECSNe for explaining ILRTs. For explaining ILRTs, we propose either the existence of a population of ECSNe with much lower explosion energies ($\sim$10$^{48}$-$10^{49}$ erg) and dimmer plateaus, or alternative model(s) to ECSNe that realize such low explosion energies.

papers.title: The UKIRT M33 Monitoring Project - VII. A 15-year K-band photometric catalogue of long-period variable stars in the central kiloparsec of M33
papers.summary: We present a homogenised K-band photometric catalogue for the central ${\approx}12$ arcmin$^2$ (${\approx}0.9$ kpc$^2$) of the Triangulum spiral galaxy M33, combining four independent PSF-based near-infrared datasets obtained with UKIRT between 2003 and 2018. These comprise the 2003-2007 UIST multi-epoch monitoring survey, the 2005 UFTI K-band mosaic (for which we present new PSF photometry), new WFCAM PSF reductions for the four central tiles, and a single K-band epoch from the 2018 UKIRT Hemisphere Survey (UHS DR3). Cross-matching all four catalogues and retaining stars detected in at least two of them yields 847 unique stars comprising 21,085 valid K-band measurements spanning a baseline of 15.11 yr. Photometric homogenisation onto the 2MASS/Vega system via 82 low-scatter calibration stars removes systematic inter-dataset offsets of up to 0.22 mag. Of the 847 monitored stars, 771 (91 per cent) are classified as variable ($\sigma_{\rm rms} > 0.10$ mag), including 385 high-amplitude variables ($A_K \geq 1.0$ mag): prime Mira-type long-period variable candidates for period determination. Cross-matching with archival Spitzer IRAC photometry yields 156 matched stars, of which 120 satisfy $\langle K\rangle - [3.6] > 0.5$ mag, identifying dust-enshrouded AGB candidates inaccessible to all-sky optical surveys. This catalogue constitutes the most extensive near-infrared photometric baseline assembled for AGB stars in any spiral galaxy beyond the Milky Way, providing the photometric foundation for the period-luminosity analysis and star-formation-history reconstruction in the companion Paper VIII. The full catalogue is available at the Centre de Donn\'{e}es astronomiques de Strasbourg (CDS).

papers.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
papers.summary: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. This cost becomes prohibitive for megapixel-scale frames with N_f~100. Although dynamic programming can reduce the computational complexity by a factor of N_f, it requires a prohibitive memory of O(N_x N_y N_f^2), unsuitable for large-format detectors. This article presents a novel algorithm to achieve the computational efficiency of dynamic programming while maintaining a memory footprint of just O(N_x N_y N_f) by slightly approximating the computation of frame shifts for alignment. By expressing the shift as a sum of terms proportional to the digits frame index in binary and rounding up each of these terms, frames can be integrated efficiently by hierarchically adding intermediate sums that are shared across different velocities with the same higher bits in binary. The approximation only introduces a small tracking error that increases logarithmically with the number of frames. This advancement enables synthetic tracking to be executed with high energy efficiency, making it practical for deployment on standard workstations rather than requiring high-performance computing infrastructure such as GPU servers or CPU clusters.

papers.title: A self-supervised machine learning approach to identify instrumental systematics in 21cm Cosmology
papers.summary: The primordial sound waves in the baryon-photon plasma are imprinted on the large-scale galaxy distribution as Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), serving as a cosmological standard ruler to constrain dark energy and the Hubble parameter. The upcoming 21cm intensity-mapping arrays are designed to map the 21cm emission across large volumes and measure the BAO scale. However, radio interferometers suffer from instrumental systematics that can hinder detection of the cosmological 21cm signal by leaking bright foregrounds into the signal-dominated modes. This work aims to demonstrate that a self-supervised model can predict the instrument systematic state (here, the amplitude of a spectral ripple in the beam width) in interferometric visibilities and potentially disentangle the instrument from the sky without a forward model. Based on the fact that an instrument stays the same as the sky rotates in a drift-scan observation, and that the same sky is observed under different instrument states, we train a convolutional autoencoder to compress the information in the simulated visibilities and separate this information into instrument-only and sky-only latent vectors. The result shows excellent prediction of the unknown instrument systematic for 15 held-out instrument states with $R^2 = 0.9975$ with a linear probe, against $R^2 = -3.55$ for a random-encoder baseline. The instrument-latent carries no detectable sky signal, as measured with a total-power sky proxy, for any held-out test data. The sky-latent vector and instrument-latent vector show partial separation but not complete disentanglement, identifying sky-latent purity as the primary open problem. The results show the ability of the model to recognize the systematic and show a promising path towards an ML-based foreground cleaning pipeline. Full instrument-sky disentanglement constitutes the natural next step.

papers.title: Cosmological Constraints on Interacting Dark Matter with SPT-3G D1
papers.summary: Models of the dark sector in which the dark matter participates in nontrivial interactions can create detectable signatures in cosmological observables, providing non-terrestrial means of probing the nature of dark matter. In this work, we test dark matter-baryon scattering, dark matter-dark radiation interactions, and dark matter annihilation using measurements of the CMB and BAO. We leverage the latest SPT-3G D1 CMB measurements of the primary anisotropies, alongside the D1 MUSE lensing data, to set up-to-date bounds on these models. From the combination of Planck, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G D1 data, we constrain the velocity-independent dark matter-baryon scattering cross-section to $\sigma_\mathrm{DM-b} < 4.6\times10^{-26}~\mathrm{cm^2}$, the dark matter-dark radiation momentum transfer rate to $\Gamma_\mathrm{0,nadm}<5.2\times10^{-8}\,\text{Mpc}^{-1}$, and the effective dark matter annihilation parameter, quantifying the fractional thermally averaged cross-section, to $p_\mathrm{ann}<3.7\times10^{-28}~\mathrm{cm^3/s/GeV}$, all at the 95% confidence level. The improved sensitivity to the first two models is in particular driven by the precision measurements of CMB lensing at small scales provided by SPT-3G D1 MUSE lensing data. For annihilating dark matter, due to the degeneracy of the effect with the optical depth to reionization, we observe a non-trivial relationship between the upper bound on $p_\mathrm{ann}$ and the large-scale polarization information. When combining CMB data with the latest measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), upper bounds on extended model parameters can appear to tighten as the model space attempts to accommodate the known discrepancy between these data. Future CMB and BAO measurements will provide better clarity on reconciling this discrepancy and enhance our ability to test dark matter interactions.

papers.title: The Role of Star Formation and Morphology in the Mass-Metallicity Relation of Galaxies at Cosmic Noon
papers.summary: We investigate the dependence of the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) on star formation and galaxy morphology at 1.71000 galaxies. The observations span >85 arcmin^2 from the pure-parallel PASSAGE and OutThere surveys. We derive gas-phase metallicities using a Bayesian framework that combines multiple strong emission-line ratios calibrated against direct auroral-line metallicity measurements from JWST. We constrain stellar masses, star formation rates (SFRs), and morphological properties using ancillary HST and JWST imaging. We stack spectra by stellar mass to constrain the MZR over log(M*/M)~6.5-11, and find that it is well described by a second-order polynomial, with a steep low-mass slope and metallicities<10% solar at log(M*/M)<7.5. Additional stacking by SFR and morphology reveals strong evidence for a fundamental metallicity relation (FMR). Specifically, at log(M*/M)<9.5, galaxies with lower SFRs are more metal-rich than those with higher SFRs at fixed mass. At log(M*/M)<9.5, we find that larger galaxies, and those having lower SFR surface densities, bulges, and/or spiral features are significantly metal rich relative to their smaller, higher SFR surface density, bulge-less, and/or non-spiral counterparts. These results suggest the secondary dependencies of the MZR reflect variations in the baryon cycle, such that recent metal-poor gas accretion drives concentrated star formation and metallicity dilution, while structurally developed galaxies retain more chemically enriched gas reservoirs.

papers.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
papers.summary: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We use population constraints based on data from the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0), as well as constraints from the O3 search for intermediate-mass black hole binaries, to forecast the number and masses of binary black holes detectable by LISA. Using the released GWTC-5.0 population posterior, we obtain $6.6^{+5.5}_{-2.2}$ expected detections with signal-to-noise ratio $>8$ in 4 years (median and $90\%$ credible interval). The alternative population models we consider use a broken power law with two or three Gaussian peaks for either the primary-mass distribution or a common mass distribution for both black holes. For the three-peak model with the common mass distribution, extrapolating from $300$ to $1000M_\odot$ roughly doubles the median expected number of LISA detections to $\sim14$. The upper end of its $90\%$ credible interval rises from tens to thousands of expected detections, although approximations may limit the reliability of the most extreme counts. For the reference GWTC-5.0 population, $39^{+22}_{-11}\%$ of the binaries detectable by LISA merge during the mission or within $10$ years after its end and are potential multiband sources. Essentially all of these mergers would be detectable by a reference Cosmic Explorer configuration if it is operating at merger. Ground-based measurements of the high-mass population can therefore inform both LISA forecasts and the prospects for observing the same binaries through inspiral and merger.

papers.title: Galactic Dynamics Drives Cyclic Star Formation in Dipole Dwarf Galaxies
papers.summary: Dwarf galaxies are dark matter-dominated systems that are sensitive to feedback and display bursty star formation histories. This makes them ideal probes of the processes that regulate star formation. This work investigates the timescales of star formation rate (SFR) variability in isolated dwarf galaxies using high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of $50$ dwarf galaxies drawn from the Marvelous Massive Dwarfs and Extended Marvelous Dwarfs simulation suites ($7.3 <$ \lmstar $< 9.1$). We measure star formation histories in $10$ Myr bins and characterize their variability with power spectral densities (PSDs). At the population level, the PSDs of both disk and non-disk galaxies follow a broken power-law, with a break timescale near $100$ Myr. Individually, our galaxies show both smooth and bursty star formation. A subset of disk galaxies show quasi-periodic SFR oscillations about their mean, which we refer to as cyclic star formation. The dominant timescale of these oscillations scales linearly with half-light radius and is approximated by the orbital period at that radius. Cyclic galaxies have Magellanic Spiral (Sm) morphologies and host lopsided dipole gas disks. In these systems, the bulk of the gas in the lopsided disk moves between its maximum and minimum distance from the galactic center, compressing the star-forming gas once per radial orbit and driving the SFR cycle. Cyclic star formation adds a narrow Lorentzian component to the PSD, peaked at radial orbital frequency of the disk ($\sim 200-500$ Myr), which is comparable to burst timescales inferred from observations.

papers.title: What shapes the bright end of the UV luminosity function? Stellar mass, star-formation variability, and dust in JADES
papers.summary: JWST surveys find more UV-bright galaxies at $z>10$ than galaxy-formation models predict, but the roles of recent star formation, stellar mass and dust remain uncertain. We analyse 1365 spectroscopically confirmed JADES galaxies at $3\leq z\leq9$, fitting NIRCam photometry and NIRSpec emission lines with \ceri. Our model includes flexible star-formation histories (SFHs) under three priors, two-component dust attenuation and nebular emission. We account for spectroscopic selection through population reweighting and assess the reliability of inferred trends. At $z=3$--5, rising SFHs are more common in low-mass galaxies, whereas most galaxies above $10^{9.5}\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ have declining SFHs. The apparent increase in rising fractions with redshift cannot be distinguished from the adopted SFH prior alone. At fixed stellar mass, recent star formation is the strongest predictor of UV brightness. UV-brighter galaxies have higher recent SFRs, younger stellar populations and less attenuation at fixed SFR. Below $10^9\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, they are also more likely to have rising SFHs, with odds increasing by up to a factor of 2.3 per magnitude brighter, although the strongest trend requires caution. In contrast, galaxies with $M_{\mathrm{UV}}<-20$ at $z=3$--5 are predominantly massive, and approximately half have declining SFHs. Dust partly offsets burst-driven UV brightening: attenuation increases with recent SFR and declines gradually after the inferred SFR peak. In model sensitivity tests, dust has the largest effect on bright-end counts, whereas removing galaxy-to-galaxy SFH scatter changes them by at most 0.17~dex. Thus, bursts can make low-mass galaxies unusually UV-bright for their mass, while the absolute bright end of the UVLF is primarily shaped by stellar mass and dust attenuation.

papers.title: Measuring the magnetization profiles of galaxy groups and clusters
papers.summary: Magnetic fields are vital in determining the physical conditions of baryons in massive halos. They are, however, notoriously difficult to observe. This impacts problems from our understanding of galaxy formation, to the observed deficit in the amplitude of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum that affects cosmological inferences. Although Faraday rotation measures (RMs) offer a direct probe of magnetic fields, it weights magnetic fields by the free-electron density. Several probes of free electrons, including fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (DMs) and kinematic SZ (kSZ) effect, are now maturing into precision tools. We combine RM$^2$ stacks from SPICE-RACS around DESI galaxy groups and ROSAT clusters with optical depth profiles constrained jointly by the FRB DM-redshift relation and the kSZ effect, and obtain 95% upper limits on the rms line-of-sight magnetic field of $0.31$ ($>11$) in groups (clusters). Although current constraints are only limits, we forecast a first detection with larger datasets from the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA). We present the first forecast of the DSA RM grid density ($\sim365$ RMs deg$^{-2}$), which when combined with 10$^4$ FRBs would measure the field in groups to $3$-$13\%$ precision, compared to current constraints of $38$-$75\%$. Although the interpretation of current measurements remains challenging owing to depolarization along turbulent halo sightlines and the unknown coherence length, larger samples and DSA/Square Kilometer Array observations may resolve these uncertainties by measuring polarization-fraction profiles and the RM structure function using extended radio sources, respectively.

papers.title: The Spatially-Resolved Recent Star Formation History of the M81 Disk
papers.summary: The nearby M81 galaxy---a tidally interacting $L^*$ spiral disk---offers a unique perspective on the interplay of secular and external processes in shaping galaxy properties. We present the most detailed, panoramic map of M81's stellar populations to date, using archival Hubble Space Telescope ACS photometry from the ANGST survey spanning the full optical extent of its disk. From color-magnitude diagram fitting, we recover spatially-resolved star formation histories (SFHs) over the last $\sim180\,$Myr. M81's global SFH is remarkably steady in the last $\sim180\,$Myr with slight enhancements seen $\lesssim15\,$Myr ago. The average SFR surface density rises toward the center before falling off within the innermost $\sim4\,$kpc. The disk is also notably lopsided, with the eastern half having formed $\sim50\%$ more stars than the western half over the same area---a trend missed by FUV-based SFR indicators due to dust systematics. Finally, the long-term SFHs of both M81 and M82 point to a pericenter passage $\sim1\,$Gyr ago. By identifying M81-M82 analogs in the TNG50 cosmological simulation, we rule out the more recent pericenter times of $150-220\,$Myr predicted by some works, as such passages are inconsistent with M81's undisturbed SFH over the last $\sim180\,$Myr. With this work, M81 becomes only the third $L^*$ spiral---after M31 and NGC 6946---to have its SFH spatially resolved across large areas of its disk.

papers.title: Improving cosmological distance measurements at high redshift using Lyman-Alpha forest BAO reconstruction
papers.summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) measures baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the Lyman-$\alpha$ (Lyman-alpha) forest and provides a robust probe of the expansion history in the matter-dominated era. Yet, non-linear structure formation broadens and shifts the BAO peak. To undo these effects, we extend standard Zel'dovich reconstruction, routinely applied to galaxy surveys, to the Lyman-alpha forest. We validate our methodology on large-volume idealized Lyman-alpha forest mocks painted on top of the \textsc{AbacusSummit} $N$-body simulations, using linear control variates to suppress sample variance and thereby reduce the error bars by a factor of up to $\approx \sqrt{50}$. In fully sampled periodic boxes, reconstruction halves the radial BAO damping scale and reduces the uncertainties on the radial ($\apar$) and transverse ($\aperp$) scaling parameters by $\approx25\%$ and $\approx15\%$, respectively. It also reduces the non-linear shift from $\Delta\apar=+0.3\%$ to $+0.10\pm0.07\%$, while $\aperp$ remains unbiased. To make this approach readily applicable to observational data, we demonstrate the impact of a survey mask with a DESI-like density of $50\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. For this mask, we compare two approaches to estimate the displacement field: either directly from the Lyman-alpha forest or using an external tracer with a number density of $\bar n \simeq 10^{-3}\,h^3\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, such as Lyman-break galaxies and Lyman-$\alpha$ emitters---both key targets for DESI-II. Both approaches give comparable gains and reduce the uncertainties on $\apar$ and $\aperp$ by $\approx 27\%$ and $\approx 10\%$, respectively, with mild improvements for futuristic high-density surveys with $160\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. Correspondingly, the figure of merit improves by factors of $1.66$ for fully sampled boxes, $1.65$ for a DESI-like, and $1.76$ for a high-density survey.

papers.title: Planetesimal Delivery to Giant Planet Circumplanetary Disks: Bulk Ice Enrichment and an Ice-rich Iapetus
papers.summary: The regular satellites of Jupiter and Saturn are substantially enriched in ice relative to the rock-rich solids of the outer Solar System. In addition, the satellites interior to Titan and distant Iapetus are icier than Titan itself. Collisional processes and subsequent migration can readily alter compositions deep in the planetary potential well, but producing a distant, ice-rich satellite with Iapetus's radius of about 700 km is a challenge \citep{mosqueira2026a}. We show that differential ablation and capture of icy and rocky fragments from differentiated outer Solar System bodies can explain the bulk Jovian and Kronian satellite ice enrichment and supply the substantial ice-rich inventory needed for Iapetus. For 1\,m--1\,km fragments with the canonical size-distribution index \(p=3.5\) and a source containing 30\% ice by mass, the fixed radial distance Saturn calculation deposits material with ice fractions of 0.66 (delivery of vapor-only rock) or 0.50 (with retained rock melt) at 20 Saturn radii and nearly pure ice at 60 Saturn radii. Following three-dimensional trajectories over repeated passages through the pressure-supported gas gives ice fractions of about 0.4 near 20 Saturn radii and 0.9 near 60 Saturn radii. The matching Jupiter calculation yields a similar bulk ice enrichment, with a corresponding compositional gradient across the Galilean satellite region. These delivery profiles supply ice-enriched material for satellite formation. Yet satellitesimal inward migration subsequently modifies the material incorporated into satellites and thus alters their bulk compositions. We briefly discuss the implications for the PDS~70 planetary system.

papers.title: Axions from Betelgeuse: Probing Axion Couplings with $^{23}\rm{Na}$ and $^{55}\rm{Mn}$
papers.summary: We investigate axion-like particle (ALP) production in the interior of Betelgeuse via nuclear de-excitation of thermally populated excited states of $^{23}$Na and $^{55}$Mn. As these ALPs propagate to Earth, they can produce photons either through their conversion in the Galactic magnetic field or through their decay. Using INTEGRAL-ISGRI and NuSTAR observations, we search for these photon signals, find no significant excess, and derive 95% CL exclusion limits on the ALP couplings. For magnetic-field conversion of ALPs, the $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ ($^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$) line observed with INTEGRAL-ISGRI constrains $|g_{a\gamma}g_{ap}| < 4.1\times10^{-21}$ ($6.9\times10^{-19}$) $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a < 10^{-10} \mathrm{eV}$. For ALP decays, the $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ ($^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$) line observed with INTEGRAL-ISGRI (NuSTAR) constrains $|g_{a\gamma}g_{ap}|$ down to $3.0\times10^{-22}$ ($2.9\times10^{-19}$) $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at $m_a \simeq 400$ ($83$) keV, weakening in both cases as $m_a^{-3/2}$ for lower ALP masses, and as $m_a^{-2}$ for $^{23}$Na below $m_a \sim 1$ keV, with sensitivity extending to $m_a \simeq 440.2$ ($124$) keV. Although our $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$-based limits are the strongest for both channels, their larger transition energy makes them more sensitive to the precise evolutionary stage of Betelgeuse, whereas the $^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$-based limits are considerably more robust against such uncertainties.

papers.title: Fresh Look at Shift Symmetric Modified Gravity
papers.summary: Shift symmetric Horndeski gravity can be a simple, well posed theory with protection against quantum corrections. Overturning conventional thought that such a theory cannot cross the phantom divide ($w=-1$) we present both analytic and numerical proof that it can. We carry out a detailed dynamical systems analysis showing the evolution of ghost free and stable regions within the model family, identify the fixed point and dynamical attractor structure, and derive the interaction of the $w=-1$ curve with these phase space structures. This reveals two mechanisms for cosmologies crossing the phantom divide while preserving shift symmetry.

papers.title: A gaussian-process reconstruction of gravitational-wave friction from dark standard sirens
papers.summary: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. We reconstruct its redshift dependence, encoded in the friction function $\alpha_M(z)$, with a Gaussian process (GP) and derive the corresponding GW-to-EM luminosity-distance ratio $\Xi(z)$ by integration, explicitly retaining the relation between the local friction modification and its accumulated effect on the observed distance, while enforcing a monotonic and invertible GW luminosity distance. We apply the method to the GWTC-5.0 catalog, jointly inferring the source population, modified propagation, and background cosmological parameters. We find no evidence for departures from GR, with $\alpha_M=0$ and $\Xi=1$ consistent with the posterior over the redshift range probed by the catalog. The result is stable under variations of the GP kernel, smoothness and amplitude priors, resolution prescription, and likelihood treatment. We further introduce function-space diagnostics for comparing flexible and parametric reconstructions, including prior calibration, prior-to-posterior contraction, common summaries of propagation-population degeneracies, and principal-component analysis. These tools make explicit which features are informed by the data and which are imposed by the function-space prior, providing a framework for interpretable non-parametric tests of gravitational-wave propagation.

papers.title: On the Interpretation of Tests of the Horizon Area Law
papers.summary: This Letter investigates gravitational-wave tests of the horizon area law. Although they provide a striking consistency check of general relativity (GR), these tests rely on models that assume GR, making their interpretation inherently model dependent. We show with a specific example---simulations of merging boson stars---that exotic compact objects can mimic merging black holes and pass an area-law test at a confidence as high as $\sim 92\%$ despite not even having event horizons.

papers.title: When Scatter Plots Hide the Data: Diagnosing Ties and Choosing the Right Display in R
papers.summary: Scatter plots draw one mark per observation, so observations that share a location are hidden. In a two-item Likert survey of 2,757 respondents, 98.7% of the data lie under other points and the plot shows only 36 dots. The density-distribution sunflower plot of Dupont and Plummer addresses this by drawing raw points in sparse regions and sunflowers, whose petals count observations, in dense ones. It is not available in R, and its single petal weight for dense cells fails when cell counts span more than an order of magnitude: small dense cells collapse to one petal, and the count a reader decodes can be wrong by 150% or more. We propose geometric petal tiers, in which each cell uses the smallest weight among 1, b, b2, . . . observations per petal that keeps its flower within P petals. Every flower then has between about P/b and P petals, and the relative error of every decoded count is below b/(2P), 17.9% at the defaults b = 5 and P = 14. We also define tie diagnostics and decision rules that use them to choose between an ordinary scatter plot, jitter or transparency, a classic sunflower plot and geometric tiers. Both are implemented in the ggplot2 extension ggsunflower. We illustrate the methods on survey, automotive, historical and large commercial data, and in a simulation over 35 conditions geometric tiers keep the worst-cell error at or below 14% where a single weight reaches a median of 251%.

papers.title: Primordial black holes from a type-IIB/F theory inflaton potential
papers.summary: We study the possibility of the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs) using an inflaton potential constructed by stabilizing all K\"{a}hler moduli employing both the perturbative and non-perturbative corrections in the large volume scenario in type-IIB/F string theory. We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the K\"{a}hler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. The effective correction in the moduli space is made by introducing a localised Gaussian bump, which induces an ultra-slow-roll feature in the inflaton potential during the early cosmological inflation. The evolution of the amplitude of the curvature power spectrum is solved numerically by using the Mukhanov-Sasaki equation, with Bunch-Davies initial conditions. The inclusion of the Gaussian bump produces a sustainable enhancement in the amplitude of curvature power spectra around $k\sim 1.12 \times 10^{9} Mpc^{-1}$ for the formation of PBHs. The abundance of PBHs ($f_{PBH}$) is calculated using the Press-Schechter formalism for different values of critical density contrast and presented in the background of contemporary $f_{PBH}$ bounds and checked for viability with existing microlensing bounds, corresponding to a mass value $10^{-6}M_\odot$ for $\delta$ threshold value $\delta_c=0.439$. The Hawking temperature and evaporation time are also determined for these black holes and found to be of the order of $2.78\times 10^{-15}$ GeV and $8.5\times10^{38}$ Gyr, respectively. The enhancement of curvature power spectra lies in the sensitivity region of the SKA observations, suggesting an indication that scalar-induced gravity waves may be probed in future observations.

papers.title: Quantum Annealing for Gamma-ray Source Detection and Localization with AGILE Data
papers.summary: The detection and localization of gamma-ray sources via maximum-likelihood analysis is a complex parameter optimization problem. We address this challenge using quantum annealing, a computational approach that solves optimization tasks by encoding them into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian. Specifically, we apply this method to observations from AGILE's Gamma-Ray Imaging Detector (GRID) in the 30 MeV-50 GeV band. We reformulated the standard analysis as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. We tested this method on a set of AGILE observations generated with AGILEpy, solving the QUBO with simulated quantum annealing. The method reproduces the classical flux and position estimates within their statistical uncertainty and identifies the correct grid node among the candidate positions in 97% of the maps. These promising results demonstrate that quantum annealing could be used in this optimization problem, laying the ground for its deployment on actual quantum annealers.

papers.title: Quasinormal Ringing of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by a King Dark Matter Halo: Higher-Order WKB Analysis
papers.summary: We study scalar and electromagnetic perturbations of a Schwarzschild black hole (BH) surrounded by a dark matter halo described by the King density profile. The lapse function can be expressed as $1-2[M+M_{\rm DM}(r)]/r$, where $M_{\rm DM}(r)$ is the halo mass enclosed within radius $r$; thus, the halo affects the geometry through its enclosed-mass function. We compute the quasinormal frequencies using the sixth-order WKB method and its Pad\'e-improved version. Rewriting the lapse function in terms of the inverse hyperbolic sine avoids the severe numerical cancellations that arise when evaluating its high-order derivatives. For the configurations examined, the fundamental frequencies agree with those extracted from time-domain evolution to within $0.2\%$.The halo lowers both the oscillation frequency and the damping rate. The change of the real part is almost entirely accounted for by the halo mass enclosed by the photon sphere, and the additional decrease of the damping rate follows the ratio of the Lyapunov exponent to the angular frequency of the circular null orbit. Since part of the halo lies inside the horizon in this metric, we also place the halo outside the BH by means of an Einstein cluster. The frequencies then decrease by a similar amount, but the real part follows the Schwarzschild value multiplied by the gravitational redshift factor of the halo. A jump in the density at the inner edge of the halo scatters the waves and changes the damping rate by up to about $9\%$. For a continuous density profile, deviations from the redshift relation remain below about $1.5\%$ for $r_{\rm in}=3M$ and below about $0.5\%$ for the cases with $r_{\rm in}\geq4M$. No unstable modes are found within the perturbation sectors and parameter configurations examined.

papers.title: Effects of Short-Range Correlations on Quarkyonic Matter
papers.summary: In this work, we focus on investigating the impact of the short-range correlations on the properties of quarkyonic matter. These correlations induce the scattering of nucleons to momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, thereby altering the momentum-space occupation distribution that underlies the quarkyonic framework. In particular, we examine to what extent the emergence of a high-momentum tail, due to the short-range nucleon-nucleon correlations, in the momentum distribution, for momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, affects the fundamental properties of quarkyonic matter, such as the energy density, pressure, and speed of sound, among others. In fact, at high densities, the behavior of the momentum distribution has been established, both experimentally and theoretically, to follow a characteristic $\sim 1/k^4$ dependence at large momenta. To the best of our knowledge, this effect on quarkyonic matter has not yet been systematically investigated. Moreover, this experimentally confirmed feature of the momentum distribution suggests that heavy-ion collisions may probe quarkyonic matter, underscoring the importance of incorporating short-range correlations into a complete quarkyonic model.

papers.title: Accretion Flow Properties of MAXI J1834-021 during Its Multi-peaked Outburst in 2023
papers.summary: The Galactic transient black hole candidate MAXI J1834-021 exhibited `faint' outburst activity for approximately $10$ months following its discovery on February 5, 2023. We study the evolution of both the temporal (hard and soft band photon count rates, hardness ratios, and QPO frequencies) and spectral properties of the source using NICER data between March 7 and October 4, 2023. The outburst profile and the nature of QPOs suggest that the source underwent a rebrightening following the primary episode of the outburst. A monotonic evolution of low-frequency QPOs from higher to lower frequencies is observed during the primary episode. Both phenomenological (diskbb plus powerlaw) and physical (Two Component Advective Flow) model fitted spectral studies suggest that during the entire epoch, the source remained in harder spectral states, with a clear dominance of nonthermal emissions from the `hot' Compton cloud. Based on the evolution of the spectral and temporal properties, the 2023 outburst activity of MAXI J1834-021 can be classified as a `failed' outburst, as no softer spectral states are observed. The spectral analysis with the TCAF model also gives an estimate of the source mass as $12.4\pm1.7~M_\odot$.

papers.title: Sym-EFT: Accelerating Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure with Symbolic Regression
papers.summary: We present an emulator suite for the one- and two-loop cold dark matter power spectrum from the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structures (EFTofLSS). Specifically, we emulate separately the various contributions to the one- and two-loop parts of the power spectrum, leaving out the possible counterterms which can be added as multiplicative prefactors. By leaving the time-dependence of the counterterms unspecified at the emulation stage, our technique has the advantage of being extremely versatile in fitting any type of counterterm parametrisation to data, or to simulations, without having to change the emulator. We construct our emulators using the method of symbolic regression which results in functions that can be used directly in computer code, while achieving errors of better than $0.5\%$ within the $k$-range of validity of EFT and maintaining ultra-fast computational evaluation of less than $\sim5\times10^{-4}s$ on a single core.

papers.title: Mock Observations for the CSST Mission: CPI-C -- Targets for High Contrast Imaging
papers.summary: We introduce CPISM, a simulation program developed for the Cool Planet Imaging Coronagraph (CPI-C) on the China Space Station Telescope (CSST). CPISM supports high-contrast exoplanet imaging by simulating observational conditions and instrumental effects to optimize target selection and observation strategies. The modular design includes target modeling, imaging simulation, observational effects, detector response, and data product generation modules, enabling flexible and realistic synthetic observations. Validation through simulations of a bright star shows strong agreement with theoretical expectations, confirming the program's accuracy. CPISM's modular design allows flexibility, accommodating different stellar and planetary models, and can simulate instrumental noise, cosmic rays, and other observational effects. This tool aids in data processing, signal-to-noise ratio analysis, and high-contrast photometry, contributing to future exoplanet discovery and characterization efforts. The program's outputs will enhance observation planning and scientific return for the CPI-C mission, providing critical insights into exoplanetary systems.

papers.title: FEADME: Fast Elliptical Accretion Disk Modeling Engine
papers.summary: We present FEADME (Fast Elliptical Accretion Disk Modeling Engine), a GPU-accelerated Python framework for modeling broad Balmer-line emission with a relativistic elliptical accretion-disk formalism. Using JAX and NumPyro for differentiable forward modeling and Bayesian inference, FEADME enables reproducible analyses of large samples of disk-dominated emission-line profiles. We apply the framework to 237 double-peaked emitters (DPEs) and five tidal disruption events (TDEs) with disk-like H$\alpha$ emission, fitting three model families per spectrum and selecting the preferred model using the widely applicable information criterion (WAIC). After posterior-quality filtering, the disk-bearing active galactic nuclei (AGN) sample contains 165 sources and the TDE sample contains 27 usable epochs. Within the common elliptical-disk model, AGN occupy a broad, continuous distribution of disk geometries and kinematics summarized by five phenomenological Gaussian-mixture morphology bins, while TDE and AGN parameters overlap in radial scale, local broadening, and emissivity slope. The TDE epochs tend toward lower fitted eccentricities and broader non-disk Gaussian components. Comparison with published circular-disk plus spiral-arm fits to the same AGN spectra produces substantially different distributions of inclination, radii, emissivity slope, and local broadening, demonstrating that these inferred parameters depend strongly on the treatment of profile asymmetry. Most AGN and TDEs favor models containing a disk and an additional broad-line component, suggesting that disk emission commonly coexists with more isotropic or wind-driven gas. These results demonstrate FEADME's utility for population studies and the importance of a consistent asymmetry prescription when comparing disk structures across accretion environments.

papers.title: Constraint on magnetized black bounce spacetime from HFQPOs data and the selection of resonance models via information criterion
papers.summary: Black bounce spacetime, proposed by Simpson and Visser (SV), can describe the Schwarzschild solution, regular black holes, and traversable wormholes in a unified manner, depending on the value of the regularization parameter $a$. This paper primarily explores the dynamics of charged particle in the magnetized SV spacetime, and constrains the parameters of the SV spacetime along with its surrounding magnetic fields. The constraints are given by using $\chi^2$ analysis combined with high-frequency quasi-periodic oscillation (HFQPO) data observed from three microquasars: GRS 1915+105, XTE 1550-564, and GRO 1655-40. The results indicate that the magnetic field significantly influences the position of the innermost stable circular orbit of charged particle and frequency distribution of epicyclic motion, which excites more resonance model variants, enhancing observational effects. Additionally, we employ the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to evaluate resonance model and its various variants. The support for different models from observational data shows significant variation: $E R_8$ as the best model is supported strongly, $ER_3$ model has moderate evidence of support, $ER_6$ and $ER_7$ models are considerably less support, while other resonance models have essentially no support. The result from AIC is broadly consistent with the results obtained from the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) and the Bayes factor. For models more supported by the observational data, the allowed ranges of the regularization parameter: $0\leq a/M<0.736$ ($68\%$ confidence level) suggests that HFQPOs data could support the magnetized black bounce spacetime as a regular black hole, and the smaller value of the regularization parameter indicates a possibility of the presence of quantum effects.

papers.title: Exposure-averaged Gaussian Processes for Combining Overlapping Datasets
papers.summary: Physically motivated Gaussian process (GP) kernels for stellar variability, like the commonly used damped, driven simple harmonic oscillators that model stellar granulation and p-mode oscillations, quantify the instantaneous covariance between any two points. For kernels whose timescales are significantly longer than the typical exposure times, such GP kernels are sufficient. For time series where the exposure time is comparable to the kernel timescale, the observed signal represents an exposure-averaged version of the true underlying signal. This distinction is important in the context of recent data streams from Extreme Precision Radial Velocity (EPRV) spectrographs like fast readout stellar data of asteroseismology targets and solar data to monitor the Sun's variability during daytime observations. Current solar EPRV facilities have significantly different exposure times per-site, owing to the different design choices made. Consequently, each instrument traces different binned versions of the same "latent" signal. Here we present a GP framework that accounts for exposure times by computing integrated forms of the instantaneous kernels typically used. These functions allow one to predict the true latent oscillation signals and the exposure-binned version expected by each instrument. We extend the framework to work for instruments with significant time overlap (i.e., similar longitude) by including relative instrumental drift components that can be predicted and separated from the stellar variability components. We use Sun-as-a-star EPRV datasets as our primary example, but present these approaches in a generalized way for application to any dataset where exposure times are a relevant factor or combining instruments with significant overlap.

papers.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
papers.summary: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. This milestone represents a major advancement for GW cosmology, as many methods, particularly those employing the spectral siren approach, critically depend on the number of available sources. We investigate the impact of a novel parametric model describing the full population mass spectrum of CBCs on the estimation of the Hubble constant. This model is designed to test the impact of heavy black holes in GW cosmology. We perform a joint inference of cosmological and population parameters using 142 CBCs from GWTC-4.0 with a false alarm rate smaller than 0.25 per year, using both spectral and dark siren approaches. With spectral sirens, we estimate the Hubble constant to be $H_0 = 78.8^{+19.0}_{-15.3}\,{\rm km s^{-1} Mpc^{-1}}$ (68% CL), while the dark siren method yields $H_0 = 82.5^{+16.8}_{-14.3}\,{\rm km s^{-1} Mpc^{-1}}$ (68% CL). These results improve the uncertainty by approximately 30.4% and 36.2%, respectively. We show that this improvement is linked to the presence of a new mass scale in the binary black hole mass spectrum at $63.3^{+4.8}_{-4.8}\,M_{\odot}$, which provides additional constraints on the Hubble constant. Besides providing the tightest standard-siren constraints on $H_0$, this highlights the importance of a heavy-mass feature in the black hole spectrum.

papers.title: Protonic thermoelectric effect of Superionic H$_2$O and magnetic field generation in Uranus and Neptune
papers.summary: The origin of the anomalous magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune, with significant tilts and multi-dipole configurations, is central to understanding the internal structure and evolution of the ice giants. Recent investigations confirmed that superionic H$_2$O ice is thermodynamically stable and constitutes the dominant H$_2$O phase within their icy mantles. Here, we use deep learning and ab initio molecular dynamics to investigate the thermal and protonic transport properties of superionic H$_2$O ice. We demonstrate that superionic H$_2$O ice exhibits a pronounced protonic thermoelectric effect, with a maximum Seebeck coefficient that can reach $\sim 620$ $\mu$V K$^{-1}$ within the interior of Uranus, whereas Neptune's is lower, within the range of 570-585 $\mu$V K$^{-1}$. Consequently, the temperature gradients in the icy mantles can induce proton migration, thereby driving magnetic field generation. Based on this mechanism, and within a dipolar approximation that captures the mean field, the disparities in mean dipolar magnetic field strength between Uranus and Neptune can be explained exclusively by their differing internal temperature gradients, and the predicted mean field strengths are comparable to those observed by Voyager 2.

papers.title: Extracting intrinsic alignments in the Dark Energy Survey's year 1 data, using the self-calibration method and LSST-DESC tools
papers.summary: We present the implementation of a Self-Calibration of Intrinsic Alignments of galaxies as an extension to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC)'s weak lensing 3x2pt pipeline (TXPipe). As a demonstration, we have run this pipeline on the Dark Energy Survey (DES) year one data set. We find indications of a non-zero intrinsic alignment signal in the higher redshift bins, while in the lower bins our results look more uncertain. We believe this is caused by known issues with the individual galaxies photo-z estimation. This effect is particularly harmful for the self-calibration method, since it has high requirements for reliable estimation of the photo-$z$s, and the need for individual galaxy point estimates and tomographic binning to match. We show how different methods of recreating the redshift probability distribution can affect the detection of intrinsic alignment.

papers.title: On the Physical Origins of the Millimeter Fundamental Plane in Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.summary: Observations of active galactic nuclei have revealed a correlation between millimeter luminosity, X-ray luminosity, and mass, suggesting the emission in each of these bands is powered by a common source. Starting with a set of five general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations with dynamically important magnetic fields, we perform ray-tracing calculations to produce spectra including synchrotron emission, bremsstrahlung emission, and Compton scattering. Our models with similar Eddington ratios to the objects for which the relationship was inferred naturally reproduce observations without tuning. Our lower Eddington ratio models depart from this relationship, likely attributable to an observational bias against extremely low accretion rates. We find that inverse Compton scattering dominates the production of X-rays over bremsstrahlung radiation in almost all models, and in all models consistent with the observed correlation. We find only a modest spin dependence in this relationship. This study demonstrates that a compact, hot accretion flow with dynamically important magnetic fields can naturally explain observed millimeter and X-ray properties in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei. Future work should explore the impacts of non-thermal electron populations, weaker magnetic fields, and radiative cooling.

papers.title: An autoencoder-based surrogate waveform model for quasi-circular binary-black-hole mergers
papers.summary: The generation of accurate waveforms from binary black hole (BBH) mergers is a major effort in Gravitational-Wave Astronomy. In recent years, machine-learning-based surrogate models for BBH waveforms have been proposed. Those offer the potential to dramatically accelerate waveform generation while maintaining accuracy competitive with that of traditional waveform approximants. In this work, we investigate the viability of autoencoders as generative models for gravitational-wave signals from quasi-circular BBH mergers. We introduce AESur3dq8, a novel surrogate waveform model based on autoencoders that enables the rapid and accurate construction of large template banks, producing millions of waveforms in under a second using modest computational resources. The model is trained on the numerical-relativity-informed surrogate NRHybSur3dq8 and subsequently fine-tuned using the SXS catalog of BBH simulations. We demonstrate that waveforms generated by AESur3dq8 achieve mismatches of order $10^{-4}$ with respect to Numerical Relativity waveforms, and that parameter estimation performed with these templates yields results fully consistent with those reported by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration for observed gravitational-wave events.

papers.title: The Evolution of the Spin Alignments of Dark Matter Halos in the Cosmic Web
papers.summary: We investigate the evolution of dark matter halo spin alignments with respect to cosmic filaments, exploring how halo mass, proximity to filaments, and major mergers influence their orientation over time. We perform a suite of dark matter-only zoom-in N-body simulations centered on ten filaments extracted from a cosmological box using the 1DREAM structure finder. This approach allows us to resolve low-mass halos within filaments while preserving the large-scale environment. Halos are identified with the Amiga Halo Finder (AHF), and their evolutionary histories are reconstructed to trace the spin, shape, and distance to the filament from redshift $z = 1$ to $z = 0$. We confirm a strong mass-dependent alignment signal: low-mass halos tend to align parallel to the filament, while high-mass halos preferentially exhibit perpendicular orientations, despite limited statistics. Perpendicular alignments become dominant at the highest halo masses in our sample, around $\log_{10}(M_\mathrm{h}/h^{-1}\mathrm{M_\odot}) \sim 12$. We also find that major mergers can induce sharp spin reorientations and temporary transitions toward more prolate halo shapes, particularly in massive halos located near the filament core, suggesting a preferential merger direction within filaments. Overall, halo mass emerges as the primary factor governing spin-filament alignments in our sample. By analyzing the global evolution, we find that the average orientations at z = 0 do not differ significantly from those at $z = 1$, indicating that the present-day spin configuration is largely established at earlier stages of halo evolution. Major mergers, although relatively rare, represent one of the few mechanisms capable of disrupting this initial alignment.

papers.title: Two-stage disruption of resonant chains
papers.summary: TESS is enabling the discovery of transiting planets around young stars. These observations suggest that most close-in planets were born in chains of mean-motion resonances that break on a characteristic timescale of order 100 Myr. This observation is surprising because the same dissipative forces that capture planets into resonance render their orbits long-term stable. We explore a two-stage disruption scenario for resonant chains of super-Earths. First, the chains have their (free) eccentricities excited by some mechanism. We show that any such mechanism that seeds eccentricities of a few percent sets in motion a second stage of dynamical instability on a $\sim$100 Myr timescale. A possible stage-one mechanism is the accretion of a handful of Mercury-sized bodies totaling a few percent of the planetary system mass, which excites the requisite eccentricities and triggers a stage two that reproduces the observed decline in the incidence of resonance. Impacts from such bodies can also explain why some young systems have period ratios narrow of commensurability. We sketch how these impactors may have grown out of debris left over from an earlier epoch of planet formation. We also identify two new trends in the observational data: a decline in multiplicity on the same timescale as the decline in the incidence of resonance, and an increase in the occupation of resonances with multiplicity.

papers.title: The study of the circumnuclear environment of accreting supermassive black holes with realistic X-ray spectral models
papers.summary: X-ray spectral modeling is a powerful tool for studying the immediate environment of accreting objects, including supermassive black holes. Several models, either phenomenological or physically driven, have been developed over the past decade to study X-ray spectra, delivering important insights into the properties of circumnuclear material of active galactic nuclei (AGN). Despite the fact that these models are able to reproduce the data well, they often lack realistic geometries, and most of them consist of simplified configurations such as a slab or a torus. We use the ray-tracing code \textsc{RefleX} to generate new spectral models that cover a wide energy range in the X-ray band, adopting a realistic configuration for the surrounding material. We introduce two new table models that are publicly available: 1) the RXToPo model, which features an X-ray source along with a dusty torus and a polar hollow cone; 2) the RXagn1 model, which includes, besides the torus and polar cone, also the accretion disk and the broad line region. Both models were applied to the X-ray spectrum of NGC 424, demonstrating their potential to study sources whose X-ray emission is dominated by reprocessed radiation.

papers.title: No Blue without Red: Evolutionary Properties of Super-Early Galaxies
papers.summary: The discovery of numerous luminous, super-early galaxies at $z>10$ by JWST has revealed a striking diversity in their ultraviolet (UV) properties, ranging from extremely blue, dust-poor systems to a smaller population of significantly reddened sources. We investigate the physical origin of this diversity within the framework of the Attenuation-Free Model (AFM), in which radiation-driven outflows redistribute dust to large galactic radii, reducing the effective attenuation. Starting from a sample of 32 spectroscopically confirmed super-early galaxies, we apply the detailed AFM analysis to a subset of 17 systems with suitable size constraints and derive their key physical properties, including halo mass, star formation efficiency, metallicity, and outflow extent. We find that these systems reside in massive halos ($\log M/M_\odot \sim 10.7$) and exhibit moderate ($0.01 < \epsilon_* < 0.05$) star formation efficiencies, while frequently reaching super-Eddington conditions that trigger powerful outflows. Within the AFM framework, we propose a possible evolutionary sequence in which galaxies transition from a dust-obscured ``Red Monster'' phase to a UV-bright ``Blue Monster'' phase as outflows clear their central regions. The recently confirmed red galaxy EGS-z11-R0 at $z=11.45$ is naturally interpreted as a system observed during this obscured phase. Compact ($r_e < 150$ pc) sources are instead difficult to reconcile within AFM; we speculate that their emission is dominated by an AGN. Our results provide a coherent interpretation of super-early galaxy properties and highlight the key role of radiation-driven outflows in shaping galaxy evolution at cosmic dawn. Future observations with JWST and ALMA will be essential to test these predictions and further constrain the nature of the earliest galaxies.

papers.title: Increasing the Precision of Surrogate Models for Weak Lensing Mass Maps with Flow Matching
papers.summary: Weak gravitational lensing maps compactly encode the evolution of cosmic large-scale structure and are a key tool for cosmological analyses. Performing inference directly at the map level allows flexible choices of statistics and can increase constraining power. Conventional methods rely solely on N-body simulations and are computationally expensive. Generative machine-learning emulators can accelerate map-level theory prediction. However, existing GAN-based map-level surrogates still have limited statistical fidelity. They can produce over-smoothed maps, may fail to capture the full distribution of generated map sets and can be difficult to train. Continuous normalizing flows trained with flow matching have recently emerged as a powerful class of generative models. We present a residual label-conditional flow matching generative network that conditions explicitly on the matter density $\Omega_m$ and clustering amplitude $\sigma_8$ for a fixed source redshift distribution $n(z)$. The model learns a continuous probability flow in a residual space from label-specific noise distributions to convergence maps. We evaluate it using pixel and peak statistics, the power spectrum, bispectrum, power-spectrum correlation matrices, and other validation metrics. Compared with the previous GAN benchmark, the proposed method improves the typical fidelity of generated maps from below 10% and below 20% to below 1% and below 5% for basic and higher-order statistics, respectively. The agreement at the level of map distributions is also very good: maps generated from random noise match well the distribution of maps generated with N-body simulations from random initial conditions. This work brings us closer to a practical mass-map emulator that captures the cosmological signal while supporting multiple forms of data analysis.

papers.title: How Common Are Common Envelopes? Quantifying Their Role in Forming Gravitational-Wave Sources
papers.summary: A central goal of gravitational-wave astronomy is to use merging binary black hole (BBH), black hole-neutron star (BHNS), and binary neutron star (BNS) systems as fossils to reconstruct the formation and evolution of massive stars across cosmic time. In practice, this inference relies on population-synthesis models that map massive stellar binaries to merging compact objects. However, these models disagree on the dominant orbital-hardening mechanisms within isolated binary evolution, particularly on whether common-envelope (CE) evolution is required. To address this, we compile and systematically compare formation-channel predictions from more than 200 isolated-binary population-synthesis simulations, organized within a unified hierarchical taxonomy. We find that BBH and BHNS formation pathways span nearly the full allowed range from CE-dominated to without-CE-dominated evolution (0-100%), while often predicting similar merger rates, revealing a fundamental degeneracy: merger-rate measurements alone do not uniquely constrain the underlying evolutionary pathways. In contrast, BNS formation proceeds almost exclusively through channels involving at least one CE phase (>90-100%), suggesting CE evolution plays a qualitatively different role in BNS than in BBH and BHNS formation. The relative contributions of with-CE and without-CE pathways are governed primarily by assumptions controlling mass-transfer stability, angular-momentum loss, CE efficiency, and supernova physics, which often act non-linearly and in correlated fashion, such that trends from one-at-a-time parameter variations do not generalize across simulation frameworks. Robust interpretation of gravitational-wave populations will therefore require transparent formation-channel definitions, reproducible analysis pipelines, systematic cross-code comparisons, and observational constraints that extend beyond merger rates alone.

papers.title: The Lifecycle and Emission Properties of PAHs in Cosmological Hydrodynamic Galaxy Formation Simulations
papers.summary: We present the first cosmological model for the lifecycle and luminous properties of PAHs in galaxies as they evolve from z=6-->0. We model 40 zoom-in galaxies, coupled with an on-the-fly model for the evolution of dust grains in the ISM. We approximate PAHs as ultrasmall (a < 13 Angstrom) carbonaceous dust grains, and couple this model with single-photon excitation calculations to compute the emergent mid-infrared spectra. (1) If we assume that dust is large upon formation, then PAHs are naturally able to form in situ in the ISM via grain-grain shattering. Interstellar collision velocities increase in low density, diffuse gas in our model; as galaxies evolve, the increase in fractional mass of diffuse gas drives an increase in grain-grain collision velocities and a corresponding rise in the PAH mass fraction (qPAH) from ~5 x 10^{-4} at z~4 to ~10^{-2} at z~0. (2) Increased PAH production in the diffuse ISM results in an inverse relationship between qPAH and the molecular gas fraction. (3) The PAH light-to-mass ratio scales linearly with the radiation field intensity (LPAH/MPAH ~ G_0) but anti-correlates with qPAH, because high-Sigma_SFR galaxies have a denser ISM that suppresses shattering. This means the physical qPAH and observed LPAH/LFIR do not evolve in lockstep. (4) The PAH-metallicity relationship (PZR) arises naturally in this framework: galaxies enrich and grow their diffuse ISM fraction simultaneously, linking rising metallicity to rising qPAH. Our models represent the first to reproduce the PZR observed across z=0-2. (5) The LPAH-SFR and LPAH-M_mol relations emerge from two effects: more massive galaxies have larger PAH reservoirs, and higher-SFR galaxies excite their PAHs more efficiently per unit mass. Taken together, these results suggest that grain-grain shattering in the diffuse ISM is the main driver behind the evolution of cosmic PAH abundances.

papers.title: The youth of the intracluster medium. I. A non-parametric characterisation of the gas and electron number density profiles of $z \simeq 2$ protoclusters
papers.summary: Context. Protoclusters of galaxies are the earliest phase in the assembly of galaxy clusters and can provide invaluable information about plasma physics, cosmic magnetism, and cosmology. However, due to small angular sizes and cosmological dimming, observing the proto-intracluster medium (proto-ICM) associated with protocluster cores is far from trivial. Aims. We aim to provide a non-parametric description of the gas mass and electron number density profiles of the proto-ICM at $z = 2$, and to study their dependence on mass, dynamical state and central activity. Methods. We extract and analyse over $3800$ regions around protocluster cores with spherical-overdensity masses above $M_\mathrm{500c} > 10^{13} \, M_\odot$ out of a large simulated volume within the Magneticum suite. We study their density profiles, temperature structure, ionisation degree and electron number density as a function of mass and other secondary properties characterising dynamical state and central activity, extending from the central halo to the surrounding protocluster environment. Results. Protoclusters present moderate deviations from self-similarity in their density profiles and temperature structure, with a strong double-$\beta$ structure especially relevant at high masses and intense AGN accretion. Hot, ionised gas is only dominant at intermediate radii ($r \gtrsim [0.1-0.5] R_\mathrm{500c}$), where its density also correlates with mass and dynamical disturbance. Conclusions. These results constitute the basis for a forthcoming parametric calibration of proto-ICM density profiles, which could be useful for interpreting observables sensitive to the density and ionisation of the diffuse gas.

papers.title: Modeling Dependence Structures in Astronomical Multi-Band Time Series Data via Multi-Output Gaussian Processes
papers.summary: Modern astronomical time-domain surveys routinely collect multi-band light curves that provide complementary information about the physical processes governing source variability. Although various multi-output Gaussian process (GP) models have been applied in different astronomical contexts, the statistical and astrophysical implications of their dependence structures have received comparatively limited attention. In this work, we examine three existing approaches to modeling cross-band dependence within a common multi-output GP framework and investigate how their underlying assumptions affect statistical inference and astrophysical interpretation. These include covariance-based, stochastic differential equation (SDE)-based, and latent-process approaches, which differ mainly in how cross-band dependence is introduced. The covariance-based approach directly specifies cross-band covariance functions to characterize dependence, whereas the SDE-based approach specifies joint temporal dynamics, with cross-band dependence arising from coupled dynamics or correlated driving processes. The latent-process approach represents dependence through shared stochastic processes and their transformations, which can reflect physical relationships among multiple light curves. We demonstrate the practical implications of these modeling choices through applications to multi-band active galactic nucleus light curves and emission-line reverberation mapping. Rather than advocating a universally preferred approach, this work provides guidance for selecting dependence structures according to scientific objectives and clarifies how these choices influence the statistical characterization and scientific interpretation of multi-band stochastic variability.

papers.title: Using Scattered Near-Infrared Light to Map Water Ice in Prestellar Cores with SPHEREx
papers.summary: We present the first coreshine-derived, spatially-resolved maps of the 3 $\mu$m H$_2$O ice absorption feature in four prestellar cores, using SPHEREx spectra. Ices are a key component of dense cores in molecular clouds, playing a central role in the chemistry of planet formation around young stars. However, spatially resolved abundance studies remain limited, typically relying on unevenly distributed background star sightlines. Here, we take advantage of the all-sky spectrophotometric capabilities of SPHEREx to construct ice absorption maps with uniform spatial resolution using the illumination of dense cores by scattered Galactic radiation, or coreshine. To demonstrate proof of concept, we analyse the spatially varying H$_2$O ice absorption in four nearby (~140 pc) prestellar cores - L1544, CrA 151, L260 and L1512. Two cores follow the expected spatial trend of ice absorption peaking at the centre, but the two densest cores show a surprising drop in observed ice absorption in the innermost regions. To interpret the absorption maps, we construct analytical and simulated models of a Bonnor-Ebert sphere illuminated by scattering. We study the effects of different geometric configurations, ice mass fractions, and spatial differences in ice composition. None of these can explain the reduced central absorption, pointing to an unexplained physical or chemical effect operating in the densest prestellar regions. Our simulations further show that spectra derived from coreshine provide a robust tracer of spatially varying ice density and composition, establishing SPHEREx scattered-light spectroscopy as a powerful new probe of ice in dense cores.

papers.title: AGN Reverberation Mapping with LITMUS: Fundamental Limits on lag Recovery Rates
papers.summary: Reverberation mapping of active galactic nuclei provides one of the most direct probes of the geometry and kinematics of the broad-line region by measuring time delays between continuum and line variability. Modern RM surveys frequently suffer difficulties with lag measurements due to poor signal to noise and aliasing, whereby multimodal lag posterior distributions arise due to seasonal gaps in our data. These challenge the reliability of commonly used fitting tools such as JAVELIN, which can return a high rate of false positives. We implement a new lag measurement package, LITMUS, and introduce a new framework that uses Bayesian evidence to identify false positive lag measurements, as well as examine the question of how many AGN present detectable lags in high redshift industrial scale surveys like OzDES and SDSS. Our analysis differs from previous RM studies in six key respects: (i) our inference is robust to the previously under-diagnosed numerical component of aliasing, (ii) we use a consistent methodology for all sources, (iii) uncertainty in the underlying AGN variability is fully marginalised, (iv) lag significance is assessed via Bayesian model comparison rather than heuristic metrics, (v) false-positive rates are quantified by comparison against random-chance recoveries and (vi) we use marginal likelihoods to distinguish between sources where a lag is not detectable in our data and sources that show no evidence of reverberation. Applied to the OzDES sample, we find that previous RM studies are likely to have overestimated the confidence of recovered lags, and we find a stark contrast between a low reverberation percentage for the MgII line (3-28% depending on assumptions) and much higher percentages in the CIV and especially the H$\beta$ line, which is consistent with 100%. We also present a re-analysed set of lags from the OzDES sample with better quantified reliabilities

papers.title: Rings in the Sky: Orbital Data Centres and Potential Impacts to Astronomy and the Sky
papers.summary: Megaconstellations of orbital data centres (ODCs) have the potential to fundamentally change the sky without a concerted mitigation effort. Potential changes include producing large coherent structures that would be visible during twilight and some portions of the night, as well as produce persistent infrared and radio source regions. We investigate the potential sky impacts of three ODC designs, as proposed by three companies. While more companies have proposed to launch megaconstellations of ODCs, other potential operators are expected to use the same design principles as presented here. These systems would produce large ring structures with each ring passing through the sky twice a day. The largest impacts are expected to occur during winter, where ring structures could be seen sweeping through otherwise dark skies. The confinement of the rings' orbital nodes will play a large role in determining whether the rings will be dense arcs in the sky or will produce sky-wide interference. The rings will persist throughout the day in polar regions, with the potential to interfere with polar science initiatives. Such structures will further have societal implications for high-latitude communities. We use simplified brightness models, which compare well with more detailed calculations, to show that brightness mitigation and/or hard limits on satellite numbers will be essential for preventing a future that has more visible satellites in the sky than visible stars during certain times of night.

papers.title: HII-CHI-mistry for active galactic nuclei: optical sulphur abundances without empirical ionisation correction factors
papers.summary: > The determination of sulphur abundances in active galactic nuclei (AGN) is uncertain because ionisation correction factors (ICFs) are commonly calibrated for HII regions. We extend the HII-CHI-mistry methodology to derive total S/H in AGN from optical emission lines through comparison with photoionisation models. Tests against Seyfert galaxies with direct-method ionic abundances favour models with alpha_ox=-1.2 and a 98% free-electron stopping criterion. While O/H agrees with previous determinations, HCm yields systematically larger S/H than direct-method analyses using classical ICFs, suggesting that these prescriptions underestimate higher sulphur ionisation stages in AGN. Applied to MaNGA Seyfert and LINER-like regions, the method reveals a common positive S/O-metallicity relation. Seyferts show slightly larger median S/O than star-forming regions at high O/H, while LINERs occupy an intermediate position. These differences become weaker when S/H rather than O/H is used as the metallicity tracer, although Seyferts still tend to populate the upper envelope. Sulphur may therefore provide a robust tracer of gas-phase metallicity, while the differences between Seyferts and LINERs may reflect differences in their ionisation conditions and ionising SEDs.
