papers.title: Unconventional SOC-activated Altermagnetic Spin Splitting and Half-Angle Locking of Spin Transport
papers.summary: Conventional altermagnetic spin splitting arises from staggered exchange and sublattice-dependent anisotropic hopping without requiring spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Here we derive a low-energy effective model showing that SOC and staggered exchange can jointly activate additional spin splitting on momentum planes where the nonrelativistic contribution vanishes. In hexagonal $\alpha$-MnTe, this SOC-activated contribution produces d-wave spin splitting near $\Gamma$ with out-of-plane spin polarization. Its leading angular pattern counter-rotates by half the in-plane N\'eel-vector rotation angle. First-principles spin-transport calculations reveal a corresponding approximate half-angle locking between the N\'eel-vector orientation and the electric-field directions maximizing the signed longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Analytical transport calculations based on the effective model trace this locking to the same angular coupling between momentum and the N\'eel vector that governs the spin-splitting pattern. Our findings connect the microscopic mechanism of SOC-activated altermagnetic spin splitting to directional spin transport, providing a theoretical basis for probing N\'eel-vector orientation and controlling spin-current generation.

papers.title: Electric Field-Induced Hole- and Electron-Type Flat Bands in Twisted Double Bilayer Graphene
papers.summary: Application of a finite electric field and small twist angle between two graphene bilayers leads to widely tunable electronic structures that support emergent phenomena. Here, we measure the electronic structure of twisted double bilayer graphene with twist angles of 3.1$^{\circ}$ and 6.0$^{\circ}$ using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (microARPES) on \textit{in situ} gated samples. At a twist angle of 6.0$^{\circ}$, we find that the dispersion around the valence and conduction band extrema is unchanged compared to separate graphene bilayers, whereas electric field tunable hybridisation gaps and band flattening effects occur at higher binding energies. In the 3.1$^{\circ}$ structure, we find that the resulting superlattice drives dispersion changes around the valence and conduction band edges. Increasing the gate-induced doping in the bottom bilayer leads to the formation of flat bands between the valence band maximum in the bottom bilayer and conduction band minimum in the top bilayer. Our experiments establish combinations of twist angle and electric field that potentially support strong electron-hole excitations and that provide a benchmark for the theoretical description of moderately twisted double bilayer graphene.

papers.title: Chaos picture of spin glasses
papers.summary: The chaos picture is a novel, coherent, and intuitive theoretical framework for spin glasses, reconciling the 40-year-old droplet vs. replica symmetry breaking debate. First, we argue the formation of a hierarchical energy landscape by pinning and dynamic filtering of random droplets. As the temperature decreases, the chaos picture describes a progressive freezing of scale-dependent droplets in real space, which mirrors a hierarchical free energy landscape fracturing process in phase space. This bifurcation process is accompanied by temperature chaos, leading to dynamic pure state coexistence without violating the droplet scaling. Crucially, the interface geometry is not critical to these mechanisms, naturally incorporating the interface crossover from planar, fractal, to space-filling as the dimensionality increases, in line with the mean-field limit. Finally, the chaos picture provides profound insights into spin-glass dynamics such as aging, rejuvenation, and memory effect, while offering a streamlined reinterpretation of the complex metastate framework.

papers.title: Molecular shape controls dipolar correlations in polar liquids
papers.summary: The dielectric constant of polar liquids depends not only on the magnitude of the molecular dipole moment but also on short range orientational correlations between neighboring dipoles. How molecular structure determines these correlations, quantified by the Kirkwood correlation factor $g_\mathrm{K}$, remains unclear. Using molecular dynamics simulations of model polar liquids without hydrogen bonding, we show that molecular shape plays a central role. We interpret $g_\mathrm{K}$ as resulting from the combination of dipolar interactions and steric effects, which together favor either alignment or antialignment of neighboring molecules. Depending on molecular shape, $g_\mathrm{K}$ can either increases or decreases upon cooling, or change monotony. A minimal model of dipoles on a cubic lattice reproduces these three regimes and attributes the nonmonotonic case to a competition between the first layer of neighbors, which favors alignment, and the second layer, which favors antialignment.

papers.title: Activation force dependence of the fluidization transition in supercooled active water
papers.summary: Using an activation model reproducing facilitation mechanisms, we found recently a fluidization transition in supercooled water triggered by the motion of a few active molecules. We investigate here the effect of the activation force on the transition. The activation force increases the probability for active molecules to overcome the energy barrier induced by caging. The induced molecular motions result in an intermittent loose structure leading to a decrease of energy barriers around the moving molecule, thus facilitating the motion of nearby molecules. Therefore we expect the force, if small enough, to increase the facilitation mechanism, and as a result cooperative motions induced by it. As a result the activation force permits to tune facilitation and cooperative motions in active glass-formers. We find an optimum force for cooperative motions that we evaluate to be around 3.5pN, a value in the range of protein motor forces. As expected for a phase transition we observe peaks of cooperative motions (dynamic heterogeneity) on the transition. This result shows that dynamical heterogeneity are the cooperative motions of physical importance for the transition.

papers.title: Quantum critical scaling in convective active matter
papers.summary: We construct a minimal field theory for critical quantum active matter, describing a nonconserved scalar order parameter with Landau-Ginzburg ordering and self-advection. When diffusive noise dominates, higher-order quantum vertices and non-Gaussian noise fluctuations remain relevant alongside the deterministic nonlinearities, with an upper critical dimension $d_c=2$. A one-loop renormalization-group analysis in $d=2-\epsilon$ reveals a purely dissipative fixed point, where nonlinear noise suppresses convection, and a quantum convective saddle, where interactions, convection, and non-Gaussian noise coexist. We determine the critical exponents, show that the convective regime is distinct from conventional Burgers hydrodynamics, and discuss how it could govern transient universal scaling in microscopic models of quantum active matter before a crossover to semi-classical dynamics.

papers.title: Topological Criticality with Charge-\(3e\) Fluctuations in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) Triangular-Lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard Model
papers.summary: A transition between an integer quantum Hall insulator and a chiral spin liquid can become critical without closing the single-electron gap, raising the question of which composite excitations govern the change in topological order. We investigate this question in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model at one particle per site and magnetic flux \(\pi/3\) per triangle. Using infinite density matrix renormalization group calculations, we identify a weak-coupling integer quantum Hall phase and an interaction-driven \(\mathrm{SU}(3)_1\) chiral spin liquid. Near the transition, both the neutral and charge-\(3e\) correlation lengths increase substantially, whereas the single-electron correlation length remains short, providing evidence for a Chern--Simons--Higgs critical theory, where a gauge-invariant monopole carries the quantum numbers of a fermionic \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)-singlet trion. We discuss the implications for doping the system and recent experiments on doping \(\nu=-2/3\) fractional quantum anomalous Hall in tMoTe\(_2\).

papers.title: The Acridine Polymorph Landscape: Characterization and Selective Control by Additives
papers.summary: Polymorphism in molecular crystals presents a major challenge for controlling crystallization. Here, we combine experiment and theory to characterize the polymorph landscape of acridine and investigate its selective control by additives. Melt crystallization experiments resolve the previously unknown structure of form VIII, while topological crystal structure prediction recovers all seven known unsolvated polymorphs with determined crystal structures. Combining a fine-tuned machine-learned interatomic potential with anharmonic free energy calculations reproduces the experimentally observed stability relationships and reveals a shallow free energy landscape. Finally, experimentally observed additive-induced polymorph preferences correlate with mixed-crystal substitutional defect energies and topological similarities between additive and acridine crystal structures. Together, these results provide a comprehensive picture of acridine polymorphism, linking crystal structure, thermodynamic stability, and additive-controlled crystallization.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
papers.summary: Symmetries of quantum systems provide a natural way to organize the eigenspaces of many-body Hamiltonians. When degeneracies exist, however, they play a more subtle role as different sets of symmetry operators can resolve the same energy subspace into states with very different correlation properties. We study this interplay using a sequence of FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ models. For a Hubbard model of FeO, the ground space is 16-fold degenerate. Resolving it by local magnetizations gives a basis of Slater determinants, while total-spin quantum numbers select entangled and non-Gaussian states from the same ground manifold. Adding density-density Hund interactions breaks the independent spin rotations and reduces the ground space to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization. These states are extremely close to Slater determinants in their natural occupations, yet have finite two-body cumulants and conserved-operator algebras whose orbit dimensions differ substantially from the Slater values. Fe$_2$O$_2$ provides a larger example in which spatial mode entanglement can be substantial while fermionic non-Gaussianity remains weak, with the conserved-operator structure again distinguishing the state from the corresponding Slater transformation class. Together, these examples show that symmetry resolution, mode entanglement, reduced-density-matrix correlations, and conserved-operator structure provide complementary information about interacting and degenerate electronic ground states.

papers.title: Thermodynamic characterization of message-passing: Framework and initial study
papers.summary: We study the thermodynamic efficiency of message-passing decoders using the mismatch cost framework. This framework quantifies the excess entropy generated when a system operates away from the thermodynamically optimal initial distribution. It provides a computable lower bound on irrecoverable energy loss. The decoder is modeled as a main decoding program with local message updates implemented as subroutines. Memory is treated as an external copying subsystem whose thermodynamic cost is excluded. Studying the $[7,4]$ Hamming code transmitted over a binary erasure channel, we show how the channel-induced initialization statistics and the step-wise evolution of the algorithmic state distribution during decoding determine the total mismatch cost. We further show that different thermodynamically optimal state distributions, representing different underlying physical implementations of the decoder, can produce different thermodynamic costs for identical decoding dynamics. Conditioning the input distribution on correctable and non-correctable erasure patterns further reveals distinct thermodynamic signatures. These results demonstrate that thermodynamic cost is jointly governed by decoding dynamics, input statistics, and hardware characteristics. This points to opportunities for thermodynamically-informed decoder design to realize energy-efficient physical implementations.

papers.title: ODAT-SE: A modular and parallel framework for simulation-based inverse problems
papers.summary: Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. It succeeds 2DMAT, which was developed for surface-structure analysis with quantum-beam diffraction and has since been applied to other fields. In version 3, the search algorithms were separated from the application-specific solvers, which became independent packages, and the software was renamed; this paper describes the current version 4.0. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions. Taking up the positron-diffraction example of the 2DMAT paper, the workflow identifies the correlated structural solutions and an effective noise scale close to the imposed perturbation, while exposing incomplete convergence of symmetry-related mode weights. Solver packages, templates, and a gallery of examples support the use of the framework as a general platform for inverse-problem analysis.

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
papers.summary: Recently, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) has been established as a framework for describing quantum phases in open systems. However SW-SSB cannot be characterized by conventional charged two-point correlators. In this work, we show that, for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, SW-SSB manifests as a persistent deficit from the maximal quantum Fisher information (QFI) under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. A model-independent inequality hierarchy establishes the equivalence of this deficit with fidelity and R\'enyi-1 correlators as asymptotic long-range-order diagnostics. It thereby connects finite-angle state overlaps to a constraint on the infinitesimal Bures geometry along the same pair-generated orbit. For symmetry-projected Gibbs states, we further derive a lower bound on the deficit governed by the mean energy injected by the pair operation. Crucially, locality keeps this energy cost uniformly bounded in system size and endpoint separation, maintaining a finite gap below the maximal QFI at any fixed finite temperature. When ordinary charged long range order is absent, this persistent geometric constraint provides a quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB.

papers.title: Threshold Criteria for Bosonic and Fermionic Trimers on a Square Lattice: A Birman--Schwinger Comparison
papers.summary: We compare two three-particle lattice models on the square lattice at total quasimomentum zero: three identical bosons with attractive contact interactions, and a two-fermion plus one distinguishable particle system with attractive interspecies contact. Using the Birman--Schwinger principle combined with symmetry reduction and strong-coupling asymptotics, we distinguish shared methodology from model-dependent spectral conclusions. For bosons, the ground-state energy behaves as minus three times the coupling plus six minus three over twice the coupling plus higher-order corrections, and exactly two bound states exist below the threshold for large coupling; the second lies at a finite distance 0.03542 below the threshold, a genuine eigenvalue rather than a threshold resonance. For fermions, the critical mass ratio is pi divided by pi minus two, approximately 2.75194; above it, a doubly degenerate level appears at strong coupling. Near onset, the binding energy follows a linear-over-logarithmic law. The results are compared with numerical finite-grid Faddeev computations and with recent three-dimensional classifications of threshold states.

papers.title: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
papers.summary: Dynamical quantum simulations are commonly designed to access a particular response function or correlation function. Yet the underlying protocol prepares a family of many-body states that contains information well beyond the observable for which the simulation was originally designed. In this work, we explore the idea of using these states as laboratories for quantum information. As a case study, we consider the local-pulse protocols used to compute Green functions in finite XX and XXX spin chains, and we interpret opposite source rotations as encoding a classical bit into the many-body system. This allows us to follow how the resulting record propagates, how it is encoded across local subsystems, and how readily it can be accessed with different measurements. We also find a clear separation between representation and readout. While fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed response in the XX chain, simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of the locally available information in the XXX chain. This reversed ordering persists when we move from finite-pulse discrimination to local source-angle estimation. Going beyond the source record, the same reduced states also allow us to reinterpret results in terms of Bell state recovery and quantum communication rates, as well as providing direct access to the evolving bipartite and genuine multipartite entanglement of the system. Our results show that dynamical quantum simulations developed for response calculations can naturally be used to ask a much broader set of quantum-information questions about the many-body states they already prepare.

papers.title: Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion
papers.summary: We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $\beta_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leq\rho_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $\rho_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $\delta\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $\delta^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $\delta$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.

papers.title: Anomalous energy transport in the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase
papers.summary: We study nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamic theories with charge and energy conservation in and above two dimensions that describe the large-scale behavior of the Hamiltonian XY model in the disordered and ordered phases. Using renormalization group analysis at one-loop order, we show that while Fourier's law holds in the ordered phase above two dimensions and in the disordered phase in any dimension, the energy diffusivity in the ordered phase exactly in two dimensions, the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, exhibits a logarithmic divergence in the thermodynamic limit. This divergence arises from elastic energy transport induced by spin-wave excitations.

papers.title: Metamagnetic ripples in the UTe2 high magnetic field phase diagram
papers.summary: The heavy fermion metamagnet uranium ditelluride possesses two distinct magnetic field-induced superconducting states. One of these superconductive phases resides at magnetic fields immediately below a first-order metamagnetic transition to a field-polarized paramagnetic state at a field strength $H_m$, while the other exists predominantly above $H_m$. However, little is known about the microscopic properties of this polarized paramagnetic state. Here we report pulsed magnetic field measurements tracking the evolution of $H_m$ for polar and azimuthal inclinations of the magnetic field in the vicinity of the crystallographic $b-a$ plane. We uncover a region of the phase diagram at high fields > 50 T with a ripple-like non-monotonic dependence of $H_m$ on the orientation of field. Within this ripple in the metamagnetic transition surface, $H_m$ exhibits an anomalous temperature dependence, implying that here the polarized state has a lower entropy than the low field paramagnetic state. Our results point towards the presence of complex magnetic interactions and possible magnetic sub-phases at high magnetic fields in UTe$_2$, which may have important implications for the manifestation of exotic field-induced superconductivity.

papers.title: Curvature-stabilized three-dimensional spiral states and local-field nucleation of skyrmions on spherical caps
papers.summary: Magnetic skyrmions stabilized by interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) are promising candidates for applications in memory, logic, and neuromorphic computing. Beyond planar films, theoretical studies predict that curvature can influence skyrmion stability by introducing effective chiral interactions. Here, we investigate skyrmion formation on self-assembled polystyrene particles coated with Pt/Co/Ta multilayers by magnetron sputtering. Vibrating sample magnetometry reveals clear differences in the magnetic reversal behavior of the curvilinear film compared to that of the planar counterpart. Using non-invasive imaging methods such as scanning transmission X-ray microscopy and high-sensitivity in-vacuum magnetic force microscopy (MFM) with low moment magnetic tipcs, we observe a maze domain pattern for the planar films while the curvilinear film reveals three-dimensional spiraling stripe states. By employing a conventional MFM operating under ambient conditions requiring a tip with a higher magnetic moment, we demonstrate that these stripe states can rupture into metastable skyrmions located at the top of the spherical particles by applying consecutive scans. Our results demonstrate that curvilinear films offer an accessible platform for stabilizing single skyrmions using local magnetic field stimuli, opening pathways to study the interplay between interfacial and curvature-induced DMIs and enabling controlled skyrmion writing on three-dimensional magnetic architectures.

papers.title: Topological Quantum Criticality in Quasiperiodic Cluster Ising Chain
papers.summary: Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiodic modulations. In this Letter, we uncover a family of topological quasiperiodic fixed points with critical scalings intermediate between the clean and infinite-randomness limits. By exactly solving the quasiperiodic cluster-Ising chain, we demonstrate that all phase boundaries separating quasiperiodically modulated phases are governed by topological Ising-like fixed points unique to strongly modulated quasiperiodic systems. Although their local bulk critical properties match those of conventional quasiperiodic Ising critical points reported before, these fixed points host robust topological edge degeneracies and exhibit a distinct symmetry-enriched realization of the quasiperiodic Ising criticality, as further supported by complementary lattice simulations.

papers.title: Quasi-flat and exact flat bands in patterned two-dimensional electron gases and honeycomb wire networks
papers.summary: We investigate the formation of flat bands in a two-dimensional electron gas patterned by a periodic triangular array of repulsive antidots. In the high-barrier, narrow-trench regime, the spectrum develops kagome-like band triplets, each comprising a nearly flat band and two dispersive bands, with wave functions concentrated along the potential-free trenches. The two lowest energy bands have a different character with graphene-like dispersion and wave functions localized near the junction centers. The appearance of the trench-concentrated nearly flat bands further motivates a honeycomb quantum graph model as an effective description of the narrow-trench limit. In the single-channel graph, destructive interference produces exact flat bands with compact localized eigenstates protected by the $D_3$ symmetry. Their energies obey a quantization condition determined by propagation along the links and scattering at the junctions. We then extend the analysis to a multichannel quantum graph and derive the most general junction scattering matrix compatible with $D_3$ symmetry. Even- and odd-parity transverse channels contain equivalent symmetry sectors, and $D_3$ symmetry therefore allows them to mix. This mode conversion can disrupt the destructive interference responsible for flat bands and generically gives those bands a finite width. Exact flatness is nevertheless retained when only one transverse-parity sector is active, or when an additional symmetry forbids mixing between the two sectors. These results connect the continuum antidot model to its quantum-graph limit and identify transverse-mode mixing as a mechanism that limits flatness in multichannel networks.

papers.title: Topologically Protected Surface Altermagnetism on Antiferromagnets
papers.summary: Altermagnetism (AM) and its associated spin-transport phenomena are typically linked to spin-split electronic band structures in bulk materials. However, the crystal surface has a reduced symmetry with respect to the bulk, which can induce AM at the surface of conventional antiferromagnets (AFMs) $\unicode{x2013}$ a local effect which cannot be detected using bulk properties. In this work we define the symmetry conditions necessary for surface AM and show how it can be topologically protected, rendering it a robust effect. We provide a minimal model for one trivial and two topological examples of surface AM. We show that the spin spectral density, accessible by spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, can exhibit a $d$-wave-like altermagnetic character at the surface, even when the full band structure is completely spin degenerate. Our topological model describes the Dirac semimetal CuMnAs, which provides an existing realization of our theory. Our results identify crystal surfaces as a platform to realize robust, topology- and symmetry-driven unconventional magnetism beyond the bulk classification of magnetic materials.

papers.title: Electromotive entrainment of charge and heat currents in graphene
papers.summary: We develop a hydrodynamic theory of charge and heat currents induced by traveling waves, such as surface acoustic waves, in graphene devices near charge neutrality. The currents depend on the intrinsic conductivity and viscosity of the electron liquid, the disorder strength, and the geometry of the device. We obtain analytic expressions for the heat and charge currents to second order in the wave amplitude for Hall-bar devices. At charge neutrality and in the absence of DC bias, the heat content is entrained by the wave in the absence of net charge transfer. At the same time, device conductance is enhanced by the wave. Away from charge neutrality, the transport charge current induced by the wave arises in the absence of a DC bias.

papers.title: Electronic correlations and dynamical screening with ab initio quantum embedding
papers.summary: First-principles descriptions of correlated quantum materials require a simultaneous treatment of strong local many-body effects and nonlocal dynamical screening. We present an efficient fully self-consistent implementation of $GW$+EDMFT that combines nonlocal correlations at the $GW$ level with a non-perturbative treatment of local correlations within extended dynamical mean-field theory (EDMFT), with a well-defined double-counting correction and a self-consistently determined impurity interaction. Self-consistency in both the Green's function and the dynamically screened interaction is essential for describing screening processes across energy scales. A key ingredient that makes it computationally feasible is the compression of two-particle correlation functions using interpolative separable density fitting (ISDF). Applying the scheme to the Mott insulator SrMnO$_3$ and the correlated metal LaNiO$_3$, we show that the self-consistent effective local interaction resolves the overscreening inherent to constrained-RPA approaches. For SrMnO$_3$, this stabilizes a Mott-insulating state in quantitative agreement with experiment, while for LaNiO$_3$ local EDMFT corrections yield a quasiparticle mass enhancement consistent with ARPES. These results establish fully self-consistent $GW$+EDMFT as a reliable \emph{ab initio} framework for strongly correlated quantum materials.

papers.title: Unified geometric formalism for dissipation and its fluctuations in finite-time microscopic heat engines
papers.summary: Microscopic heat engines operate in regimes where thermodynamic quantities fluctuate strongly, making stochastic effects an essential aspect of their performance. However, existing geometric formulations of finite-time thermodynamics primarily characterize average dissipation and do not systematically capture its fluctuations. Here, we develop a unified geometric framework that consistently describes both the mean dissipated availability and its fluctuations. In the linear-response regime, we show that these quantities are governed by metric tensors constructed from equilibrium correlation functions, providing a common geometric structure for dissipation and its fluctuations. This framework yields geometric bounds on both the mean and variance of the dissipated availability, and thereby on the efficiency and its fluctuations. The formalism applies broadly to stochastic systems, including Markov jump processes and overdamped and underdamped Brownian dynamics, establishing a unified geometric description across microscopic heat engines.

papers.title: Phonon number relaxation in a 3D superfluid with a concave acoustic branch
papers.summary: We consider the collisional evolution towards equilibrium of a spatially homogeneous and isotropic phonon gas of a three-dimensional superfluid with a concave acoustic excitation branch, at a non-zero but arbitrarily low temperature $T$. Three-phonon collisions $1\phi\leftrightarrow 2\phi$ are forbidden by conservation of energy-momentum. Four-phonon collisions $2\phi\to 2\phi$ of Landau and Khalatnikov lead, after a time $\propto T^{-7}$, only to a partial thermal equilibrium, a Bose law of non-zero chemical potential for the phonons, because they conserve the total number of phonons. Relaxation towards complete thermochemical equilibrium is therefore ensured by the much slower five-phonon collisions $2\phi\leftrightarrow 3\phi$ of Khalatnikov, in a time $\propto T^{-9}$. Using kinetic equations on the occupation numbers of the phonon modes and explicitly calculating the $2\phi\to 3\phi$ collisional amplitude with quantum hydrodynamics at low temperature, we determine the corresponding evolution of the fugacity $z_\phi$ of the phonon gas from the non-degenerate regime $z_\phi=0^+$ to complete equilibrium $z_\phi=1^-$. Using the conservation of total energy, we find that the fugacity varies with a non-integer power law $\propto t^{4/5}$ at short times and an exponential law at long times; the speed of change of entropy, always positive, is asymptotically proportional to the square of the speed of change of fugacity, $(\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}t)S_\phi\propto[(\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}t)z_\phi]^2$, as Landau predicted for an arbitrarily slow adiabatic transformation. Our results bring to a close the study initiated by Khalatnikov in 1950 and could be experimentally verified in a gas of cold spin-1/2 fermionic atoms in the sector of the BEC-BCS crossover where the acoustic branch has a concave start, or in superfluid liquid helium-4 at sufficiently high pressure.

papers.title: Quantized Collective Fluctuations in Correlated Fermion Systems
papers.summary: Collective excitations in fermionic systems play a crucial role in determining their physical properties. An important challenge is to develop efficient theoretical approaches for describing these excitations and their coupling to fermionic degrees of freedom. In this work, we revisit the problem of quantifying the contributions of individual bosonic modes of collective fluctuations to observable properties of correlated fermion systems within the framework of the Fluctuating Local Field (FLF) method. Whereas the auxiliary field in this method was previously considered only classically, we formulate its systematic extension termed Quantum FLF (Q-FLF) that incorporates selected bosonic Matsubara modes, thus tailoring it to description of quantum collective fluctuations. As a testbed, we apply the approach to a half-filled one-dimensional Hubbard chain and compute the Green's function, the total energy, and the antiferromagnetic susceptibility. Our results demonstrate that the proposed scheme enables an efficient and selective characterization of the contributions of individual bosonic modes. In particular, low Matsubara frequencies are found to have a quantitative impact on integrated observables such as total energy and antiferromagnetic susceptibility. At the same time, an accurate description of single-particle properties requires inclusion of higher-frequency bosonic modes.

papers.title: Vortex Dynamics Driven Transverse Transport in Superconducting Thin Films
papers.summary: The generation of transverse voltage in superconducting thin films carrying a longitudinal current has been recently related to demonstrate exotic, symmetry-breaking transport phenomena. To understand the underlying phenomenon we chose two distinctly different systems to investigate; a conventional (Nb) and a nonconventional (Ni/Bi bilayer) superconductor. A systematic study of this transverse response in these type-II superconducting thin films we aimed towards establishing its microscopic origin. Both longitudinal and transverse magneto transport measurements were carried out with Hall-bar patterned devices as a function of temperature with magnetic field applied out-of-plane. In both systems, a sharp, field antisymmetric transverse resistance emerges in the superconducting transition region, closely following the field derivative of the longitudinal resistance while it was vanishingly small or absent in the fully superconducting or normal states. Based on the vortex-flow model, the behavior could be quantitatively attributed as the transverse voltage arising due to the motion of Abrikosov vortices under a combined action of Magnus like force and viscous drag force, rather than from any exotic or intrinsic Hall-type mechanism. The close correspondence between a nominally conventional superconductor Nb and an unconventional superconductor heterostructure incorporating a ferromagnetic layer indicates that the vortex dynamics alone, independent of magnetic proximity effects or unconventional pairing, seems to be sufficient to account for the observed transverse signal. Our observations while seems to provide a quantitative, material-independent model for interpreting transverse voltages in superconducting films, raises the concerns in attributing such signals to exotic physics without first ruling out conventional vortex-flow contributions.

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved superconducting diode response
papers.summary: The superconducting diode effect manifests as nonreciprocal properties of critical currents, yet a systematic tensorial framework for its symmetry-governed responses remains lacking. We develop such a framework by relating the angular harmonics of critical currents to the magnetic field. Crystalline symmetries constrain the dipolar response to be purely antisymmetric (Hall-like) in Rashba superconductors with $C_{3v}$, $C_{4v}$, or $C_{6v}$ symmetry, whereas they require a diagonal, traceless tensor in Dresselhaus superconductors with $D_{2d}$ symmetry. For systems with fourfold symmetry, the octupole response appears at linear order, whose response tensors take symmetric off-diagonal and identity forms for $C_{4v}$ and $D_{2d}$ symmetries, respectively. Furthermore, nematicity activates otherwise forbidden tensor components, providing a sensitive probe of rotational symmetry breaking in superconductors. At cubic order in the magnetic field, the nonlinear response tensors likewise exhibit distinct symmetry-dependent patterns. Our framework establishes a symmetry-resolved characterization of the superconducting diode effect and provides a route to probing the underlying electronic structure and symmetry-breaking orders.

papers.title: Point-gap topology of damped magnon excitations in skyrmion strings
papers.summary: We theoretically study the non-Hermitian topology of magnons with finite lifetimes due to Gilbert damping. By incorporating the spin-wave theory and perturbation theory for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation including nonlocal damping terms, we analytically evaluate the spectral winding number for point gaps, which indicates the existence of the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). We find that, in noncollinear magnetic textures, the NHSE can occur even in the absence of nonlocal damping, due to the momentum-dependent mixing of the particle and hole components of magnon eigenmodes, which is absent in collinear magnets with a single magnon band. In the presence of nonlocal damping along one direction, we show that the winding number for an energy band with a unique minimum is determined from the sign of the wave number at the band minimum. We demonstrate these results using a model that hosts a skyrmion-string lattice as a steady state. We further investigate spin-wave propagation dynamics excited by a magnetic-field pulse and show that the propagation direction changes drastically from band to band depending on the presence of local and nonlocal damping, consistent with the nontrivial winding numbers.

papers.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
papers.summary: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy. In the absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC), this specific configuration perfectly suppresses both local Andreev reflection and direct electron tunneling (ET), thereby isolating and profoundly enhancing CAR. The introduction of Rashba SOC, however, induces spin-flip scattering that relaxes these strict selection constraints, yielding finite probabilities for competing scattering channels and subsequently reducing the overall CAR efficiency. Nevertheless, for SOC strengths below a critical threshold, CAR remains the dominant transport mechanism over ET. This proposed architecture provides a scalable, stray-field-free method to achieve purely electrostatic control over nonlocal transport, advancing the development of highly efficient superconducting spintronic devices.

papers.title: Revisiting spin Hamiltonian parameters in a Kitaev material via Bayesian optimization of magnetization curves
papers.summary: Determining the spin Hamiltonian of a magnetic compound is crucial for understanding its magnetic properties. A standard approach is to derive model parameters from ab initio calculations based on the crystal structure. However, the resulting Hamiltonian can depend sensitively on methodological details of the ab initio procedure. This issue is particularly evident in $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, a candidate Kitaev material. Here, we present an alternative, data-driven approach to determine the spin Hamiltonian parameters of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ by Bayesian optimization of experimental magnetization curves along the $b$- and $c$-axis directions. We optimize five parameters, namely the Kitaev interaction $K$, off-diagonal interactions $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$, the Heisenberg interaction $J$, and the $c$-axis $g$-factor $g_c$. The parameter set that minimizes the cost function is $(K,\Gamma,\Gamma',J,g_c)=(-6.0, 7.5, -0.3, -1.75, 2.3)$, where the exchange couplings are in meV. We find that the cost function is insensitive to the absolute value of the Kitaev coupling $K$. Thus, the magnetization data alone do not determine its energy scale. The cost function also depends only weakly on $\Gamma'$ and $J$, while the optimization favors a large positive $\Gamma$. By computing the static spin structure factor, magnetic susceptibility, and specific heat, we show that these quantities favor the large-$\Gamma$ scenario over the small-$g_c$ scenario and that the parameter set that minimizes the cost function yields good agreement with the experimental structure factor and susceptibility, and qualitative agreement with the specific heat. The combination of Bayesian optimization and accurate low-energy solvers provides an effective approach for determining parameters of spin Hamiltonians. This methodology opens a systematic route to determining spin Hamiltonians in quantum magnets from experimental data.

papers.title: Gaussian-Bond Hall Viscosity and Nonlocal Hall Response of a Sampled Landau Level
papers.summary: Hall viscosity on a lattice depends on how strain changes microscopic hopping amplitudes. For a specified Gaussian envelope, bond-length derivatives close on the undeformed hopping, expressing the stress as an embedded momentum Hessian and relating the viscosity to higher-order band geometry. The density-normalized viscosity approaches the continuum value 1/4, with an exponentially small sampling correction at finite flux. By contrast, for a straight-bond Peierls source, a low-frequency mass, and a fixed-envelope susceptibility, the viscosity--conductivity comparison exhibits an algebraic deviation, whose leading coefficient follows from a weak-field expansion.

papers.title: Sustainability-Aware Discovery of Dual-Atom Hydrogen Evolution Catalysts via a Unified Machine Learning Framework for Activity and Carbon Cost
papers.summary: Catalyst discovery for green hydrogen has optimized activity alone, deferring economic and environmental costs to stages where they disqualify otherwise promising candidates. Here we introduce a unified machine learning framework that screens catalytic activity and monetized carbon cost in a single pipeline. A machine learning potential predicts hydrogen evolution activity and stability at density-functional-theory accuracy. A second model, trained on published estimates of the social cost of carbon, converts each candidate's embodied CO2 into a monetary burden. Screening 460 graphene-supported dual-atom catalysts across 23 transition metals and 20 nitrogen-coordination motifs yields 26 active, synthesizable candidates. The two axes then conflict. The most active candidates span Mn-, Fe-, Zr-, Cr-, Cu-, Ni-, Ti-, Nb-, V-, Pd-, Au-, and Rh-based catalysts, indistinguishable in adsorption energy yet spanning a 58,000-fold range in carbon cost. Joint optimization selects Mn2@2Nf and Zr2@2Nc, matching the best precious-metal activity at tens-of-thousands-fold lower carbon cost, independent of catalyst loading.

papers.title: Slave-rotor theory of correlated altermagnets on the Lieb lattice
papers.summary: We investigate the metal-insulator transition driven by the onsite repulsive interaction $U$ in an altermagnetic Hubbard model defined on a Lieb lattice. Using the slave-rotor approach at half-filling, we find that the system exhibits a cascade of interaction-driven phase transitions. As $U$ increases, the system evolves from a normal metal to an altermagnetic metal, then to an altermagnetic insulator, and eventually to an altermagnetic Mott insulator characterized by the complete suppression of the quasiparticle weight. These phases are supported by the calculation of the electronic spectral function, which features spin-split bands in both the metallic and insulating regimes. However, the spin splitting becomes substantially suppressed in the Mott-insulating phase. Our results suggest that the observation of spin splitting in the spectral function of $d$-wave altermagnets with a Lieb-lattice-like structure may be limited to the weak-to-moderate correlation regime.

papers.title: Dichotomous electronic system in a bilayer Ni$^{1+}$ nickelate
papers.summary: "Infinite layer" nickelates ${\cal R}$NiO$_2$ (${\cal R}$=rare earth), having empty apical O sites, become superconducting upon hole doping, stimulating research into the related sequence Nd$_{n+1}$Ni$^{+p}_n$O$_{2n+2}$, formal charge state $p$=1+$\frac{1}{n}$, $n$=2,3,4,...., with the $n$=5 member being found to be superconducting. The two layer system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_{7-\delta}$, with $\delta$=0,$\frac{1}{2}$,1 ($p$=2.5,2,1.5) approaches the peak in the nickelate superconducting dome but shows no superconductivity. Newly reported La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_5$F reaches the Ni$^{1+}$ goal while, as we show, introducing a partially occupied electron band $E^*$, based on an interstitial density that extends over the three open "apical" layers and leads to a single cylindrical electron Fermi surface giving self-doping. The commonly inert Ni $d_{xz},d_{yz}$ orbitals partner with interstitial $E^*$ to provide an incipient non-analytic Dirac point, with the critical point being reachable by pressure or further F insertion. The $E^*$ electron cylinder and the conventional Ni $dp\sigma$ hole carriers combine to provide a two-fluid dichotomy of hole and electron quasiparticles, affecting normal state properties that should verify the dichotomous aspect of transport.

papers.title: Bidirectional motion of antiferromagnetic skyrmions driven by competing spin torques
papers.summary: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are swirling topological spin textures with rich dynamics and intriguing transport properties, yet their bidirectional dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the dynamics of antiferromagnetic skyrmions driven by current-induced spin-transfer and spin-orbit torques. We computationally demonstrate that antiferromagnetic skyrmions moving in one direction at low current densities can reverse their motion direction when the driving current is above a threshold. Based on the Thiele approach analysis, we show that this bidirectional motion originates from a change in the relative strengths of two effective forces arising from spin-transfer and spin-orbit torques. Furthermore, exploiting this bidirectional motion on a single racetrack, we design programmable logic gates. Our results not only uncover a hidden mechanism for bidirectional skyrmion motion but also facilitate the development of antiferromagnet-based logic devices.

papers.title: Magnetic Field Control of the N\'eel Vector and Magnon Visibility in Altermagnetic MnTe
papers.summary: Altermagnetic order gives rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting of electronic and magnonic excitations even in the absence of a net magnetization. Here, we investigate the magnetic field dependence of the spin-wave spectrum of altermagnetic $\alpha$-MnTe using inelastic neutron scattering and linear spin-wave theory. An in-plane magnetic field continuously reorients the N\'eel vector by overcoming the weak crystalline anisotropy, while remaining small compared with the dominant exchange scale. We find that this reorientation leaves the magnon energies and line widths essentially unchanged, but strongly modifies the measured spectral intensity through the transverse-momentum projection. Our results demonstrate a clear separation between the soft orientational degree of freedom of the antiferromagnetic order and the robust exchange-dominated chiral magnon spectrum. This combination establishes $\alpha$-MnTe as a platform for reconfigurable magnon coupling, in which external fields tune how excitations interact with polarized probes without substantially altering their frequency or coherence.

papers.title: Quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4
papers.summary: We show the emergence of a quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4 obeying Boltzmann statistics, in the absence of atomic exchange. Using path integral centroid molecular dynamics simulations over 0.1-3.3 K and 1-60 bar, we investigate the transport properties of two distinct liquid states: the low quantum dispersion liquid (LQDL) and the high quantum dispersion liquid (HQDL). While LQDL exhibits conventional liquid behavior consistent with the Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation, HQDL emerges at lower temperatures and displays anomalous gas-like transport characterized by superdiffusion and ultralow viscosity, accompanied by a breakdown of the SE relation. This counterintuitive emergence of gas-like dynamics upon cooling reflects the dominant role of nuclear quantum fluctuations, in contrast to thermal fluctuations at higher temperatures. Across the LQDL-HQDL boundary, we identify a transport crossover marked by a qualitative change in the velocity autocorrelation function (VAF), a transition in the Prandtl number, and the emergence of transport minima in shear and kinematic viscosities, thermal conductivity, and thermal diffusivity. These minima reflect a crossover from liquid-like to gas-like transport upon cooling in the low-temperature subcritical region, in addition to the universal transport minima observed in the supercritical regime. The transition from oscillatory to monotonic VAF defines a second Frenkel line, distinct from the conventional Frenkel line observed in the supercritical region. LQDL is a heat-transport-dominated dissipative fluid, whereas HQDL is a momentum-dominated inertial fluid. These results demonstrate that nuclear quantum fluctuations alone induce gas-like liquid behavior and provide a unified picture of transport phenomena in distinguishable helium-4 without superfluidity.

papers.title: Crystal forming ability of amorphous refractory metals under nanoindentation: a molecular dynamics study
papers.summary: Amorphous refractory metal coatings combine high hardness with chemical inertness, yet their metastability makes them prone to mechanically induced crystallisation (devitrification) under contact loading, and how readily such a glass re-orders to its parent body centred cubic (bcc) crystal is unknown across the refractory series. We prepared amorphous V, Nb, Mo, Ta and W by melt quenching to 300 K, benchmarked each interatomic potential against ab initio liquid radial distribution functions and self-diffusion coefficients, and probed them by large scale molecular dynamics nanoindentation. Indentation drives a localised amorphous to bcc transformation by bulk nucleation, growth and coalescence. A crystal forming ability (CFA), the maximum slope of the sigmoidal bcc fraction versus depth curve, spans about a factor of four and decreases as V > Mo > Nb > Ta > W; it falls with indenter velocity as CFA scales as v^(-m), with a mean exponent of 1.08, so CFA.v is nearly constant and the transformation rate is almost velocity independent. Transforming atoms carry excess non affine displacement and local shear strain, not hydrostatic pressure, marking a shear associated displacive pathway; the bulk driving force is largest for the most resistant element, W, so resistance tracks cohesive bond strength rather than the thermodynamic driving force. Early bcc like order correlates with the sharpness and depth of the transition, whereas the mechanical work to half transformation correlates with the peak density of persistent bcc clusters. A cluster population balance links nucleation, growth and coalescence to a terminal microstructure whose completeness does not follow the CFA order.

papers.title: EBSD and Subtle Crystallographic Differences - A Study of Resolving Interlayer Spacings in Nb-Ni and Nb-Co mu-phases
papers.summary: In ordered intermetallics, slight variations in lattice site occupancy and specific interlayer spacings have been identified as the sources of significant changes in critical resolved shear stress and therefore how a given phase may affect alloy properties. So far, atom positions and lattice site occupancies have traditionally been characterised by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), which are methods that offer either local detail or high statistical significance but not both. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), by contrast, provides high spatial resolution across large sample areas and therefore, has the potential to enable the local investigation of interlayer spacing and site lattice occupancy with improved statistical reliability. The objectives of the study are to benchmark EBSDs capability for resolving these subtle features and to correlate them with compositional and mechanical properties. In this case study, we therefore show that EBSD can resolve key crystallographic features of mu-phase intermetallics, specifically interlayer spacings. We combine pattern matching with large-scale dynamical simulations of template libraries guided by XRD based information on lattice parameters. For this, we generate structures that vary in the spacing between triple-layer and Kagome layer and in the site lattice occupancy of the 3a site. This approach successfully predicts the change of interlayer spacing between Kagome and triple layers in Nb-Co and Nb-Ni mu-phases, in good agreement with XRD and HR-TEM.

papers.title: Thermal Hall Signatures of Distinct Schwinger-Boson Flux Sectors on the Honeycomb Lattice
papers.summary: Thermal transport offers a bulk probe of charge-neutral excitations in frustrated magnets. It remains challenging, however, to determine whether such transport can distinguish different parton mean-field structures of the same spin system. This question is particularly relevant on the honeycomb lattice, where distinct $0$-flux, $\pi$-flux, and chiral $\pi/2$-flux sectors have been proposed. In this paper, we compare self-consistent saddle-point solutions in these three sectors for a frustrated $J_1-J_2$ Heisenberg model with a next-nearest-neighbor Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and a perpendicular magnetic field. Using finite-temperature Schwinger-boson mean-field theory and the Kubo formula for bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes systems, we evaluate the intrinsic spinon thermal Hall conductivity. At a common parameter point where all three branches remain gapped, the $0$-flux response is positive and the $\pi$-flux response is negative for $D>0$ and $h>0$ under the sign conventions used in this paper, whereas the $\pi/2$-flux response changes sign with increasing temperature. We further show that a projective symmetry combining a sixfold rotation with time reversal forces the zero-field response of a fixed chiral $\pi/2$-flux domain to vanish. Within the mean-field regime examined in this paper, the sign and temperature dependence of $\kappa_{xy}/T$ therefore provide a flux-sensitive transport signature.

papers.title: Decoding Oxygen K-edge Fingerprints of NCM-811 Degradation via Ab Initio Many-Body Theory and High-Throughput Screening of Crystal Proxies
papers.summary: The degradation of LiNi$_{0.8}$Co$_{0.1}$Mn$_{0.1}$O$_2$ (NCM-811) in Li-ion batteries produces complex transition-metal oxides and binary phases that fundamentally limit cathode performance. While identifying these degradation products via X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is essential for mitigating electrochemical performance loss, interpretation remains challenging due to the structural complexity of real-world samples. In this work, we present an integrated theoretical-experimental framework combining high-resolution oxygen K-edge XAS with \textit{ab initio} simulations based on many-body perturbation theory and high-throughput screening from density functional theory. We first evaluate the spectroscopic fingerprints of eight layered, spinel, and nominal rock-salt reference oxides, identifying discrepancies between the idealized single-crystal bulk phase and experimental spectra. Using high-throughput screening to analyze the oxygen $p$-projected density of states of 38 distinct polymorphs of NiO, CoO, and MnO, we propose that the spectral differences can emerge, among other factors, from local structural variations represented here by simplified structural proxies. Our work establishes a viable and rigorous computational pathway to interpret the complex landscape of degraded battery materials.

papers.title: Sequential Retrieval in Dense Associative Memory: Asymptotic Dynamics and Storage Capacity
papers.summary: We study the retrieval dynamics of an $n$-body asymmetric dense associative memory model, in which sequential retrieval is implemented by shifting one pattern index in the higher-order Hebbian interaction. The model exhibits sequential retrieval of the stored patterns, and the retrieval state corresponds to a stable limit-cycle attractor. The storage capacity is defined as the maximum loading rate for which this limit cycle remains stable. Using generating functional analysis, we derive the dynamical equations describing the sequential retrieval state. The generating functional analysis reveals that the retarded self-interaction term vanishes in the asymmetric model, and the resulting overlap dynamics is reproduced by an Amari-Maginu-type signal-to-noise analysis. Also, we find that for the interaction order $n\ge 3$, the normalized storage capacity decreases monotonically with increasing interaction order, in contrast to symmetric Modern Hopfield models.

papers.title: A Solvable Model in the Half-filled Landau Level
papers.summary: A solvable microscopic model of interacting electrons in a half-filled Landau level is presented. The Hamiltonian is a well-defined limit of the electron-electron interaction. The low energy sector consists of a set of independent, spatially interlaced, one-dimensional systems of non-interacting fermionic dipoles, each system with a Fermi sea ground state. The total number of dipoles in the set of Fermi seas forming the two-dimensional ground state equals the number of electrons in the system and the density of states at the Fermi level is that of a two-dimensional Fermi gas. The model is obtained by generalizing, or rather adopting, the existing exact solution on a thin, but not too thin, torus to the two-dimensional bulk case.

papers.title: A Hierarchy of Exact Lower Bounds on the Laughlin Spectral Gap
papers.summary: We develop a bootstrap approach to deriving lower bounds on the spectral gap of the first Haldane pseudopotential Hamiltonian on the sphere with $N_\Phi$ flux quanta for arbitrary $N_\Phi$, including in the thermodynamic limit $N_\Phi \to \infty$. This method can in principle be generalized to pseudopotentials describing other model wavefunctions such as the Moore--Read state or Read--Rezayi sequence. Our approach is based on Knabe's observation that if $H$ is a Hamiltonian with ground state energy zero then the spectral gap is at least $\epsilon > 0$ if and only if $H^2 \succeq \epsilon H$. To show this inequality, we split $H^2$ into two parts, one that can be analytically bounded and another that can be bounded using a finite semidefinite program (SDP). Crucially, the size of this program is determined only by cutoff parameters, and the program depends on $N_\Phi$ only parametrically, allowing us to obtain numerically exact (up to solver precision) lower bounds on the gap. In order to turn these numerical bounds into mathematically rigorous results, we introduce an algorithm that can produce nearly-optimal exact interior feasible points for large rational SDPs even if the affine constraints are highly redundant and ill-conditioned. We additionally provide an algorithm that establishes the rank stability of the SDP in the $N_\Phi \to \infty$ limit, which is needed to certify the bound in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond establishing a Laughlin gap greater than $1/100$ in the thermodynamic limit and revealing a potential method for deriving spectral gap lower bounds for other pseudopotentials, our work provides a general method for turning numerical SDP bounds into rigorous mathematical proofs, which may have wide applicability. In particular, this work demonstrates that bootstrap methods can be used to rigorously resolve major open problems in quantum many-body physics.

papers.title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
papers.summary: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

papers.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
papers.summary: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

papers.title: Extremal and global-time statistics of sluggish random walks with stochastic resetting
papers.summary: We study a sluggish random walk, whose diffusivity decreases as a power law with distance from the origin, under Poissonian resetting to the origin. Using a mapping to a signed Bessel process and renewal theory, we obtain exact results for the maximum trajectory value in a finite window, the time at which it occurs, and the time of the last visit to the origin. Resetting changes the growth of the typical maximum from a power law in time to a power of its logarithm. The centered maximum approaches a Gumbel law, whose width shrinks in physical space for any positive sluggishness exponent, unlike the Brownian case. In the Bessel coordinate, the probability that the maximum exceeds a value growing in proportion to the observation window length decays exponentially, with a rate that has a second-order dynamical transition and is independent of sluggishness. The time of the maximum is uniform in the bulk, with boundary layers that shift its mean above the midpoint logarithmically with window length. The time since the last visit to the origin follows a Gamma law with a sluggishness-dependent shape. Reflection symmetry makes the last-visit time uncorrelated with the occupation time of the positive half-line.

papers.title: Many-Body Bound States in the Continuum
papers.summary: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is a spatially localized energy eigenstate embedded in a continuous spectrum of extended eigenstates. While diverse types of single-particle BICs have been reported in the literature, understanding how such localization persists in interacting many-body systems remains a fundamental problem. Here, we present numerical evidence and a perturbative analysis supporting the existence of many-body BICs in a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard chain with an attractive impurity potential, a system previously known to host a BIC in the two-particle sector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Bethe-type construction of the known two-particle BIC breaks down already for three particles even for arbitrary finite superpositions of Bethe waves. The resulting BICs violate the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis for several local one- and two-body observables, leading to nonthermal dynamics from experimentally accessible initial states.

papers.title: Nonstabilizerness as a diagnostic of criticality and exceptional points in non-Hermitian spin chains
papers.summary: We investigate nonstabilizerness, also known as ``magic,'' to understand criticality and exceptional points in non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems. Our focus is on parity-time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric spin chains, specifically the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising and XX models. We calculate stabilizer R\'enyi entropies in their ground states using non-Hermitian matrix product state methods. Our findings show that magic exhibits unique and model-specific signs of phase transitions. In the Ising chain, it peaks near the regular Hermitian-like critical line but disappears across exceptional points. In contrast, in the XX chain, it reaches its maximum at the exceptional line where $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry is broken. Finite-size scaling reveals that these effects become more pronounced with larger systems, highlighting nonstabilizerness as a sensitive marker for both quantum criticality and non-Hermitian spectral degeneracies. We also investigate magic in momentum space for the XX model analytically and find that it reaches a minimum around exceptional points. Our results indicate that magic takes extremal values at the exceptional points and serves as a valuable tool for examining complexity, criticality, and symmetry breaking in non-Hermitian quantum matter.

papers.title: Simple slow operators and quantum thermalization
papers.summary: We establish a rigorous operator-space condition for the thermalization of typical initial states. We introduce a concept of simple slow operators (SSOs), defined as operators that evolve slowly under Heisenberg-picture dynamics and have significant small-sized components. We show that the non-thermalization of typical initial states drawn from a weakly entangled state ensemble implies the existence of SSOs; equivalently, the absence of SSOs implies that typical initial states thermalize. We establish these results by introducing the concept of an ensemble variance norm of an operator, defined as the typical magnitude of the expectation value of that operator with respect to states in the ensemble. For low-entanglement ensembles, the norm is related to operator sizes, allowing us to establish a direct link between operator dynamics and thermalization.

papers.title: Operator space transport in collective spin Lindbladians
papers.summary: Boundary time crystals (BTCs) are paradigmatic examples of continuous time crystals that emerge in collective, dissipative quantum systems. Their microscopic origin, however, remains obscured by the complexity of Lindbladian many-body dynamics and has largely been investigated through semiclassical and numerical approaches. Here, we develop an exact operator space framework for collective spin Lindbladians based on irreducible tensor representations. We map the Lindbladian dynamics onto a local non-Hermitian hopping problem, where weak symmetries impose selection rules on operator transport, while the hopping amplitudes and their relative strengths determine the resulting dynamical regimes. We identify the microscopic ingredients that distinguish models supporting conventional collective precession from those supporting BTC dynamics. Our approach further reveals how non-unital dissipation can provide a source for the traceless operator subspace, providing a microscopic mechanism for the reduced sensitivity of BTC dynamics to initial conditions beyond mean-field descriptions. More broadly, our results establish operator space transport as a general perspective for understanding dissipative many-body dynamics and its connections to non-Hermitian phenomena.

papers.title: Where solitons are in a KdV soliton gas
papers.summary: The Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) equation is a paradigmatic model of integrable classical fields, with solitonic solutions where localised profiles interact by elastic, factorised scattering. When solitons interact, their shapes are modified, and individual solitons cannot be identified. This is a key problem in soliton gas where one needs a density of solitons per unit distance: can we locate asymptotic objects, quasiparticles, even at finite times in the macroscopic limit? Quasiparticles' positions should satisfy locality properties, the field in mesoscopic regions being determined by quasiparticles lying there. We solve this problem for the KdV equation. We define solitons' positions as functions of spectral and impact parameters via an expansion bijection generalising that of hard rods. These ``KdV rods'' solve the semiclassical Bethe equations, implementing the collision rate ansatz, and satisfy a repulsion condition generalising the rods' lengths to the KdV scattering shifts and related to the condensate condition. This gives an explicit characterisation of multi-soliton fields in terms of solitons' positions instead of impact parameters. We construct fluid-cell projections, that project out solitons lying outside mesoscopic regions: the resulting field is unchanged in this region and supported there up to small corrections. We show that in the weak limit, conserved densities are given by the empirical density for these solitons' positions. Thus we have associated a kinetic theory of quasiparticles to the KdV equation. The results hold under natural assumptions on spectral and impact parameters, and no randomness is required. Our proof is based on novel solitonic tau functions. This is a crucial step towards rigorously deriving the kinetic equation of the KdV soliton gas, first proposed by Gennady El in 2003. We believe the methods are generalisable to other solitonic models.

papers.title: Boundary-Canceled Score-Hamiltonian Sampling
papers.summary: Diffusion sampling is related to imaginary-time quantum annealing through a forward/backward Schr\"odinger equation pair and its one-sided counterdiabatic connection. For a smooth, gapped Score-Hamiltonian path, the exact connection transports the target density at any evolution time. We apply quantum-annealing performance analysis to residuals from approximating this connection with a trained score. If the first $r$ terminal schedule derivatives vanish, the squared Hellinger error scales as $T^{-2r-2}$, with a prefactor determined by the terminal learning residual and inverse gaps. Direct two-dimensional imaginary-time evolution with one fixed neural score reproduces these powers and prefactors. Terminal schedule design thus suppresses the distributional effect of imperfect score learning without retraining the network.

papers.title: Walshness: an intrinsic neural-network representability metric for quantum states
papers.summary: Neural quantum states (NQS) have emerged as powerful representations of quantum states with rapidly expanding applications across quantum many-body physics. Yet our understanding of when neural networks can efficiently represent physical quantum states remains limited, in part due to the nonlinear parameterization of NQS, the intricate sign structure of quantum states, and the sensitive dependence on basis choice. We introduce Walshness, a complexity metric of a quantum state which quantifies whether it admits a compact neural-network representation. We rigorously prove that a general quantum many-body state admits an efficient NQS representation if it has bounded Walshness, and vice versa, for various NQS architectures. We provide an algorithm for finding the optimal basis by minimizing the energy of a corresponding classical spin model. This allows us to empirically improve the learnability of various physical quantum states, including ground states of the transverse-field Ising model and mixed-field toric code, often reducing infidelity by orders of magnitude, and generalizes the basis choice given by the well-known Marshall sign rule in frustrated antiferromagnets. Our results provide an intrinsic complexity metric for quantum states with provable connections to their neural-network representability.

papers.title: Topological Superradiant Universality Classes in Cavity-Mediated Spin Chains
papers.summary: Superradiant phase transitions are fundamental phenomena in light-matter coupled systems. Here, we uncover a novel class of superradiant criticality that is topologically distinct from previously known superradiant transitions. Using cavity-mediated cluster-Ising chains as an illustrative example, we numerically demonstrate that the critical line separating the superradiant phase from the cavity topological phase hosts robust symmetry-protected edge degeneracies, a feature absent in conventional superradiant transitions. Remarkably, although its local bulk critical properties are indistinguishable from those of the previously identified topologically trivial superradiant transition, the two criticalities cannot be smoothly connected without breaking the protecting symmetries or passing through a multicritical point. We further show that such topological superradiant criticality is generic, also occurring in cavity-mediated $\mathbb{Z}_{n}^{}$ cluster-qudit chains, as supported by complementary lattice simulations.

papers.title: Acceleration data-based robust on-board monitoring of hunting proximity in railway vehicles under uncertainty: A feasibility study
papers.summary: The feasibility of on-board, real-time proximity assessment to railway hunting initiation under uncertainty arising from vehicle/track and other operational conditions is assessed. In this context, a novel method that classifies hunting proximity into one of several prespecified speed proximity intervals is introduced, based on a grey nonlinear vehicle model with parameters estimated from on-board acceleration measurements and model-based estimation of the Maximum Lyapunov Exponent (MLE) as a hunting proximity measure. The method's performance and robustness are assessed via Monte Carlo simulations using a MATLAB-based multi-body vehicle model and four operating scenarios. The method is shown to achieve excellent performance achieving 97.08 % classification accuracy, which marks a significant improvement over a potential alternative. Its robustness to faulty suspensions and hollow-worn wheels is also demonstrated, although certain performance compromise is observed under worn-track conditions.
