papers.title: Efficient Localization of Directional Emitters via Joint Beampattern Estimation
papers.summary: Localization methods designed for omnidirectional emitters degrade on directional sources, where directive beampatterns induce pronounced received signal strength (RSS) modulations. We present a direct position determination (DPD) approach that augments standard angle of arrival (AOA) and time difference of arrival (TDOA) measurements with RSS modulation to jointly estimate emitter position and beampattern parameters. Two algorithms reduce the four-dimensional search to two dimensions: a block coordinate ascent (BCA) method that alternates between position and beampattern subproblems, and a profile likelihood method that concentrates the beampattern parameters out via a generalized eigenvalue solve, a weighted least squares fit, and Newton refinement on the constrained Rayleigh quotient. We derive the Cram\'er--Rao lower bound (CRLB) and benchmark against an AOA-TDOA baseline and a prior-art approach that assumes known beamwidth and estimates only the orientation. The profile likelihood method approaches the CRLB, substantially outperforms all baselines at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and remains robust under model mismatch with the assumed von Mises template. A sensitivity analysis shows performance peaks when receivers lie on the main-lobe edges where RSS gradients are maximized.

papers.title: A Benchmark Library for Distributed Power System Analysis and Optimization
papers.summary: DPLib is an open-source benchmark library created to support research and development in distributed power system analysis and optimization. Unlike centralized tools such as MATPOWER and PGLib, no general purpose, reproducible data library package currently exists for distributed power system studies. DPLib, available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DPLib.git}{GitHub}, fills this gap by providing 40 multi-region benchmark test cases ranging from 5 buses to 20758 buses, along with a graph-based partitioning toolkit that converts MATPOWER-compatible systems into distributed regional datasets. The toolkit generates standardized \texttt{.mat}, \texttt{.csv}, and \texttt{.m} files, regional MATPOWER version 2 cases, local and global bus mappings, generator and cost assignments, explicit inter-regional tie-line records, and bus-to-region partition maps. It supports unweighted, electrically weighted, and user-defined partitions, and is compared with METIS, KaFFPa, and an IPA-inspired baseline. DPLib also provides ADMM-based distributed DC and AC OPF solvers for validation. Numerical studies report partitioning sensitivity, centralized run times, distributed OPF iterations, run times, and optimality gaps. These results establish DPLib as a reproducible data layer for distributed power system research.

papers.title: Optimal transmit field distribution for partially obstructed continuous radiating surfaces in near-field communication systems
papers.summary: This paper deals with the optimal synthesis of aperture fields for (radiating) near-field communications in obstructed environments. A physically consistent model based on knife-edge diffraction is used to formulate the problem as a maximization in Hilbert space. The optimal solution is obtained as a matched filter that ``matches" the shape of a diffraction-induced kernel, thus linking wave propagation with signal processing methods. The framework supports hardware implementation using continuous apertures such as metasurfaces or lens antennas. This approach bridges physically grounded modeling, signal processing, and hardware design for efficient energy focusing in near-field obstructed channels.

papers.title: Control and Stability of a Multilevel Power System for a Future Distribution Network
papers.summary: The growing integration of renewable energy sources into distribution networks poses significant challenges to frequency and voltage stability due to their intermittent nature and low-inertia dynamics. This paper proposes a multilevel control framework for a future decarbonized power system, using energy storage systems as power buffers to mitigate frequency and voltage fluctuations. A nonlinear interconnected model is formulated to describe the multilevel aggregated dynamics of the distribution network. To reduce the operational complexity and communication overhead of the control system, a distributed linear quadratic regulator strategy is developed based on bottom-up information exchange, where each level implements local feedback control over a short time horizon. Local stability conditions are established for the open-loop nonlinear model, and the closed-loop stability is characterized by the Hurwitz property of the system matrix. Performance bounds are also derived to quantify the gap between the distributed and centralized control strategies.

papers.title: Stealthy bias injection attack detection based on Kullback-Leibler divergence in noisy linear systems
papers.summary: This paper studies the design of observer gains to enhance the detectability of stealthy bias injection attacks (BIAs) in linear systems driven by Gaussian noise, where adversaries compromise a subset of sensors and exploit system dynamics and noise to remain stealthy. We formulate the observer-gain design as a max-min optimization problem that enhances the detectability of the least detectable BIAs, with detectability measured by the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) subject to a prescribed attack impact. To reduce the computational complexity of the derived non-convex design problem, we consider attack onset, one-step, and steady-state detectability. We show that the Kalman filter is optimal at attack onset regardless of the subset of attacked sensors. For the one-step and steady-state cases, the observer gain design problems are approximated by bi-convex optimization problems, which can be efficiently solved using alternating optimization (AO) and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Moreover, more tractable linear matrix inequality (LMI) relaxations are developed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed stealth-aware detection framework is demonstrated through an application to a thermal system.

papers.title: Integrated Spoofing-Robust Automatic Speaker Verification via a Three-Class Formulation and LLR
papers.summary: Spoofing-robust automatic speaker verification (SASV) aims to integrate automatic speaker verification (ASV) and countermeasure (CM). A popular solution is fusion of independent ASV and CM scores. To better modeling SASV, some frameworks integrate ASV and CM within a single network. However, these solutions are typically bi-encoder based, offer limited interpretability, and cannot be readily adapted to new evaluation parameters without retraining. Based on this, we propose a unified end-to-end framework via a three-class formulation that enables log-likelihood ratio (LLR) inference from class logits for a more interpretable decision pipeline. Experiments show comparable performance to existing methods on ASVSpoof5 and better results on SpoofCeleb. The visualization and analysis also prove that the three-class reformulation provides more interpretability.

papers.title: Unsupervised Learning for Scalable Downlink Power Control in Cell-Free Massive MIMO
papers.summary: In cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output systems, downlink power control is essential to ensure uniformly high service quality across users. Existing solutions range from computationally demanding centralized optimization to scalable distributed schemes with limited fairness. This letter proposes an unsupervised, physics-informed framework that directly optimizes max-min fairness without optimal labels or user position information. The method scales with the number of UEs, requires no retraining when the number of UEs changes, and admits a fully scalable extension. Numerical results show that it nearly doubles the worst-user spectral efficiency over existing scalable schemes.

papers.title: Revisiting Certainty Equivalence: The Structural Coupling Between Estimation and Control in Underactuated Nonlinear Systems
papers.summary: The certainty equivalence (CE) principle underpins a wide range of control architectures by enabling the separation of estimation and control design. While this property holds for linear systems, its validity in nonlinear settings remains limited and often implicitly assumed. This paper revisits CE from a nonlinear perspective, showing that estimated states induce an intrinsic coupling between estimation and tracking dynamics. By analyzing the closed-loop system in tracking-error coordinates, we demonstrate that nonlinear state dependence gives rise to higher-order interaction terms during aggressive transients. Motivated by this limitation, we propose an estimation-aware (EA) control paradigm that incorporates estimation quality into the feedback law to isolate estimation-induced loops. The formulation remains filtering-agnostic while preserving general applicability to smooth, underactuated nonlinear systems. We derive analytical conditions guaranteeing bounded tracking under uncertainty, validating the framework under high-fidelity quadrotor flight simulation along complex 3D trajectories at speeds up to 57.6 km/h. Frequency-domain evaluations demonstrate that the EA law extends tracking bandwidth by 39% and improves stability margins by up to 55%, effectively mitigating severe cross-couplings to offer a robust alternative to classical CE-based designs.

papers.title: Programmable Sequential Memory in Coupled Oscillator Networks
papers.summary: The Hopfield network established that static memories can be stored as energy minima of an energy-based model. Real intelligent agents, however, must navigate sequences of memories rather than isolatedcsnapshots. Biological cortex addresses this through a separation of timescales, where fast synaptic dynamics encode individual states while slow neuromodulatory processes govern transitions between them. Inspired by this organization, we propose a sequential memory architecture that is fully continuous and admits exponential storage capacity. The architecture is programmable, since the transition structure is carried by a mechanism that is decoupled from the stored patterns, driven by the input context, and free to be chosen, optimized, or learned from data. Specifically, we construct an autonomous three-timescale dynamical system with three coupled layers. A fast Kuramoto layer stores phase patterns as exponentially stable phase-locked configurations, an intermediate recognition layer sets the dwell times, and a slow attention layer routes the transitions. We analyze the stability, dwell time, and capacity of the system, and we validate the dynamics through numerical simulations of sequential memory retrieval.

papers.title: Smoothing the Ramp, Not the Peak: Scheduling-Induced Power Dynamics of LLM Inference and Their Grid-Scale Consequences
papers.summary: Large language model inference serving is a fast-growing electricity load whose power dynamics remain uncharacterized from a grid-planning perspective. Using real, measured GPU power traces, we show that chunked prefill scheduling, a latency-motivated technique already deployed by default in production LLM serving, is a controllable knob that regulates power ramp rate without touching peak power. Contrary to the intuitive hypothesis that splitting a long prompt's computation into smaller steps should flatten its power spike, peak power stays relatively the same while mean ramp rate falls substantially. Critically, this ramp-rate benefit is not a fixed property of the policy: it grows monotonically with system saturation, and we confirm this along two independent axes: concurrency and long-prompt request load (from near zero at low whale incidence to 39.6% at high whale fraction/size). We translate this single-GPU mechanism into an operational grid quantity, regulation-reserve procurement, posed and solved as a chance-constrained problem using a model-free bootstrap directly resampling real measured power traces. For independently operating servers, chunked prefill reduces the fast-ramping reserve requirement by an estimated 24% at heavy load (95% CIs within 13-34%) and 12% at moderate load, consistently across reliability levels from 95% to 99.9%. Repeated with 100 trials per policy on two-GPU tensor-parallel deployments, the reduction is about 36% for a dense 14B model and 10% for a sparse mixture-of-experts model. The benefit holds for ramps resolved at up to 2 s and persists at a reduced 16-20% when servers' load changes are synchronized. Together, these results identify a no-cost lever for fast-timescale demand shaping that is available today, whose benefit is largest when data centers run hottest.

papers.title: Sonifying I2S Transport Signals to Detect Transmission Faults
papers.summary: This paper outlines a sonification design to support fault detection in the transmission of I2S transport signals. I2S is a protocol for communicating real-time digital audio between integrated circuits that, while in wide and general use, does not include built-in error detection. Moreover, given the nature of the protocol transmission faults affecting timing, framing and alignment can be difficult to identify using conventional visual methods. The proposed design addresses this with an approach informed by Audification, wherein oversampling controls temporal rescaling to render protocol structure (SCK and WS) and payload data (SD) across separate stereo channels. A preliminary computational feasibility study was carried out to measure feature-space separability of I2S faults in the generated auditory representations as opposed to listener performance. It evaluates the design across several payload types and error conditions including jitter, bit-slip, and word-length errors. Class separability was assessed through clustering analyses of extracted features. The evaluation results show that while oversampling produces systematic changes in feature values, it does not meaningfully improve separability between error classes. However, a modest but consistent improvement in separability is observed as a function of the joint representation of structural and payload information across channels. The findings suggest that feature-space separability in sonified communication protocol data may be dependent on the integration of complementary information streams, rather than on signal scaling alone.

papers.title: Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
papers.summary: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter with oracle cutoff at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.

papers.title: Stochastic MPC under Heavy-Tailed Disturbances: An Extreme Value Theory Approach
papers.summary: Safety-critical control systems must contend with disturbances whose extreme deviations occur far more frequently than classical light-tailed models predict. Existing stochastic MPC (SMPC) formulations tighten constraints using an assumed distribution, a moment bound, or a finite scenario sample, each of which degrades under an unknown heavy-tailed disturbance. This paper develops an SMPC formulation for linear systems under heavy-tailed disturbances that is only assumed to be regularly varying, which allows an explicit extreme value theory (EVT) characterization of the tube error tail that is asymptotically exact. We further show that closed-loop dynamics induce temporal clustering of rare excursions across the prediction horizon, and characterize this clustering through a closed-form extremal index estimable from data. The resulting clustering-corrected constraint bounds the probability of a rare-event episode over the horizon, rather than only the marginal per-step exceedance probability. Simulations of a linear two-CSTR-in-series process and of a nonlinear unicycle navigating past an obstacle under Student-$t$ disturbances validate both approaches and demonstrate reduced frequencies of safety constraint violations.

papers.title: Deep Behaviour Cloning of Model Predictive Control for Real-Time Operation of a Hydrogen-Diesel Dual-Fuel Engine
papers.summary: Hydrogen-diesel dual-fuel (H2DF) combustion engines offer a promising pathway for decarbonising hard-to-electrify transport sectors, yet their highly nonlinear dynamics and coupled process variables demand constraint-aware control strategies. Model Predictive Control (MPC) meets these requirements but requires an online optimisation in every combustion cycle, which limits deployment on low-cost embedded hardware. This paper trains a feedforward deep neural network (DNN) by behaviour cloning (BC) to imitate an MPC expert, using 86,000 engine cycles of demonstration data collected at 1500 min-1 on a modified Cummins QSB 4.5-litre hydrogen dual-fuel engine. Two variants, one with process feedback and one without, are validated experimentally. Both track unseen fast-transient load steps (3-8 bar indicated mean effective pressure, IMEP) with normalised root mean square error (NRMSE) values of 7.80% and 9.03% against the expert's 8.01%, while keeping mean NOx and particulate matter emissions at or below those of the expert. Inference takes 2 ms or less on a Raspberry Pi 400 (ARM Cortex-A72 at 2.2 GHz), including 1 ms communication latency, compared to up to 7 ms for the MPC expert, a 3.5x speedup. Open-loop profiling on a low-cost ESP32 microcontroller at 180 MHz gives 4.3 ms per inference, 4x faster than required for the 18 ms cycle window. Beyond the training range the cloned policy saturates its controls but exceeds the pressure-rise-rate limit. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first experimental BC controller for cycle-to-cycle combustion control of an internal combustion engine (ICE), trained from demonstrations recorded on the engine itself.

papers.title: Sequential RF Fingerprinting for AIS: Rejecting Unknown Vessels and Insider MMSI Spoofs Days After Enrollment
papers.summary: Any AIS transmitter can claim any vessel's identity (MMSI), because nothing in the protocol authenticates it; only the transmitter's analog hardware reveals who is really sending. We treat AIS traffic as streams of bursts keyed by claimed MMSI and accumulate physical-layer evidence with a sequential test. Each burst is scored by its k-nearest-neighbor distance to enrolled fingerprints in the feature space of a classifier whose weights are fixed after training, calibrated into a tail probability, and accumulated by a geometric-entropy-minimization cumulative-sum (GEM-CUSUM) statistic. The same test rejects unknown transmitters when scored against all enrolled vessels, and exposes insider spoofs when scored against the claimed vessel. A threshold refreshed from genuine traffic alone keeps it at a stated false-alarm rate as fingerprints drift. On AIS in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) recordings captured over 13 days at the Istanbul Strait (Bosphorus), the detector rejects unseen vessels at least 10 days after enrollment. Evaluated over 50-burst trials with every vessel weighted equally, it reaches an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.956 (95% confidence interval 0.913-0.989), where the best score computed from one burst at a time reaches 0.899. A threshold refreshed from the first quarter of the enrolled vessels' traffic holds 5.3% false alarms (3.0-9.2% across five independently trained encoders) at 88.8% detection. Scored against the claimed MMSI, enrolled transmitters spoofing another vessel are rejected at 0.991, a threat that open-set tests cannot see (AUROC 0.500, chance level). The lightweight Transformer GLFormer, reimplemented from its paper (no code is public) and retrained on the same data, reaches 0.652 in the same detector with its published in-phase input and 0.849 when given the same I/Q input as our encoder.

papers.title: On the Performance of RIS-Empowered Transmitters with Receive Combining Techniques
papers.summary: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered transmitters offer a promising basis for hardware-efficient multi-antenna architectures in next-generation wireless networks. In particular, combining these transmitters with low-complexity reception techniques such as receive antenna selection (RAS) can further simplify the receiver architecture. In this paper, we investigate the impact of practical phase-shift constraint on RIS-empowered multi-antenna systems employing maximal ratio combining (MRC) and RAS. Since each RIS element can apply only a single phase-shift at a given time, the system performance degrades substantially when multiple receive antennas are active simultaneously. To quantify this effect, closed-form outage probability expressions are derived and asymptotic analyses are carried out over Rician fading channels. We show that the practical phase-shift constraint of RIS-based transmitters can degrade the diversity order of MRC and in addition, RAS outperforms MRC in the examined system models, contrary to the conventional performance ordering of these techniques.

papers.title: A model predictive control framework with robust stability guarantees under unbounded disturbances
papers.summary: To address feasibility issues in model predictive control (MPC), most implementations relax state constraints by using slack variables and adding a penalty to the cost. We propose an alternative strategy: relaxing the initial state constraint with a penalty. Compared to state-of-the-art soft constrained MPC formulations, the proposed formulation has two key features: (i) input-to-state stability and bounds on the cumulative constraint violation for unbounded disturbances; (ii) close-to-optimal performance under nominal operating conditions. The idea is initially presented for open-loop asymptotically stable nonlinear systems by designing the penalty as a Lyapunov function, but we also show how to relax this condition to: i) Lyapunov stable systems; ii) stabilizable systems; and iii) utilizing an implicit characterization of the Lyapunov function. In the special case of linear systems, the proposed MPC formulation reduces to a quadratic program, and the offline design and online computational complexity are only marginally increased compared to a nominal design. Numerical examples demonstrate benefits compared to state-of-the-art soft-constrained MPC formulations.

papers.title: Perturbed Gradient Descent Algorithms are Small-Disturbance Input-to-State Stable
papers.summary: This article investigates the robustness of gradient descent algorithms under perturbations. The concept of small-disturbance input-to-state stability (ISS) for discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems is introduced, along with its Lyapunov characterization. The conventional linear Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition is then extended to a nonlinear version, and it is shown that the gradient descent algorithm is small-disturbance ISS provided the objective function satisfies the generalized nonlinear PL condition. This small-disturbance ISS property guarantees that the gradient descent algorithm converges to a small neighborhood of the optimum under sufficiently small perturbations. As a direct application of the developed framework, we demonstrate that the LQR cost satisfies the generalized nonlinear PL condition, thereby establishing that the policy gradient algorithm for LQR is small-disturbance ISS. Additionally, other popular policy gradient algorithms, including natural policy gradient and Gauss-Newton method, are also proven to be small-disturbance ISS.

papers.title: Gradient-Free Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability for Scalable Safety-Critical Control
papers.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides a principled framework for synthesizing safety certificates and robust controllers for safety-critical robotic systems. However, applying reachability analysis to high-dimensional nonlinear systems remains challenging: classical grid-based solvers suffer from the curse of dimensionality, continuous-time neural solvers require accurate spatial value gradients, and reinforcement-learning-based approaches often suffer from weak boundary anchoring and non-stationary adversarial policy optimization. We propose a discrete-time neural reachability framework for control-disturbance-affine systems that learns backward reachable tubes (BRTs) and backward reach-avoid tubes (BRATs) through Bellman-Isaacs value propagation. Our key idea is to combine equation-driven self-supervision with structured policy learning: rather than computing explicit PDE-gradients, we exploit the bang-bang structure of optimal safety interventions to construct approximate teacher actions from gradient-free value probes, converting adversarial actor learning into supervised policy learning. To stabilize long-horizon value propagation, we leverage the learned actor to train the value function backward from the terminal boundary using a windowed temporal curriculum, where each window is used as the boundary condition for the next window. Across benchmark problems up to 80 dimensions, our method learns accurate reachability value functions while improving stability over existing learning-based solvers. We further demonstrate observation-space scalability on F1-tenth racing with over 16,000-dimensional egocentric inputs. The learned safety filter generalizes zero-shot to unseen tracks and transfers to a physical RC car, achieving real-time robust collision avoidance.

papers.title: It Takes Two Moments: Rigidity and Limits of Continuous Encoders for Over-the-Air Computation
papers.summary: We study over-the-air computation of functions, such as empirical variance, formed by combining two separately postprocessed sums of locally transformed observations. We consider continuous encoders subject to pointwise peak-power constraints over a single use of a complex multiple-access channel. With four or more transmitters, we identify conditions under which exact noiseless recovery forces every continuous encoder collection into a common affine structure that preserves both sums, reducing infinite-dimensional encoder design to selecting a finite set of coefficients. To quantify resilience against channel noise, we introduce a robustness score that measures the separation of noiseless received aggregates relative to variations in the desired function value. Within this characterized encoder family, we formulate robustness maximization as an exact convex semi-infinite program, eliminating rank constraints without a relaxation gap, and construct a decoder that attains the minimum uniform noise-amplification constant. For several function classes, including empirical variance, we derive closed-form robustness-optimal encoders and scores. Under mild regularity conditions, we also establish sharp limits on the Gaussian mean squared error at high signal-to-noise ratios and show how using the input distribution reduces average error at the expense of uniform robustness.

papers.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
papers.summary: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated posterior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covariance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph reoptimization. Surrounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% horizontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consistency checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% relative to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity decisions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.

papers.title: Correspondence Is Not Transfer: A Pairing-Controlled Study of Clinical Audio-Metadata Alignment
papers.summary: Clinical audio models are often trained by aligning recordings with participant metadata or text derived from it. This metadata is rarely a clean disease signal, since a single profile also contains symptoms, age, sex, missing responses, and recruitment information. We examine what alignment adds to frozen audio features by varying only the audio-meta data pairing. We keep the audio backbones fixed and train only a projector under correct pairing and three shuffled conditions that progressively preserve the disease label and recorded sex. We then evaluate each projector on profile retrieval, attribute probing, and disease classification on covariate-matched test sets. On UKCOVID, correct pairing clearly improves retrieval and makes sex easier to decode, confirming that the pairing manipulation works. Most of the sex-probe gap disappears when the control also preserves recorded sex, while a small retrieval gap remains. Matched disease AUROC differences are small, and every interval includes zero, so modest benefits or harms are not ruled out. The same pattern appears when we rerun the frozen pipeline on CODA TB, Cambridge COVID-19 Sounds, and Coswara, where retrieval and sex-probe contrasts are consistently positive but disease contrasts are not. We find no consistent evidence that better profile correspondence translates into better disease prediction and suggest reporting these outcomes separately.

authors.name: Liu He, Xi Wang, Jiahong Yuan, Yuanchao Li
